"Caw caw, as you can see, this room has doors of different colors—only one leads to the next room."
"Caw caw, the other doors...as you already know, lead to the 'endless' void—falling in means certain death!"
"Caw, all of you must still agree on one answer and choose the same door before I'll lead you through!"
"So now...make your 'decision' and tell me which colored door you want to choose!"As Crow-Man spoke, Lin Yu instantly understood.
Unforgotten spoke simultaneously: "This is the Monty Hall paradox...also called the Three Doors Problem!"
Hearing Unforgotten's quiet words, Lin Yu looked at her in surprise.
"You actually know this?"
Unforgotten looked at Lin Yu with slight displeasure: "It's not some advanced or cutting-edge theory...isn't it normal that I know it?"
"Though stealing your bike was wrong, you shouldn't question my knowledge!"
Lin Yu was momentarily speechless.
He had indeed subconsciously underestimated Unforgotten's education—after all, the girl's profession was 'Thief'.
Since everyone's awakened profession was usually related to their life, and Lin Yu had also encountered a 'Thief' in the first dungeon.
So Lin Yu had almost instinctively assumed this girl was a professional thief like Yao Zhengye!
And a teenage professional thief probably never attended school.
Knowing elementary math was one thing...
But the "Three Doors Problem" was probability theory content—though basic—
Its popularity wasn't that widespread.
Lin Yu looked at April, Number Eight, and Iron Uncle.
The two college students and the white-helmeted construction supervisor clearly hadn't heard of this theory.
They all looked blankly at Lin Yu and Unforgotten.
"What's the 'Three Doors Problem'?"
Unforgotten glared at Lin Yu: "Then Nine Waters, you explain it!"
With the water level rising, Lin Yu wasn't in the mood to argue with Unforgotten, so he briefly explained the problem.
"This problem originated from a TV game show, exactly matching our situation."
"Simply put, a person must choose one of three doors. Only one has a prize—the correct door—while the other two are wrong."
"After choosing, the host opens another wrong door, then asks if they want to switch—the debate is whether switching increases the probability of choosing correctly."
Due to time pressure, Lin Yu didn't let them think freely.
"I'll give the conclusion directly—the answer is yes. Not switching gives a one-third chance, but switching raises it to two-thirds!"
This counterintuitive conclusion immediately drew skepticism from Iron Uncle, April, and Number Eight.
"You mean we first choose a door, then after Crow-Man opens one, we immediately switch?"
Iron Uncle asked incredulously.
"Right," Unforgotten said urgently, "This is a probability theory problem, mathematically proven long ago. We can explain why in the next safe room!"
"For now...just do it this way!"
With the water now completely above Unforgotten's head, she kept treading water, her tone anxious.
"Fine, I'll trust you this once," Iron Uncle gritted his teeth, "We randomly pick one now, right? Let's choose red!"
"Okay, red it is!"
April and Number Eight quickly agreed.
After all five chose red, Crow-Man laughed.
"Caw caw, first choice is red...good, now I'll give the 'hint'!"
Then Crow-Man flapped its wings, opening the yellow door opposite the red one.
"Splash—"
Beyond the yellow door was pitch-black void, water gushing out violently, pushing everyone toward it.
Though relieved the water level was dropping, they soon realized...
The current's speed was dangerous too!
"This reward sucks!"
Number Eight cursed, grabbing April to prevent her being swept away.
Iron Uncle paddled against the current, squatting to stabilize himself.
Unforgotten, already unable to touch bottom, completely lost balance.
"Help!"
She flailed desperately, nearly swept out.
When she was less than half a meter from the yellow door...
Lin Yu, steady as a rock in the current, sighed and used his 'Soldier' fivefold physical ability to stride over, grabbing Unforgotten's windbreaker collar to drag her back to the center.
Still shaken, Unforgotten looked at Lin Yu: "Thanks...thanks, Nine Waters."
"You're truly magnanimous—even though you kept threatening me with your gun earlier, in the end you still saved my sorry ass..."
She panted heavily.
Lin Yu flicked her forehead: "I just think your crimes don't deserve death!"
Though stealing his bike was despicable, Lin Yu didn't think she deserved to die.
After joining the 'Death Game', Lin Yu's mindset had changed: when necessary, he could absolutely kill.
But that didn't mean he'd become a cold psychopath who'd ignore people in danger or kill indiscriminately.
While he and Unforgotten had conflicts, it wasn't to the point of killing her.
Moreover...
Lin Yu was beginning to suspect that despite being a 'Thief', Unforgotten might be the most useful teammate in this "Deadly Quiz" game!ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
After all, she seemed quite intelligent.
As the yellow door stayed open and drainage outpaced inflow, the water level soon receded below everyone's waist.
The current weakened too; Lin Yu released Unforgotten's collar, but the girl still clung to his arm, visibly shaken.
"The water won't sweep you away now!"
Lin Yu said helplessly.
"No way! That couple over there is still holding on!"
Unforgotten pointed at Number Eight still embracing April.
Lin Yu sighed: "They're a couple...we just met."
"I could pair up with you too," Unforgotten shamelessly said, "Nine Waters bro, I like you!"
"Cut the crap."
Lin Yu said resignedly, but didn't force her to let go.
Their exchange reached the other three.
April nudged Number Eight, who awkwardly released her.
"The current's fine now."
Iron Uncle, squatting alone, suddenly mused.
"Youth is wonderful...but though the water's receding, we should switch doors fast!"
"Now the only remaining door is the blue one, right?"

chapters.title: Chapter 51: The Choice! The Second Room!
chapters.content:
As the water level in the room gradually receded, the pressure of potentially drowning at any moment disappeared, and the group's tension visibly lessened.
Lin Yu finally had a moment to think calmly.
Suddenly, a realization struck him.
"Wait... let's not rush into making a choice yet."
Lin Yu interrupted everyone who was about to choose the "blue door," speaking in a serious tone.
Iron Uncle looked at Lin Yu with confusion: "Is there a problem, Nine Waters... is there something wrong with this 'Three Doors Problem'?"
"It can't be wrong - this is something already conclusively proven in mathematics."
Unforgotten said firmly.
Lin Yu shook his head: "No, this isn't about the conclusion of the 'Three Doors Problem' itself... I'm just thinking that even following that logic, the final result isn't 'one hundred percent'... right?"
April recalled Lin Yu's earlier words: "I remember you said if we change our choice, the probability of picking the 'correct door' becomes two-thirds... meaning we still have a one-third chance... of dying."Lin Yu nodded: "Exactly, that's what I'm considering - no matter how you look at it, a one-third probability is still too high."
Hearing this, Iron Uncle sighed: "The Death Game always involves an element of luck. In one of the eight dungeons I've experienced, all players even had to play Russian roulette... after all, this is the 'Death' Game."
Unforgotten also nodded in agreement: "That's right... honestly, having a two-thirds survival probability is already pretty good."
Despite their words, Lin Yu remained unconvinced.
"But this doesn't seem consistent with the style of this 'Deadly Quiz' game."
"The first two questions were 'reward-punishment questions,' while this one is a 'choice question,'" Unforgotten waved her hand, "Isn't it normal for there to be differences?"
Number Eight put on a heroic expression: "Yeah, I think we should make a decision soon - sometimes, to win the game, you need some courage."
"When you become brave, the Goddess of Luck will stand by your side!"
Lin Yu looked at Number Eight in surprise.
This 'Student' had been timid throughout the game, seeming even more cowardly than Chen Zhuo.The most update n0vels are published on Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
Yet now he was saying such words.
However, Number Eight's sudden bravery lasted less than a second before being interrupted by his girlfriend April.
April poked him.
"Don't rush the decision... I think you just don't want to get splashed by water anymore."
April said sternly.
Number Eight sheepishly rubbed his nose: "Ah, you caught me."
April sighed: "So... when it comes to life-and-death matters, don't interfere with others' thinking!"
Although most of the water had already drained through the doors, the ten drainage holes and trapdoor on the ceiling were still releasing water.
The flowing water kept intermittently wetting everyone's calves and shoes, leaving the room damp.
Splashing water also occasionally soaked their upper bodies and hair, making everyone quite uncomfortable.
But hearing April's words...
Lin Yu suddenly realized something.
"I understand now... this isn't the 'Three Doors Problem' at all."
He spoke with sudden enlightenment, then looked at Crow-Man.
"Because actually, the number of doors we can choose from was four before you opened the yellow door, and now it's still three, right?"
As Lin Yu spoke, Crow-Man laughed.
"Caw caw, yes, it's still a choice among three."
Crow-Man's words shocked Iron Uncle.
"What do you mean? Was the 'reward' from the first round fake? Can we still choose that disappeared green door?"
"No, the 'rewards' are all real," Lin Yu said calmly, "And... both reward hints were true."
He pointed at the black trapdoor on the ceiling that was still releasing water.
"From the beginning, this guy said we needed to choose from 'doors'... but it never specified they had to be one of these four doors."
"And if we hadn't answered the first question correctly, this trapdoor probably wouldn't have opened... we'd have never known there was a trapdoor above us."
"This 'choice question' is just like the first two 'reward-punishment questions' - it contains a trap... one that combines elements from the previous two questions!"
Lin Yu smiled as he spoke: "And it just said... if we choose a door, it will 'take us' through the door."
"Why use such strange wording... its habit of hiding traps in the questions proves in a way that... every word it says might be carefully designed."
"So, this is also a hidden 'hint.'"
Lin Yu looked at Crow-Man and said: "In this game, we don't need 'probability'... trying to use the Three Doors Problem from probability theory is itself a 'mathematical' solution."
"But this game... at least all the questions in this room, use 'mathematics' to conceal 'traps.'"
Hearing this, Crow-Man asked: "But... isn't that still not enough? What if this black door is also a 'trap'?"
Lin Yu shook his head.
"Then that's where 'luck' comes in... but since water is flowing from this black trapdoor, I don't think it leads to 'the void.'"
After speaking, Lin Yu grinned.
"Moreover... the 'designer' of this game dungeon probably wouldn't make it so boring by setting meaningless traps, right?"
Crow-Man looked at Lin Yu, its eyes glimmering.
"Caw caw, indeed, I quite admire you."
"State your choice - which colored door do you want to select?"
Lin Yu pointed upward and declared: "I choose the black door on the ceiling."
As Lin Yu spoke, Crow-Man looked at the others.
"Caw caw, are your choices the same as his?"
Seeing that Lin Yu's choice of the "black door" had succeeded...
The others couldn't possibly choose differently now.
"I also choose the black door."
Iron Uncle quickly said.
April and Number Eight then spoke in unison: "We choose the black door!"
Unforgotten looked at Lin Yu with admiration, giving him a thumbs up.
"You're truly amazing, Brother Nine Waters... thanks to you, we've solved all three questions in this room!"
Then she turned to Crow-Man and grinned.
"Then I also choose the black door."
Hearing their choices, Crow-Man nodded.
"Good, the 'choice' has been made—"
As Crow-Man spoke, it fully spread its wings.
The black wings were more expansive than anyone had imagined.
It wrapped everyone in its wings, then flew toward the black trapdoor.
Just as it was about to hit the trapdoor...
The black trapdoor suddenly enlarged, with the entire ceiling splitting open!
Then...
They arrived in the second room!

chapters.title: Chapter 52: Coo!
chapters.content:
After flying upward for about five minutes, the Crow-Man gradually came to a stop.
Lin Yu felt himself being gently set down.
The ground beneath his feet seemed to be made of wooden planks, creaking slightly with each step.
Though Lin Yu wasn't entirely certain.
His uncertainty stemmed from the fact that compared to the first pure white, softly lit room, this one was pitch black.
Lin Yu looked down and could barely make out the dark floor.
Only two black candles on candlesticks ahead provided faint illumination, barely lighting up the surrounding space.
On either side of Lin Yu, the other four players were also adjusting to the darkness.
Soon, Iron Uncle, who adapted fastest, spoke up.
"Wait... where's the Crow-Man?"Only then did everyone notice that the Examiner Crow-Man had disappeared.
Originally covered entirely in black feathers, it had completely vanished into this utterly dark room.
Number Eight panicked: "Ah, what do we do... the Examiner's gone? Does this mean we have to figure this level out ourselves?"
Just then, the Crow-Man's distinctive raspy, layered voice echoed through the room.
"Caw caw, welcome everyone to the second room. This room still contains two 'reward-punishment questions' and one 'decision question'."
The Crow-Man's voice reverberated in the chamber.
"Caw caw, in this room, 'questioning me' will be replaced by questioning specific creatures, and there will be a limit to the number of questions you can ask. So... good luck."
As the Crow-Man's voice faded, the sound of flapping wings came from above.
Then two black crows landed on the left and right candlesticks.
With their arrival, the candles seemed to burn slightly brighter, illuminating the area around the candlesticks.
Between and beside the two candlesticks stood three swaying rope bridges.
The Crow-Man's voice sounded again.
"Caw caw, among these three bridges, only one will safely take you to the opposite side... the other two will suddenly collapse when you reach the middle, sending you falling into the endless void."
"Caw caw, before you stand two great deities manifested as crow avatars - one represents 'truth' and the other represents 'falsehood'."
"Caw caw, 'truth' will only speak truthfully, 'falsehood' will only lie. And they will only answer 'yes or no' questions."
"You have two opportunities to question them to determine your final planned route."
After speaking, the Crow-Man fell silent.
This time, Number Eight grew excited after listening: "I've heard of puzzles like this! You just need to ask one crow what the other would say if you asked whether a bridge is safe, and that gives you the answer!"
"If we ask the 'truth' crow and the bridge happens to be safe, it would naturally answer 'no'—because that's what the lying crow would say; similarly, if the bridge isn't safe, it would answer 'yes'!"
"But likewise—if we ask the 'falsehood' crow, if the bridge is safe, the truthful answer would be 'yes', so it would lie and say 'no'; and if the bridge isn't safe, it would say 'yes'!"
"So it doesn't matter which one we ask, the result is the same!"
April looked at him in astonishment: "You actually figured that out."
Number Eight said somewhat sheepishly: "Just read it in a magazine before... since there are three bridges, two questions should be perfect."
Iron Uncle also nodded: "With good luck, we might confirm it with just one question!"
Lin Yu narrowed his eyes but remained silent.
No, this problem... isn't that simple.
But he didn't speak up.
Because Lin Yu had already realized something—what was different between the second room and the first room.
Meanwhile, Unforgotten also stayed quiet in the group.
Number Eight eagerly walked up to the crow on the left and asked:
"Crow, if I asked the other crow whether the leftmost bridge is safe, would the other crow answer 'yes' or 'no'?"
But the left crow didn't respond.
Number Eight looked puzzled.
"Huh? Why isn't it answering?"
April and Iron Uncle exchanged confused glances.
"Did the Crow-Man lie to us?"
"Or is it malfunctioning?"
Unable to watch any longer, Lin Yu sighed and reminded them: "Because that's not a 'yes or no' question... you need to phrase it properly."
"If I asked the other crow whether the leftmost bridge is safe, would it give an affirmative answer?"
Lin Yu said quietly.
Number Eight had an epiphany.
"Oh right, haha," Number Eight scratched his head, somewhat embarrassed, "Cough, my bad, sorry."
At the same time, he felt frustrated.
In the previous room, it had been practically Lin Yu's show.
Coming to the second room, he'd finally encountered a puzzle whose solution he knew, wanting to impress everyone—especially his girlfriend April—only to mess up the phrasing.
But fortunately, it wasn't a big deal!
Number Eight raised his head again, looked at the leftmost crow, cleared his throat, and repeated the question using Lin Yu's "proper phrasing":
"If I asked the other crow whether the leftmost bridge is safe, would it give an affirmative answer?"
This time, the left crow finally responded.
Its answer was...Thɪs updatᴇd by ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
"Coo."
That single syllable instantly shattered Number Eight's composure.
"'Coo'... what the hell is that?!"
He yelled in frustration.
Nearby, Iron Uncle and April exchanged glances again.
"Is 'coo' its answer?"
April asked incredulously.
From the darkness, Unforgotten, who had remained silent until now, burst into laughter.
"Ahahahaha, after all, the Crow-Man never said these things would answer 'yes' or 'no'... they're just crows after all!"
Unforgotten slapped her thigh as she laughed.
Number Eight grew anxious: "Then what do you suggest we do!"
Unforgotten waved her hand in the dark: "I don't know... but I think, with one question left, we should leave it to Nine Waters."
"Brother Nine Waters probably knew from the start that these crows wouldn't speak 'human language'."
Hearing this, Lin Yu looked at Unforgotten in surprise.
Although he had indeed guessed it early on, Lin Yu was curious.
"How did you know I'd figured it out?"
"Because when you corrected Number Eight's phrasing earlier, you ultimately said 'would it give an affirmative answer'... plus Brother Nine Waters, you're very smart, so I concluded that if even I vaguely guessed it, you couldn't have missed it."
Unforgotten said cheerfully with a smile.
"And I believe you've already thought of a way to 'solve this', right, Brother Nine Waters?"
"Otherwise, you wouldn't have let Number Eight ask that question just now!"

chapters.title: Chapter 53: The Cruel "Solution"
chapters.content:
Hearing Unforgotten's words, Lin Yu shook his head slightly.
"It's not exactly solving the puzzle, but there is indeed a way to clear this stage."
Lin Yu looked at Number Eight.
"Don't let its words throw you off. Although we only have two questions left, remember there are 'three bridges' here. Given that only one bridge is safe, regardless of what 'caw' means to the crow..."
"As long as you ask the same crow, its three answers must contain two identical responses and one different one."
"In other words, we can just randomly pick another bridge to ask about and see what answer we get."
"If both answers match—then naturally, the remaining bridge must be the safe one."
Number Eight stared at Lin Yu in astonishment. "You can actually do that?!"
Lin Yu nodded slightly.
"Of course."But April sensed something amiss.
"What if its answer differs from the previous one?"
Lin Yu smiled. "Then I have another solution. Let's just ask first."
He turned to the crow on the left.
"If I asked the other crow whether the far-right bridge is safe, would it give a positive answer?"
The left crow raised its head and responded with another inhuman syllable.
"Caw!"
Hearing this, Lin Yu narrowed his eyes.
"What a shame—it's different."
Iron Uncle realized something. "If they're different, then one of these two bridges must be correct!"
As Iron Uncle spoke, Lin Yu nodded.Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
"Exactly. A fifty-fifty chance now."
Number Eight blinked. "Fifty percent? That's worse than the previous two-thirds probability!"
April also nodded. "Does that mean this question also has a 'trap'?"
Lin Yu shook his head.
"No, unfortunately... I think this time there's no trap. We genuinely have to choose between two."
The Crow-Man's riddle this time contained no trick.
"The theme of this room differs from the previous one."
The remaining four exchanged uneasy glances.
Number Eight asked nervously, "So... are we really down to luck now?"
"Not quite. You're still overlooking the fundamental difference between the second room and the first... That's the Crow-Man's little trick, but it doesn't qualify as a trap."
As he spoke, Lin Yu drew his pistol from his waist.
"In the first room, all of us had to 'answer directly' to its questions."
"But in this room... what we need is to respond through 'action.'"
"Therefore, we no longer need unified answers or simultaneous responses."
At this point, Iron Uncle understood, his voice low.
"I see... So this stage isn't so much about a 'trap' as it is about selecting someone to 'sacrifice,' right?"
Lin Yu smiled.
"Exactly. Although we'll indeed be relying on luck next, only one person needs to take that gamble!"
"Just one person needs to cross one bridge, and we'll know—"
Under the faint candlelight, April and Number Eight's expressions shifted.
"Then... who will be the one to gamble?" April asked.
Iron Uncle spoke up. "For fairness, we should draw lots—"
Lin Yu cut him off.
"Lots my ass. I took out this gun to remind you of one thing," Lin Yu said coldly. "I decide who the unlucky one is."
With that, he aimed the gun at Unforgotten, the Thief who had been lurking in the shadows without a word.
"Well then, dear Thief, time to make yourself useful."
Lin Yu flashed a charming smile.
Faced with Lin Yu's sudden aggression, Unforgotten sighed and stepped forward, raising her hands.
"Why me?"
Lin Yu shrugged. "Someone's gotta do it. I can't, so I have to pick from the remaining four."
"Among them, you've cleared the fewest dungeons, while Craftsman here has the most. The other two are a package deal. Though I'm confident no one here can beat me in a fight—me, a gun-wielding Soldier—but still..."
"Just in case, I'll start with the easiest target."
"Besides, you did piss me off before, remember?"
Unforgotten kept her hands up, her expression torn between resignation and resentment.
She glanced at the others. "Hey, you're just gonna let him do this? What if you're next?!"
Lin Yu chuckled. "Don't be so gloomy, Unforgotten. You've got a fifty-fifty chance of surviving! For fairness—pick a bridge yourself. That way, your fate's in your own hands!"
Unforgotten gritted her teeth. "Fine... the left one. Damn it, if I die, I'll haunt you forever!"
Lin Yu remained unfazed, keeping his gun trained on her while addressing the others.
"Speaking of which, does anyone have 'rope' or similar items?"
Iron Uncle hesitated, then quickly said, "I do. Safety rope, specifically."
He produced a long coil of safety rope.
Lin Yu glanced at April. "Tie it around her."
April looked startled but took the rope from Iron Uncle and secured it around Unforgotten.
Lin Yu then said, "Now toss me the other end."
April threw it to him. Lin Yu caught it midair, wrapped it twice around his hand, and gripped it firmly—there was nothing sturdy here to tie it to.
Seeing this, Unforgotten's tense expression softened slightly, though she still glared.
"You bastard."
But Lin Yu kept his gun raised, his voice icy.
"Go."
Unforgotten flipped him off before turning and stepping onto the swaying rope bridge, disappearing into the darkness.
Watching her vanish, Iron Uncle murmured to Lin Yu,
"That was harsh, but someone had to play the villain."
"You picked her because she's the lightest, right? And made sure she was tied..."
"You're taking a big risk yourself here."
April and Number Eight also looked at Lin Yu differently now—mostly with gratitude. Though his earlier coercion had shaken them, seeing him hold the rope himself led them to the same conclusion as Iron Uncle.
Lin Yu had simply been seeking the "optimal solution."
But Lin Yu shook his head.
"Don't overestimate me."
Securing Unforgotten with the rope might have stemmed partly from a "no unnecessary deaths" mindset, but his main reasons were more pragmatic.
Lin Yu said quietly, "Without the rope, what if Unforgotten picked the right bridge but stayed silent out of spite? Or faked a scream to mislead us?"
"After all, we don't know if the bridge 'collapses' entirely or if we'd even notice from here."
"Even if she meant no harm, what if the other side has soundproofing?"
His explanation didn't fully convince the other three.
To Iron Uncle, April, and Number Eight, it would be far more reassuring if Lin Yu—the strongest fighter in this dungeon—had some "humanity" and "compassion."
But Lin Yu offered no further justification. He simply watched the rope stretching into the darkness.
Even now, he hadn't revealed all his reasons for choosing Unforgotten.
"What an interesting Thief."
Soon, a light tug came from the rope.
From the darkness, Unforgotten's voice called out:
"This bridge is safe—it's this one!"

chapters.title: Chapter 54: The Second Question, The God of Change!
chapters.content:
After Unforgotten's shout, Lin Yu gently tugged the rope to confirm she was standing on stable ground before stepping onto the leftmost bridge.
The other three players followed closely behind.
Although the rope bridge swayed slightly, it posed no real challenge for the group.
Soon, they safely reached the opposite side—still pitch black, but with slightly improved visibility.
This time, there were three candlesticks, each significantly larger than before.
Unforgotten stood helplessly on the other side, though she didn't seem particularly resentful.
"If this stage still requires someone to 'scout the path' in the end, don't pick me!"
She pointed toward the gloomy darkness ahead.
Following the candlelight, everyone saw that bridges still extended into the darkness.
But this time...There were five bridges!
Then, three crows flapped their wings and landed on the candlesticks.
Crow-Man's voice echoed through the darkness again.
"Caw caw, congratulations on passing the first 'reward-punishment question'... Since no one died, you have five questioning opportunities this round."
Lin Yu nodded slightly.
Crow-Man's "explanation" matched Lin Yu's expectations.
This was the difference between the first and second rooms!
In the first room, everyone acted as a "collective," requiring unanimous choices.
But in the second room, each person could choose their own path...
In other words, the "reward-punishment questions" here allowed divergence—different answers could be chosen.
Those who answered correctly would live; those who answered wrong would die.
But whenever someone answered wrong, it would bring both "rewards" and "punishments" to the survivors.
The fact that the number of allowed answers matched the number of players confirmed this.
"Indeed, we should try to minimize deaths as much as possible."
Lin Yu thought to himself, then continued listening to Crow-Man's speech.
"Caw caw, among these five bridges, only one will safely take you to the other side... The other four will collapse midway, sending you tumbling into the endless void."
"Caw caw, before you now stand three divine crow avatars—besides 'Truth' and 'Falsehood,' there's also a crow representing 'Change'—it may speak truth or lies."
After Crow-Man finished explaining the rules, everyone naturally turned to Lin Yu.
"Nine Waters, what should we do this time... We each have one question—how should we proceed?"
Iron Uncle asked.
Number Eight also felt troubled: "There's actually one that might lie or tell the truth... This is way too difficult!"
April remained relatively calm: "But we have five questions."
Lin Yu silently contemplated.
"Five questions..."ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
"That might mean no one needs to risk their life scouting paths."
He already had the answer in mind.
Unforgotten looked at Lin Yu in surprise: "That fast?"
Lin Yu nodded.
"Of course, since we have five chances this time."
He then turned to Iron Uncle.
"You'll ask the middle crow first, Iron Uncle—here's the question:"
"'If I asked you whether the left crow represents Change, would you answer 'coo'?'"
Iron Uncle now trusted Lin Yu implicitly. He stepped forward and repeated the question to the middle crow.
"Hey, if I asked whether the left crow represents Change, would you answer 'coo'?"
The crow looked at Iron Uncle, then let out a "coo."
Lin Yu narrowed his eyes.
"Good, it seems 'coo' and 'caw' might be interchangeable."
From the first reward-punishment question, Lin Yu had confirmed one thing:
"coo" represented affirmation in crow language.
Though he wasn't sure if it was the same crow or if meanings had changed...
As long as they still used "coo," five questions would be more than enough.
Through this first question, Lin Yu confirmed that at least the far-right crow wasn't the one representing "Change."
So he gestured to April and Number Eight.
"Next question—April, ask the far-right crow: 'If I asked whether you represent Falsehood, would you answer 'coo'?'"
Hearing this, April instinctively tried to analyze the reasoning but couldn't immediately grasp it, so she simply followed Lin Yu's instructions.
She approached the far-right crow and repeated the question verbatim. The crow quickly responded:
"Caw."
Lin Yu nodded.
"Good, the rest should be simple."
"Number Eight, ask it: 'Among the three leftmost bridges, is there a safe one?'"
"Repeat this exactly—not a single word different."
Lin Yu spoke gravely. Number Eight scratched his head.
"Nine Waters, why am I the one getting special warnings?"
April immediately said: "Because you look the least reliable!"
Number Eight fell silent.
"Fine..."
He shuffled over to the far-right crow and repeated the question.
This time, the crow again answered "caw."
Lin Yu looked at Unforgotten.
Unforgotten waved her hand: "Enough, I already know what to do."
Without waiting for Lin Yu to speak,
she strode up to the far-right crow and pointed boldly at the far-right bridge.
"Crow, is this bridge safe?"
The crow looked at her and said: "Caw."
Unforgotten concluded:
"Done. This crow represents 'Truth,' and 'caw' means no... So the second bridge from the right must be safe."
"No need for your last question, Nine Waters."
She crossed her arms and looked back at Lin Yu.
Lin Yu studied Unforgotten up and down.
Indeed, this thief had followed his reasoning the entire way!
She'd also realized the far-right crow represented "Truth."
"You're quite clever. But what if the meanings of 'coo' and 'caw' reversed between the first and second questions?"
Lin Yu said coolly.
Unforgotten hesitated.
"I don't think that's likely, right?"
Lin Yu said coldly: "What if it did? This is a life-or-death game!"
Unforgotten shrank back.
"Hey, you still have one question left," she said carefully. "Just use it to confirm whether the meanings changed."
Lin Yu sighed: "And if they have?"
"Then I'll just test one of the two left paths myself!"
Unforgotten said impatiently.
Lin Yu smiled.
"Those are your words."
He turned to the far-right crow and asked:
"Crow, among the third and fourth bridges from the left, is there a safe one?"
The crow flapped its wings.
"Coo."
Unforgotten exhaled deeply.
"Damn, you scared me!"
"So the fourth bridge from the right is definitely safe!"
Lin Yu looked somewhat disappointed.
"Tch, what a pity."
"Pity what? Were you happy forcing me to choose?"
Unforgotten said indignantly.
Lin Yu sneered: "This time, it was your own doing—who told you to jump to conclusions?"
Their back-and-forth left Iron Uncle, April, and Number Eight completely baffled.
The three exchanged glances, all wearing expressions of "We don't get it, let's just go with it."

chapters.title: Chapter 55: Testing the Waters
chapters.content:
Following the fourth rope bridge from the left, the five of them safely reached the opposite side once more.
This time, the lighting arrangement had changed again.
The illuminating candlesticks had taken the form of a massive "stone altar."
Circular candles were arranged around the stone altar—and on either side of it, there were only two rope bridges.
From within the darkness, Crow-Man's voice sounded again.
"Caw caw, congratulations on passing the 'reward-punishment question' with all members intact... Therefore, when the decision-making question begins, there will be a 'hint' present."
"Caw caw, welcome to this room's 'decision-making question'."
As soon as the words fell, a crow flapped its wings and descended from the darkness onto the stone altar.
Then, the crow's form rapidly expanded, transforming into the appearance of "Crow-Man."
Lin Yu stepped forward with his hands in his pockets."Wow, so this is the 'hint' that's present?"
"Caw—"
The Crow-Man on the altar made a sound, then sat among the candles and spoke softly.
"Both bridges this time lead to the next room..."
"Beep—"
"...However, one can carry three people and the other can carry two—everyone must step onto both bridges simultaneously, otherwise both bridges will collapse."
"You only have one chance to ask me a question—I won't answer any questions that reveal which bridge can carry how many people."
As Crow-Man spoke, the five exchanged glances.
Number Eight was the first to speak: "This Crow-Man says it won't answer questions revealing which bridge carries how many people, so shouldn't we think of an indirect way to ask?"
"Like if three of us take the left bridge, can we pass or something like that?"
Before the others could react.
Crow-Man interrupted him first.Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
"Caw caw, I won't answer that kind of question either!"
As it spoke, Lin Yu spoke up again.
"I actually thought of a solution for this game—I plan to ask, 'If two people walk on each bridge and the remaining person is already dead, will the bridges still collapse?'"
As he spoke, Lin Yu pulled out his pistol.
"If the answer is yes, I'll randomly shoot one, so four people can survive."
After Lin Yu finished his proposal, Unforgotten immediately screamed.
"Who'd believe you'd do it randomly! You're absolutely going to shoot me!"
Unforgotten looked at Lin Yu in terror as she spoke.
Lin Yu glanced at Unforgotten: "Oh, you saw through me... Maybe I should shoot first and ask later."
"Honestly, I think if two go on one side... it definitely won't collapse."
As he spoke, Lin Yu pulled the revolver from his left pocket.
"Stop pulling out guns all the time! What if—damn it, don't gamble on that possibility!" Unforgotten said, sweating profusely. "And... and this 'decision-making question' might have a trap."
As Unforgotten spoke, Lin Yu laughed.
"Oh? Where's the trap?"
With the gun pointed at her, Unforgotten's speech noticeably sped up.
"Well, look, didn't Crow-Man say at the beginning that in this room, asking it questions would be replaced by asking specific creatures!"
"So the Crow-Man sitting there might not be the 'Examiner' Crow-Man, right?"
As Unforgotten spoke, Lin Yu nodded.
"That makes sense, but so what?"
He still didn't lower the gun.
"Earlier, it flew over in the form of a 'crow'... Doesn't that mean it's actually some kind of 'avatar'?"
"And among the three known avatars, aside from the one representing 'truth,' the other two crows both lie!"
"If this guy is one of 'change' or 'falsehood,' then we might not need to believe anything it said about the two bridges!"
Unforgotten spoke rapidly, and the other three players, hearing her rapid-fire words, all looked thoughtful.
"That does seem reasonable..."
Iron Uncle murmured.
Lin Yu nodded.
"It's very reasonable, because Unforgotten is right."
Lin Yu's right hand came out of his pocket—holding a lie detector flashing red light.
He had pressed the button when Crow-Man spoke its first sentence.
"This is the 'Lie Detector' I got from the first dungeon. The 'beep' earlier was from it... It means Crow-Man's first sentence was a lie."
"Its first sentence was 'Both bridges lead to the next room,' which was the premise of its entire speech... This means everything it said afterward is wrong."
"So we can completely ignore what this Crow-Man said—it's purely here to mislead us."
Lin Yu spoke calmly. Unforgotten froze for a moment before speaking with a sob in her voice.
"You had something this good and didn't bring it out earlier?! And you knew it was lying, so you were just scaring me for fun?!"
"I wanted to test how smart you really are," Lin Yu said with a smile, putting away the pistol. "What, you can mess with me but I can't mess with you?"
Iron Uncle coughed and spoke.
"Alright, since its words are misleading... does that mean only one of these two bridges leads to the next room?"
Number Eight's eyes lit up.
"In that case, couldn't we just ask it—no need to ask which bridge carries how many people, just ask which bridge leads to the next room!"
Lin Yu shook his head.
"If there were only 'truth' and 'falsehood' avatars, it wouldn't matter even if everything it said was lies... We could just interpret it backwards."
"But since there's a 'change' avatar, that means if it might be the 'change' avatar, asking it anything is pointless."
As Lin Yu explained, Number Eight froze.
"Ah, it can be like that too... Then what do we do?! Another fifty-fifty chance?!"
After speaking, Number Eight also looked at Unforgotten.
Noticing his gaze, Unforgotten angrily pulled out her utility knife.
"What do you mean, huh? What do you mean? You don't have a gun but you still want me to go first? Believe it or not, I'll stab you to death! Student brat! Can't beat Nine Waters but I can beat you?"
Unforgotten screeched in rage.
Number Eight quickly said, "I absolutely didn't mean that, I'll follow whatever Nine Waters big bro decides."
As he spoke, he looked at Lin Yu with an ingratiating smile.
Lin Yu, however, walked silently up to Unforgotten, gently reached out, and took the utility knife from her hand.
Unforgotten watched Lin Yu's actions, confused and angry.
"What do you mean? You're afraid I'll actually stab it? You're not really planning to make me randomly pick one, are you?"
Lin Yu shook his head.
"No, because if 'both lead to the next room' is a lie, then the truth could be 'only one leads to the next room,' but it could also be 'neither leads to the next room.'"
"Combined with the Examiner Crow-Man's voice from the darkness earlier... this 'Crow-Man' in front of us, whose every word is untrustworthy, must also be some kind of 'hint.'"
"So, what is it hinting at?"
"Considering the answer to the last room's 'decision-making question,' I have a guess..."
As he spoke, Lin Yu threw the utility knife behind Crow-Man.
"Hey—my knife!"
Unforgotten screamed.
But before her voice faded, a crisp sound came from the darkness.
"Clatter."
Lin Yu smiled.
"The candles were arranged so convincingly... From our angle, we couldn't see there's a path behind at all..."
"But unfortunately, throwing something reveals it."

chapters.title: Chapter 56: The Third Room! Five Statements!
chapters.content:
Just as the black trapdoor above was the correct choice during the final "Decision" in the first room, the two rope bridges in the second room's final "Decision Question" were both fake—the real path to choose was in the middle!
The circle of candles on the stone altar was meant to mislead players, just like water pouring down from the trapdoor. This ring of candles made everyone think it marked the boundary of the stone altar—but that wasn't the case.
After Lin Yu pointed this out, the crow disguised as the Crow-Man representing "change" dissipated, and the crow flew into the darkness. From behind the stone altar, the real Crow-Man slowly emerged.
"Caw caw, so, what is your final choice?"
"Obviously this path."
Lin Yu calmly looked in the direction the Crow-Man had come from. The Crow-Man chuckled lowly again.
"Congratulations, you've answered the second room's 'Decision Question' correctly."
The Crow-Man spread its wings and flew up, then the room suddenly lit up. Countless previously extinguished candlesticks were revealed on the ceiling and side walls of the second room—much larger than the first, about the size of a soccer field—illuminating everything.
Lin Yu's expression changed slightly as he surveyed the scene. April beside him screamed in fright.
"Ah!"Beneath them was only a narrow plank wide enough for four people to stand side by side—everything else was a bottomless abyss! The rope bridges they'd crossed weren't spacious either... Worse, except for the two "correct" bridges, the others had cuts in their ropes at the midpoint—no doubt they'd snap if stepped on.
Even the last two bridges were like this, especially since they led to a precarious, isolated stone pillar.
Number Eight beside April looked pale but tried comforting his girlfriend. "It's okay, we've made it."
Iron Uncle and Unforgotten remained relatively calm.
"This height reminds me of when I used to climb tower cranes!" Iron Uncle laughed, then looked at the "stone altar" where the Crow-Man stood.
Beneath it was a stone bridge previously hidden in darkness, extending to a black door. Lin Yu's utility knife lay quietly on that bridge.
"Let's go!"
Unforgotten nimbly jumped onto the stone altar, then down onto the bridge, picking up her utility knife before walking ahead briskly. Iron Uncle cautiously followed behind her.Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn NovᴇlFirenᴇt
Though physically capable, Lin Yu hesitated at this height. But eventually, he matched the pace of the two ahead.
April and Number Eight were much more cautious. Just jumping onto the spacious stone altar took them time. Even though the stone bridge was wider and more stable than the rope bridges, they moved much slower—after all, they couldn't see the abyss before!
Still, everyone safely reached the black door... Behind it was a spiraling staircase upward.
After climbing for about five minutes, they encountered another black door. Unforgotten, leading the way, pushed it open—
A gray, misty room appeared before the five. Hazy smoke swirled around, obscuring the ceiling and walls.
The Crow-Man emerged from the fog again.
"Caw, welcome to the final room."
It took out an ancient key from its chest. The thick fog parted to form towering walls of mist, creating a narrow passage between them—like the sea split by divine power in ancient legends.
At the end stood a locked gate.
"Caw, this room has only one 'Decision Question,' no 'reward-punishment question.'"
"Caw caw—answer correctly, and you may choose to leave this dungeon."
"Caw caw—but I warn you, not all may pass the 'Decision.'"
"Caw caw—each of you must identify a 'lie' in my statements and explain how you know it's false, or face punishment. Now, five statements!"
The Crow-Man spread its wings and paced before them.
"One—All of you are honest; no one has tampered with their identity!"
"Two—All of you trust each other; no one has hidden their cleared dungeon count."
"Three—All of you are straightforward and considerate; no one has lied about their profession."
"Four—Between those who know each other, no betrayal has occurred."
"Five—Among you, no one has ever thought, 'I wish they were dead.'"
After the Crow-Man finished, everyone's expressions darkened.
Lin Yu narrowed his eyes. "How amusing... Almost malicious."
These five "statements" seemed tailored for their group!
The rooms' "competitive nature" seemed to escalate.
From cooperating in the first room to solve puzzles and spot traps, to treating "survivor count" as a "resource" in the second... Now this third room felt deliberately provocative.
As Lin Yu pondered, Iron Uncle spoke first.
"Ahem, I think the fifth statement is definitely a 'lie'!"
The Crow-Man turned to him. "State your reason."
Iron Uncle pointed at Lin Yu and Unforgotten. "At the start, this Soldier wanted to kill this Thief! He considered it multiple times!"
The Crow-Man chuckled. "Insufficient reasoning."
It watched Iron Uncle with interest. "Choose one you're certain is a lie."
After a long silence, Iron Uncle smiled wryly.
"Fine. The first is a lie—I lied about my forum ID!"
"My old ID was 'Heavenly Artisan.' Now, I have no forum account."
Lin Yu showed no reaction, but April, Number Eight, and Unforgotten stared at Iron Uncle in shock, as if seeing a monster.
"'Heavenly Artisan' of the Marauders?!" April gasped. "I saw your bounty on the forum's new list this month..."
"You killed five players in reality—Order is hunting you!"

chapters.title: Chapter 57: Invitation, Deception, Betrayal
chapters.content:
Although Lin Yu had never heard the name "Heavenly Artisan" before—since he rarely checked the forum's bounty section—he was familiar with the organization called "Marauders."
It was one of the three organizations banned from the forum, sharing equal notoriety with the "Psychological Society," the insane group that had killed him.
When April exclaimed about Heavenly Artisan's deeds, it became clear that Iron Uncle—no, this "Heavenly Artisan"—was also a formidable figure.
Killing other players in real life was considered a "violation" unanimously agreed upon by all players!
Though there were no courts or police among the players, the largest organization "Order" and its "Game Masters" essentially served as judicial and law enforcement bodies.
Anyone who used in-game abilities to commit crimes in reality would be publicly wanted on the forum once discovered by Order.
Moreover, Order members would unconditionally hunt down those wanted "violators" both in-game and in reality!
After Heavenly Artisan revealed his identity, his expression was no longer as calm as before.
He sighed, looking at the now-alert and wary Unforgotten, April, and Number Eight with a shadowed expression.
"This is exactly why I had to conceal my identity.""Although I joined the Marauders, I don't indiscriminately kill innocents in cooperative puzzle games... If you'd treated me like this from the start, the game would've been difficult to proceed."
After speaking, Heavenly Artisan turned his gaze to Lin Yu.
"I actually admire you, Nine Waters... To be honest, your composure exceeds my expectations."
Lin Yu shrugged nonchalantly.
"No, I just never considered you a good person from the beginning."ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
Although in this game, this self-proclaimed "Iron Uncle"—Heavenly Artisan—had worked hard to play the role of a kindly old man...
But...
A guy who survived ten dungeons being a nice person?
Highly unlikely.
While there were naive lucky survivors in this game—
Like Chen Zhuo.
Or that "Number Eight" over there—probably a genuinely timid mouse.
But "Iron Uncle" was definitely no saint.
Ultimately, his acting just wasn't good enough.
At least, not good enough to fool Lin Yu.
During the second dungeon, his poorly concealed indifference toward human life while pretending otherwise almost made Lin Yu laugh.
However, Lin Yu's calm demeanor instead provoked hearty laughter from Heavenly Artisan.
"Haha, I really like you!"
"With your 'Soldier' profession and that powerful pistol item... You're perfect material for the Marauders!"
Lin Yu shook his head.
"I'll have to decline. I'd like to keep accessing the forum for a while longer."
As he spoke, Heavenly Artisan laughed.
"No problem. Change your mind? Feel free to contact me anytime."
After Heavenly Artisan finished speaking,
The Crow-Man tossed him a key.
"Caw caw, you may now leave the dungeon."
Heavenly Artisan caught the key in surprise.
"Oh? I can leave now?"
The Crow-Man nodded.
"Caw caw, of course!"
Heavenly Artisan smiled.
"Fine then, my presence was making everyone uncomfortable anyway."
With that, he walked toward the door at the end.
He opened it and stepped into a blinding white light.
The door closed and locked again, as a new key materialized in Crow-Man's hand.
Watching him leave, April and Number Eight simultaneously exhaled in relief.
"That scared me to death!"
Number Eight said, still shaken.
Lin Yu glanced at him and shook his head. "What were you afraid of? I'm an armed Soldier. Even if he's wanted, do you think he could kill you all right in front of me?"
Number Eight gave Lin Yu a strange look. "Brother Nine Waters, even with your strong profession and item... That 'Heavenly Artisan' is a 'Promoted' player—one who completed Promotion in just ten dungeons and got invited by the Marauders! In a fight, you probably wouldn't stand much chance!"
Lin Yu could tell Number Eight was being diplomatic.
Promotion again...
What exactly was this "Promotion"?
Lin Yu was puzzled.
But before he could inquire further, April chimed in.
"Right, his bounty is worth eight thousand credit points..."
Hearing this, Lin Yu froze.
"How much?!"
"Eight thousand points."
April said seriously.
Lin Yu suddenly felt his eyes grow hot.
Eight thousand points... wasn't that eight hundred thousand RMB?!
Capturing him could get his sister a whole new storefront!
Even if not for his sister, saving that amount would mean not worrying about "finding a job" for years after graduation—he could keep acting in the plays he loved!
Lin Yu instantly felt regret.
Had he known earlier, he would've tried to kill the guy in the dungeon.
Unforgotten couldn't help adding, "Do you even check the forum? 'Heavenly Artisan' is the hottest bounty post recently!"
Lin Yu shook his head. "I told you, I just cleared my first dungeon. I haven't figured everything out yet."
Hearing this, Unforgotten looked stunned.
"Wait, you really only cleared one dungeon? I was planning to use you to challenge the second statement as a lie!"
Lin Yu spread his hands. "Feel free to test me if you don't believe."
"Not necessary," Unforgotten said, then smiled at April and Number Eight. "But you two better hurry, or I might steal your confirmed 'lie'!"
"The Crow-Man said not everyone might pass... Some of these five statements could be truths mixed in!"
At this, April and Number Eight's expressions changed again.
Lin Yu also watched them with interest.
Frankly, after the Crow-Man's statements, these two had shown the most troubled expressions.
Something very interesting was definitely about to happen between this couple.
Just as Lin Yu predicted,
Prompted by Unforgotten's warning,
April and Number Eight gritted their teeth and spoke simultaneously:
"I choose number four!"
Their voices overlapped perfectly.
The Crow-Man looked at them and laughed heartily.
"Interesting! State your reasoning—the young man was slightly faster, so you'll speak first!"
The fourth statement the Crow-Man had made earlier...
Was: "Between the two of you who know each other, neither has ever betrayed the other."
April and Number Eight stared at each other, their expressions grim.
April spoke in a low voice.
"Say it—how did you betray me?"
Number Eight paled, biting his lip as he spoke.
"I... A-Yao, I'm sorry. That night during finals week last year when I told you I was pulling an all-nighter at the library..."
"I actually went to see my ex-girlfriend."

chapters.title: Chapter 58: Lovers Turned Foes, Blood Debt Paid in Blood
chapters.content:
After Number Eight confessed with a face full of guilt.
April slowly exhaled, her eyes gradually turning cold.
This young woman with the 'Doctor' profession had a rather gentle appearance.
But at this moment, her icy expression sent chills down even Lin Yu's spine.
April looked at her boyfriend and spoke softly.
"I actually had some suspicions about this matter long ago, but I never imagined you'd truly reached the point of 'betraying' me that day."
Number Eight wanted to explain himself, but could only lower his head weakly in the end: "I'm sorry, A-Yao."
April let out a cold laugh: "Save your insincere apologies. You didn't wrong me - you only wronged yourself."
After saying this, April paused.
"No wait, you did wrong me too - never mind all those final assignments I helped you with, just think about how many times I've saved you in this 'Death Game'?""Even after going through life and death together, did she still mean more than me? Just because she's pretty and wild? I hope you enjoyed your STDs!"
April mocked mercilessly.
Number Eight finally couldn't take April's accusations anymore: "Don't slander her like that... besides, that was a whole year ago!"
"Just that one time a year ago?" April interrupted coldly, "Think harder - don't lie to yourself too."
Number Eight's face changed dramatically: "You knew all along?"
"Before this dungeon, they were just suspicions... no, more like willful blindness," April shook her head with a smile, "And just now you actually defended her... good, very good."
As April spoke, Number Eight's face flushed red.
"So what? She didn't actually do anything wrong... besides, the only reason I'm trapped in this damn game is because you insisted on taking that trip that day... you owe me this life!"
Number Eight roared. April froze momentarily before bursting into laughter.
"Good! Good! So that's what you really think!"
"Yeah, so what?" Number Eight completely abandoned his previously meek demeanor and shouted, "You're just a control-freak with attachment issues! I've never felt relaxed with you - all you do is belittle and insult me over and over... so what if you saved me? I never asked you to!"
April watched the furious Number Eight coldly.
This only made Number Eight more hysterical: "You're no better! You were going to pick the fourth option too - doesn't that mean you betrayed me first?!"
He glared at April angrily.
April shook her head: "No, I didn't betray you. I chose the fourth option... because I was thinking about what happened at the library last year - and when you said you were going to the internet cafe last week, and your high school reunion last month."
"But more than 'clearing the game', I wanted to confirm whether those things were true."
Right on cue, Crow-Man's voice rang out.
"Caw caw, congratulations, you may now leave the dungeon."
As Crow-Man spoke, he tossed the key to Number Eight.
April looked at Number Eight and simply shook her head.
"Get lost."
She waved dismissively. Number Eight roared back: "Fine, I'm gone!"
With that, Number Eight took the key and walked toward the foggy exit.
April watched his retreating figure and exhaled, her expression utterly exhausted.
Lin Yu and Unforgotten watched this 'Doctor' with great interest.
"What an entertaining show. So scumbags aren't just the playboy type... and anger after being cheated on can be this restrained."
Lin Yu mused while rubbing his chin.
Unforgotten walked up and patted April's shoulder.
"Hey, are you really just letting him leave like that?"
April shook her head.
"Whatever, he can do what he wants..."
"To be honest, I'm tired - even though the god who designed this 'Death Game' said only those who desperately want to live get chosen."
"I really wanted to live before... but now... I'm just exhausted."
April said wearily.
Unforgotten stuffed her hands in her pockets and shook her head: "Don't let emotions cloud your judgment. Are you an orphan? Other than that trash boyfriend, you've got nothing else right?"
"You two were classmates right... both students, yet you awakened the 'Doctor' profession. You must've been a top medical student."
"Wouldn't your survival be more valuable than that useless, morally bankrupt scumbag's?"
In just a few sentences, Unforgotten seemed to strike a chord in April's heart.
Hesitantly, April looked at Unforgotten: "But... I don't know which of the remaining three statements are lies anymore..."
"You actually do know," Unforgotten smiled, pulling out her utility knife. With a series of 'click-clack' sounds, she extended the blade segment by segment. "Sister April... didn't there come a moment just now - when he defended that bitch, when he blamed you, when he showed no gratitude - when you didn't have this thought?"
"This is the 'Death Game' after all."
April silently took the utility knife from Unforgotten, her eyes darkening like an abyss.
If her gaze earlier was 'icy', then now...
April's eyes had become bottomless voids.
Then she turned to Crow-Man.
"I believe your fifth statement was the lie."
Crow-Man looked at April and laughed.
"Caw caw, then... please provide proof!"
Without a word, April strode swiftly toward the gate with the utility knife, her pace quickening until she was nearly running.
Finally—
Just before reaching the gate, she pounced on Number Eight's figure as he was about to use the key.
"What are you doing!"
"A-Yao, that hurts!"
"I was wrong, A-Yao... stop stabbing!"
"Help!"
"You bitch, just die!"
"Ah—"
Piercing screams rang out one after another.
Then complete silence.
Soon after, April returned covered in blood. She gently wiped the splattered blood from her face, carefully holding the knife's blade to return it to Unforgotten.New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on
"Thank you, Miss Unforgotten."
Then she looked at Crow-Man.
"Is this proof sufficient?"
Crow-Man observed the blood-drenched April and laughed cheerfully.
"Caw caw, how splendid—more than sufficient! You may leave now!"
It waved its hand, and another key materialized in its grasp.
As Crow-Man tossed the key to April, the 'Doctor' caught it and looked back at Unforgotten.
Unforgotten smiled and waved her off.
"Don't mention it... so, how do you feel now?"
April smiled.
"I feel wonderful."
With that, she turned and walked toward the foggy passage's end.

chapters.title: Chapter 59: A Web of Lies
chapters.content:
April's figure quickly disappeared through the mist-shrouded door at the far end.
Only Unforgotten and Lin Yu remained on the field.
Lin Yu looked at Unforgotten with a strange expression.
While "April" had indeed harbored killing intent toward "Number Eight" for some time,
the final push that made April strike had largely come from this seemingly innocent girl before him.
Noticing Lin Yu's gaze, Unforgotten gave an embarrassed laugh.
"Brother Nine Waters, would you like to choose first?"
Lin Yu stared at her and said quietly, "You go first... You'll probably pick the 'number of dungeons cleared' option, right?"
"You don't seem like someone who's only cleared three dungeons."
Caught in her lie, Unforgotten crossed her arms. "Oh dear, you saw through me... I couldn't help it earlier—I really can't stand 'scumbags'!"Her face broke into a radiant smile.
"Your acting was excellent—I almost believed you," Lin Yu sighed. "But what's the point of hiding how many dungeons you've cleared?"
Unforgotten shrugged. "Just my 'modus operandi.' After all, my class is 『Thief』—playing weak actually helps me use my abilities more effectively!"
As she spoke, her smile widened.
"Don't believe me? Why not check your belongings?"
Lin Yu's face showed alarm as he summoned his two "items."
Fortunately, both the Lie Detector and pistol were still there.
He looked at Unforgotten in confusion, prompting another burst of laughter from her.
"Ahahaha! Fooled you again, 『Soldier』!" Unforgotten waved her hand, revealing a pitch-black hammer. "I stole this instead—when that guy revealed himself as 'Heavenly Artisan,' of course I targeted him!"
"This thing is way more valuable than your pistol," she said cheerfully.
Lin Yu picked up the Lie Detector and said coldly,
"Who are you really? How many dungeons have you cleared? What's your purpose in approaching me?"
Unforgotten pursed her lips.
"Your Lie Detector still works?"
"Of course. It can be used three times per dungeon," Lin Yu lied smoothly. "So don't try deceiving me."
"Otherwise, even if you're stronger, I'll fight you to the death here."
As he spoke, Lin Yu felt a surge of "belief" emanating from Unforgotten.
Instantly, his fabricated claim about the Lie Detector having three uses 『materialized』 as truth.
Just as he'd estimated—had he said four uses, this "belief" might not have been enough to actualize the lie.
"Relax... I'm just a girl looking for fun. I didn't specifically target you."
"I'm not from the 『Psychological Society』 or the 『Marauders』, so you can rest easy," Unforgotten said playfully.
Lin Yu removed his finger from the button.
Her words were true.
"Then how many dungeons have you cleared?" he demanded coldly.
"Only twelve in three short months," Unforgotten stuck out her tongue. "And I'm not that strong—my direct combat abilities are weak."
The Lie Detector remained silent.
Lin Yu exhaled.
"Fine..."
He put away the device and immediately addressed Crow-Man: "I choose the second statement, because she just admitted to clearing twelve dungeons—contradicting her initial claim of three."
Lin Yu spoke rapidly.
Crow-Man responded instantly:
"Caw caw! Congratulations for spotting the lie... You may leave now!"
Unforgotten looked stunned, then burst into laughter again.
"Ahahaha! So that's your game... You tricked me!"
"What a great trick... You never cared about my origins or motives—you just wanted to trap me like this!"
Lin Yu nodded calmly.
"Of course. While your acting was superb, I could still tell," he sighed. "You're more confident than you let on, but... you really are just here for fun."
He accepted the key from Crow-Man.
Unforgotten narrowed her eyes. "I see... So my only way out now is proving why the 'third statement' is false."
"My class truly is 『Thief』, meaning... you lied about yours, right?"
Lin Yu shook his head. "No, I really am a 『Soldier』... That's the crux of this final 'decision question.'"
"Among the five statements, one appears to correspond to each person—but actually, one doesn't match anyone. So I had to steal someone's 'key.'"
As Lin Yu spoke, Unforgotten studied him.
"I find that hard to believe. Wouldn't that put you at a huge disadvantage?"
Yet despite her words, Lin Yu could sense
his 『Soldier』 class remained intact—
meaning Unforgotten had actually believed him.
Just as he'd anticipated.
After all, he'd sounded completely convincing!
"So," Lin Yu smiled, "while this is only my second dungeon... Miss Veteran Player Unforgotten, after a dozen dungeons, do you still think this game is 'fair'?"
Unforgotten chuckled softly.Google seaʀᴄh NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
"Alright... You're right. This game isn't fair at all."
Lin Yu jingled the key. "Exactly. Besides... Now you're the one with problems."
Unforgotten sighed. "True. Good thing I always leave myself an out."
"You're impressive, 『Soldier』 Nine Waters. You're fascinating," she said with a wave. "Hope we meet again—whether outside or in another dungeon."
Lin Yu narrowed his eyes at her words. "You can leave too?"
"Of course... You must have realized—there only seems to be one key, but that's not actually the case."
Lin Yu looked toward the corpse still lying before the distant door.
"So that's why you instigated his murder."
Unforgotten smiled.
"Right. If someone had to stay behind... better it be that boring guy."
She turned toward the door.
"See you later, Brother Nine Waters."
With light steps, she approached the corpse and retrieved another key, holding it up for Lin Yu to see.
Then she opened the door and disappeared through it.
After Unforgotten vanished, Crow-Man addressed Lin Yu:
"Caw caw, you may leave now too."
Lin Yu turned to face Crow-Man and exhaled.
He casually tossed aside the key, his expression curious.
"When did I say I wanted to leave?"
Crow-Man fell silent.
"Caw... This is the final question..."
"Wrong. This is the first 'reward/punishment' question of the third room. The reward is leaving the dungeon," Lin Yu interrupted with a grin. "But I refuse it."
"Honestly, everyone's been lying to me—the kind-looking uncle was actually vicious, that cheerful guy had ulterior motives... Even you, 'Examiner,' are full of deceit."
Lin Yu stepped forward, looking up at Crow-Man.
"Stop wasting time. I've seen through all your tricks and lies."
"Frankly—your acting isn't as good as that 『Thief』's just now."

chapters.title: Chapter 60: Speak My Name
chapters.content:
After hearing Lin Yu's words, the Crow-Man chuckled softly.
"Caw caw, you're even more impressive than I imagined, Player 'Lin Yu'."
"I'm quite curious—how did you figure it out? Was it just because of my 'acting'?"
When the Crow-Man revealed his real name, Lin Yu remained composed and spoke unhurriedly.
"To be honest, it wasn't just your 'acting.'"
"You yourself have been giving us 'hints' all along... frankly, once you notice them, they're quite obvious."
"That's why I had to deliberately steal Unforgotten's key in the end to mislead her—to keep her thinking limited and focused on 'how do I get out'."
"After all, she's quite clever too."
As Lin Yu spoke, the Crow-Man spread its wings.
"Then... where exactly did I give you hints?""Caw—in the second challenge, we learned that 'caw' represents a 'negative' answer," Lin Yu said. "But aside from appearing alone, it can also be used at the start of a sentence as a 'negative' marker. Am I right?"
"From the moment we entered the game until now, every sentence you spoke that began with a single 'caw' was a lie."
"And those with two 'caw's represent a double negative that equals affirmation—meaning they're truths. So most of your rule explanations were lies."
Lin Yu paused here before continuing.
"After entering the third room, when you said this was the 'final room' and 'this room only has one question,' you only used one 'caw,' meaning both statements were false."
"This also aligns with what you said when explaining the general rules in the first room!"
"'This game consists of three rooms in total'—one 'caw,' false, proving the third room isn't actually the last."
"'Each room contains three questions'—two 'caws,' true, meaning this room should indeed have three questions."
"And that last sentence in all the rules back then... you first said two 'caws,' paused, then one 'caw,' meaning that statement was half-true—I believe the first half was true while the latter half was false."
"That latter half was 'answering all decision questions correctly will clear the dungeon'... which is false. You don't need to answer all decision questions correctly to clear it."
"Going back to the first two rooms... you also hinted through your questions that you, the Examiner, are someone who 'lies.'"
As Lin Yu laid out his clear reasoning, the Crow-Man burst into laughter.
"Caw caw, what a brilliant analysis! While realizing the meaning of 'caw' and 'caw caw' isn't difficult... you actually remembered every single thing I said!"
"Nothing special."
Lin Yu replied modestly.
For him, this truly wasn't difficult—his memory had always been decent.Follow current novels on
Memorizing random numbers or patterns might be challenging, but remembering people's words...
That came relatively easily.
After all, memorizing lines is an actor's fundamental skill.
The Crow-Man looked at Lin Yu with admiration in its eyes.
"Caw caw, excellent, excellent. I'm growing fonder of you by the minute..."
Despite Lin Yu having criticized its acting and deceit earlier, the Crow-Man didn't seem angry.
It paced back and forth, studying Lin Yu up and down.
Then, Lin Yu spoke softly.
"Can we proceed to the next question now?"
The Crow-Man laughed heartily.
"Caw caw, of course. Listen carefully to this room's second question..."
"Who designed this dungeon? Speak his name!"
As the Crow-Man spoke, Lin Yu froze.
"You absolute bastard, throwing out this kind of 'unreasonable' question now."
He instinctively cursed.
All previous questions—while potentially full of traps or twisted—had at least been "traceable."
They could be reasoned through and analyzed to deduce answers.
But this question...
It reminded Lin Yu of a scene from a novel he'd read—a battle of wits where two geniuses competed to stump each other.
One contestant broke all unwritten rules by asking "what did I eat for breakfast today"—an utterly unanswerable, meaningless question bordering on cheating.
While that novel's protagonist had near-omniscient intelligence and could deduce answers even to such "unreasonable" questions through minute clues...
Lin Yu lacked such abilities. He was just a sophomore performance major at Jiangcheng Media University—nothing more than a college student more passionate about acting than most.
While this question wasn't completely "unreasonable" (after all, Lin Yu had experienced the entire dungeon)...
Questions like these could easily be made unanswerable if the designer wished.
What if the dungeon's creator was named "Dala Bengba Bandebeidibudobiruweng" or some other nonsense?
Facing Lin Yu's skepticism, the Crow-Man laughed.
"Caw caw, you may still ask me questions or request hints... though I won't answer things like 'how many characters in the name' or 'what syllables it contains.'"
Hearing this, Lin Yu exhaled.
"Fine."
He calmed down upon the Crow-Man's words.
Thinking carefully—while this Crow-Man had terrible taste in humor (worse than Unforgotten's)—the entire dungeon had followed logical patterns.
In other words, this seemingly "unreasonable" question must have its own solution.
It must be hidden somewhere within the game.
Lin Yu pondered slowly until...
A spark of inspiration flashed through his mind.
He recalled the Crow-Man's very first words.
"Caw caw, I will serve as this game's Examiner"—two 'caws' meaning truth, plus being the opening line, had made Lin Yu instinctively overlook this statement.
But upon reflection...
Just as the Crow-Man had done in the first room.
One of its habitual tactics was "using truths to deceive."
So...
That opening line was a trap.
Lin Yu looked at the Crow-Man: "May I ask—what is your name?"
The Crow-Man chuckled.
"Caw caw, I refuse to answer that."
Lin Yu understood.
"As I thought... you're not just this game's Examiner. You're also its designer."
He exhaled, and the Crow-Man laughed softly.
"Ahahahaha."
For the first time, it emitted a human-like laugh—though the timbre remained that of countless overlapping voices.
"How delightfully surprising, Lin Yu. You figured it out instantly."
"However... this doesn't count as your success."
"You must still speak 'my name.'"
So declared the Crow-Man.

chapters.title: Chapter 61: Future Lin Yu, Lin Yu the God?
chapters.content:
Lin Yu had long vaguely sensed that the Crow-Man in front of him was “the designer of this dungeon.”
Because the degree to which it controlled this game… was simply overwhelming!
So, Lin Yu couldn’t help but test it a little earlier.
In the first two rooms, Lin Yu had subtly praised the dungeon designer.
Judging by the Crow-Man’s slightly pleased reaction back then…
It must indeed have been him.
Those who design such intricately linked, trap-filled questions—whether human or something else—often have a bit of narcissism.
Having confirmed that this somewhat narcissistic Crow-Man was “the game designer”…
Though the name still had to be guessed, Lin Yu now had a direction.
He exhaled and looked at the Crow-Man.“Your ‘name’ has actually already appeared in this game, hasn’t it?”
The Crow-Man looked at Lin Yu and nodded.
“Caw caw, that’s right, it has appeared, and in full form.”
“I see,” Lin Yu whispered, “How disrespectful of me—I didn’t expect that standing before me was a ‘god.’”
As he spoke, the Crow-Man laughed.
“Caw caw, it seems you already know my identity… So, which god do you think I am?”
The Crow-Man asked, and Lin Yu grinned widely.
“It’s simple. In the second room, the crow representing the incarnation of ‘Change’ can transform into an image just like yours.”
“That one represents the ‘God of Change’… right?”
“And your behavior in this game is both truthful and deceitful.”
Lin Yu said, and the Crow-Man laughed again.
“That’s right… You’re incredibly clever, Lin Yu. Hurry and give me your answer.”
Looking at the Crow-Man, Lin Yu remained silent.
He narrowed his eyes and spoke softly.
“So, you really want my answer to be ‘God of Change,’ don’t you?”
Once this question was posed,
The Crow-Man fell silent.
After a moment, he laughed sincerely again.
“Hahaha, it’s really hard to fool you…”
“Yes, after playing a whole game of ‘trap questions,’ it wouldn’t make sense if there were no traps at this moment.”
Lin Yu said calmly.
The Crow-Man looked at Lin Yu: “Is there another reason?”
“There’s also your narcissistic personality, and the deliberately ambiguous wording in the second room,” Lin Yu said. “When you introduced the two and three crows, you said ‘two great gods transformed into crow avatars’ and ‘three great gods transformed into crow avatars’…”
“To be honest, this can be understood as ‘avatars of three different gods’…”
Lin Yu paused for a moment.
“But it can just as easily be understood as ‘three different avatars of one god’… right?”
Lin Yu opened his hands.
“Judging by the personality you have shown so far, calling other gods ‘great’ really doesn’t match my observations of you… So my answer is…”
“The game designer’s name is ‘Truth, Falsehood, and God of Change’… roughly something like that. You probably wouldn’t be too particular about the exact words or order, right?”
After Lin Yu finished speaking, the Crow-Man laughed and shook his head.
“Brilliant, truly brilliant. You are frighteningly perceptive.”
“‘Truth, Falsehood, and God of Change’ is my name… Congratulations, you got this question right.”
The Crow-Man said this without quibbling over the exact wording with Lin Yu.
“Let’s move on to the next question. The reward this time is that you can make one request to me, though… I can still refuse.”
“Oh, and there’s a shorter ‘answer’ to the previous question…”
As he spoke, feathers began to fall off his body one by one, revealing an elegant dark double-breasted suit, white gloves, and leather shoes.
This outfit seemed somewhat familiar to Lin Yu.
Then, the “Crow-Man” raised both hands and took off the crow headpiece.
Lin Yu was stunned when he saw the face beneath the crow headpiece.
Because beneath the mask… was a face identical to his own.
“The other answer to the previous question is ‘Lin Yu.’”
His voice was no longer the overlapping sound of thousands but exactly the same as Lin Yu’s.
He showed a gentle smile.
“Nice to meet you—though for me, this is already the second time.”
“Me, ten years ago.”
The Crow-Man in front of him… no, the “Lin Yu” opposite him smiled.
Lin Yu suddenly felt unreal.
It was like how last week he was suddenly killed and suddenly entered this game.
“You are me from ten years later?!”
“Ten years later… I become a god?!”
That future “Lin Yu” nodded.
“Of course. With the ‘Fraudster’ unique class, plus my intelligence—your intelligence—I solved this game. Becoming a god… wasn’t that difficult.”
“Due to details, I can’t reveal too much of the process, but it wasn’t very hard.”
The god version of “Lin Yu” said proudly.
“You can’t reveal too many details? Then how do you expect me to believe you? After all, you’ve been lying all along!”
The god “Lin Yu” sneered: “‘Manipulating time’ is exclusive to gods. The reason I can meet you from ten years later is because I became a ‘god’… You’d think that a ‘unique class’ and six people believing in you would be enough for you to activate the ‘Rewind’ ability that manipulates time, right?”
“But it’s precisely because you are destined to become a god in the future that you were able to complete that ‘ruse’!”
Lin Yu rubbed his head, his face full of hesitation.
“I still don’t quite believe it. If this is true, what kind of torment did I suffer in this game over the past ten years…? How did my personality become such a birdlike mess?”
The god “Lin Yu” laughed: “Actually, you only went through one thing: realizing that you are smarter than most people… Well, I’m quite surprised myself. I almost forgot how little self-awareness I had ten years ago!”
The god “Lin Yu” shrugged toward Lin Yu.
“In any case, now it’s time to make a choice. I know you have doubts about me,” the god “Lin Yu” said, “So it’s okay. You can choose to believe me or not.”
“If you believe I’m your future self, then choose to follow me over there. We’ll enter the final room, and I will help you obtain everything needed to ‘become a god.’”
The god “Lin Yu” pointed behind the mist.
There, a spiral staircase wound upward.
“Of course, if you don’t believe me, you can take the key and leave through the door… I will still give you enough ‘help’ so that in the next dozen or so dungeons, you won’t have to worry much about survival.”
The god “Lin Yu” said.
Lin Yu still had some doubts, but his expression showed about seventy or eighty percent belief.
“Hmm… But if you really are ‘me from ten years later,’ you should already know what I will choose, right?”
“Wouldn’t you already know what I would choose?”

chapters.title: Chapter 62: The Fourth Room!
chapters.content:
Facing Lin Yu's final doubt, the deity "Lin Yu" waved his hand.
"No, my second dungeon ten years ago wasn't 'Deadly Quiz', but 'Desert Island Survival'... I survived till the end by playing the fisherman role."
Lin Yu recalled.
Though his memories were hazy from nearly drowning, they were gradually becoming clearer now...
The bloody text he saw before entering the game this time did seem somewhat off!
The deity "Lin Yu" continued looking at Lin Yu:
"'Deities' can alter the past—everything can be changed except the fact that you'll inevitably 'ascend to godhood'."
"Just like your 『Rewind』 ability."
Lin Yu stroked his chin, his eyes filled with belief: "Alright, I believe you... but what's the point of doing this?"
"'Changing the past' also affects the future. If you grow stronger faster, I'll become stronger too!""Lin Yu" said solemnly.
Lin Yu looked at him and sighed: "Anyway, let me verify something—what's my girlfriend's name?"
"You don't have a girlfriend."
The deity "Lin Yu" answered immediately.
"There must be one in the future?"
Lin Yu persisted.
"No. I—or rather you—would we ever be the type to want a girlfriend?"
The deity "Lin Yu" responded decisively.
Lin Yu nodded slightly: "Correct answer. Now I believe you... but I want to use the 'reward' from my last question to make a request of you."
"Between us, who stands on ceremony?" The deity "Lin Yu" smiled. "Just say it."
Lin Yu looked at him earnestly: "I say, can you stop spouting nonsense?"
The smile froze on the deity "Lin Yu"'s face.
"You still don't believe me?"
Lin Yu sighed.
"Rejected this request after all... How preposterous. Last dungeon I played a deity, this dungeon a deity is playing me!"
Hearing this, the deity "Lin Yu" showed a trace of anger, clenching his fists.
"I never imagined my ten-years-younger self would be so suspicious! I can name your profession, everything you did in the first dungeon... I know your past inside out! You're investigating who trapped you here, you want to use this game to earn money for your sister, your best friend in real life is Shen Bingmiao..."
Lin Yu sighed.
"Exactly. So you should also know... how passionate I am about acting..."
He interrupted the deity "Lin Yu"'s anger, speaking helplessly: "I already said, your acting can't even compare to 'Unforgotten'—after ten years, even if my acting hasn't improved, it wouldn't regress this much!"
"Look at your 'anger at being distrusted' act—your eyebrows are twitching too exaggeratedly, your tone too rushed... What, after becoming a deity I'd lose the ability to 'immerse' in emotions?"
