"I need to find someplace like a freezer..." he muttered, then considered his options.
Restaurants usually had such places, right?
His sister's restaurant?
No...
Absolutely not.
What about Tycoon's?
Also no good—who knew how long Tycoon's restaurant had been abandoned.
Moreover, Lin Yu didn't particularly want to develop too close a connection with Tycoon.
After much deliberation, Lin Yu arrived at the best solution.
"Looks like the school cafeteria is my only option!"
Lin Yu's mind settled on the most suitable choice available.
As a Jiangcheng Media University student, his presence on campus late at night wouldn't raise suspicions.
He could even tell his sister he was staying at school and send some photos to alleviate Lin Zhao's worries.
As for how to sneak into the cafeteria freezer or cold storage, a complete plan quickly formed in Lin Yu's mind!
"First and second cafeterias are out—they're school-run with centralized cold storage elsewhere, ingredients delivered fresh each morning."
"Cafeteria Four closes late and is too close to the library—those overachievers might spot me..."
"That leaves Cafeteria Three as most suitable—not only is it outsourced, but its location is more remote."
"Most importantly, Cafeteria Three has a back door secured only by an old padlock!"
Having reached this conclusion, Lin Yu went to inspect Cafeteria Three.
It was mealtime, so his presence there wasn't suspicious.
After hastily eating some braised chicken rice, Lin Yu peered through the window at the kitchen area.
Massive freezers were lined up behind each counter—more than spacious enough to hold a person.
Gaining kitchen access would be simple too; though the counters had metal shutters, most wouldn't actually be lowered after closing due to trust in student integrity and campus surveillance.
Thus, Lin Yu confirmed that entering the game from Cafeteria Three's freezer should work.
With this settled, Lin Yu texted his sister Lin Zhao again.
"Working on group project at school tonight, pulling an all-nighter with classmates. Won't be coming home."
Lin Zhao always supported academic matters.
"Okay, don't overexert yourself," came Lin Zhao's prompt reply.
With Lin Zhao's approval secured, Lin Yu spent the remaining time studying on campus.
Seizing the opportunity, he visited the library to review the Shakespeare plays recommended by his professor.
Though he'd read them in high school, after two years of performance studies and several stage appearances, his perspective had changed.
"Shakespeare truly was a genius—writing such brilliant plays during medieval Europe centuries ago..."
Lin Yu marveled.
He couldn't imagine how earth-shattering it must have been for a medieval European actor, accustomed to mediocre scripts, to first encounter these groundbreaking works and yearn to perform them.
Soon...
Night fell quietly.
As the library's closing saxophone melody played, Lin Yu realized—
It was 11 PM!
Nonchalantly replacing the Complete Works of Shakespeare, he exited with the crowd.
While most students streamed toward dorms, Lin Yu silently turned onto a different path leading to Cafeteria Three.
As predicted, the cafeteria near the sports field stood quiet at night—only a few strolling couples broke the stillness.
The back entrance by the staff bike shed was completely deserted.
Lin Yu easily reached the back door and made an unexpected discovery.
"Huh, it's not even locked!"
He stared in surprise at the merely draped padlock.
Cafeteria Three's lack of security exceeded his expectations!
Not only were the counter shutters left open, but even this door was barely secured!
He'd planned to pick the lock using online tutorials or force it open if necessary.
Now, that wouldn't be needed.
Lin Yu quietly opened the door, slipped inside, and closed it behind him.
Inside, he headed straight for a dumpling stall.
This shop was famous for its prepackaged frozen dumplings—though its affordable prices (buy three taels of four-flavor dumplings and get a boxed drink free) kept business booming.
Their freezer was naturally the kitchen's largest.
And completely undivided!
Opening the freezer door revealed bulk dumpling packages stacked inside.
Lin Yu removed two bags, then set a timed text message to Shen Bingmiao on his phone.
"Trapped in Cafeteria Three's dumpling freezer! Help!"
Set for 12:05 AM, after confirming battery and signal, he left the phone outside on a table.
Though the freezer seemed openable from inside, Lin Yu feared potential mishaps.
Passing the Death Game only to freeze to death in here would be truly unfortunate!

chapters.title: Chapter 75: Entering the Game! Promotion Trial and the Fraudster!
chapters.content:
Nighttime, 11:50 PM.
After climbing into the freezer and closing its heavy door, Lin Yu soon felt a slight chill creeping through his body.
Having seen the dungeon's entry requirements earlier, he had specifically visited the drama club before going to the library that afternoon to borrow a thick coat.
Now with the additional face mask, Lin Yu's outfit was indeed sufficient to withstand Jiangcheng's "harsh winter."
Even so, Lin Yu's exposed skin still prickled with mild stinging pain.
"After all, it's a freezer. The cooling effect is really impressive."
Lin Yu exhaled and tried opening the freezer door in the complete darkness.
No issues...it could definitely be opened from inside.
However, Lin Yu still didn't cancel the timed message set on his phone outside.
It could be opened now, but what if something went wrong?If he exited safely, he could always manually cancel the freezer's alert message.
Therefore, Lin Yu remained calm.
As time passed minute by minute inside the freezer, Lin Yu gradually began shivering from the cold, showing symptoms of hypothermia.
His consciousness started fading.
Then...
Just as Lin Yu felt himself about to lose consciousness.
Blood-red text appeared!
[Entering game soon—]
[Game Name: Frostpeak Mountains]
[Clear Condition: Survive seven days]
[Current game player count: 13]
...
[Detected that you will undertake a 'Promotion Trial' in this game. Loading special tasks now.]
[Promotion Task 1: During this game, tell each participating player a different lie that completely contradicts all others, then activate your 'Fraudster' class ability to make them 'come true.' Ensure none of these lies are exposed or seen through until game ends.]
[Promotion Task 2: Find the hidden 'Fraudster' in this game and expose their deception.]
[Complete both tasks to pass this Promotion Trial.]
[Tasks are not mandatory.]
Significantly more blood-red text than before squirmed into view.
Lin Yu's consciousness gradually cleared.
"So this is the Promotion Trial? It's indeed highly relevant to the 'Fraudster' class!"
Lin Yu understood immediately.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
The first task required lying to each person with different, mutually contradictory lies.
In other words, he needed to tell twelve lies, make all twelve come true, and avoid detection.
The second task...was rather puzzling.
Find the 'Fraudster' and expose their deception.
'Fraudster' was clearly a specific reference, but to what?
Lin Yu knew the 'Death Game' did have a class called 'Fraudster.'
Not extremely rare, but relatively common.
Though it sounded similar to 'Fraudster,' their abilities were completely different.
The 'Fraudster' class was typical Rule Type, able to randomly create a "false rule" beneficial to themselves that lasted for a duration based on the dungeon's length.
It sounded similar to the Fraudster's 'Make True,' but 'Fraudsters' couldn't control what rules they created.
Conversely, 'Fraudsters' didn't need others to believe them or even require a "target."
They just needed to activate their ability for it to work.
Lin Yu initially wondered if among the thirteen players, another had the 'Fraudster' class.
But upon reflection, that possibility seemed unlikely.
Unlike 'Fraudsters,' 'Fraudsters' had no reason to hide their class.
This "Frostpeak Mountains" dungeon was clearly survival-type, likely requiring teamwork.
Thus, players would probably "cooperate" and share their classes.
Even if the 'Fraudster' had a terrible personality and loved lying—like the 'Thief' A Nian he'd met before—
It would still be hard to conceal!
After all, rules created by 'Fraudster' abilities were known to all players.
Hiding their class wouldn't be easy.
Having considered this, Lin Yu currently had no leads on the second task.
"Need to wait for the game to progress and gather more information before further analysis."
Lin Yu quickly formulated his strategy.
"First work on Task One while ensuring my safety, simultaneously collecting clues about the 'Fraudster.'"
As Lin Yu reached this conclusion, he fully regained consciousness.
His senses sharpened abruptly—howling winds roared past his ears, icy snowflakes stinging his face.
Opening his eyes, he saw nothing but white. He lay on a simple wooden bed in the last intact corner of a snow-collapsed cabin.
A burly middle-aged man wearing a fur hat and old coat sat at the entrance.
Hearing Lin Yu stir, the man turned around, his frost-reddened face showing surprise.
"Oh! You're awake! I thought you'd frozen to death!"
Studying the man, Lin Yu sat up from the bed with growing suspicion.
His appearance and words suggested a "game NPC"!
Lin Yu quickly verified using methods taught on the "forum."
He tried discussing the 'Death Game,' but like with ordinary people in reality...
He couldn't utter any information about the 'Death Game'!
This was one quick way to identify "players" versus "NPCs."
Though some "game NPCs" could recognize they were in a 'game.'
Like the "Crow-Man" from last game—after all, it was literally a deity's avatar.
But most "game NPCs" in 'Death Game' dungeons didn't know they were serving as NPCs or that players from other worlds had invaded their lives.
They'd explain rules and guide players through "reasonable" means—like the "letter" Lin Yu saw in his first dungeon.
Though he never met the writer, that person was a classic NPC.
Of course, some might be hostile or even enemies players needed to fight.
However...
Looking at this rugged man, Lin Yu guessed:
"This is probably a friendly NPC!"
Keeping his composure, Lin Yu gripped the pistol hidden in his coat and asked:
"Who are you?"

chapters.title: Chapter 76: A Thorny Problem
chapters.content:
Facing Lin Yu’s cautious inquiry, the burly uncle chuckled.
“I’m just like you, a prospector here in the mountain searching for treasure.”
“Just didn’t expect such heavy snow to close off the mountain so quickly.”
The burly uncle exhaled warm breath into his hands and continued.
“Even the ‘Abandoned Village’ marked on this map as a temporary resting spot has been crushed under the snow. Looks like we need to find a new base where we can light a fire as soon as possible.”
“There should be other camps or caves around here.”
“It’s fine during the day, but at night, the wind and snow get even worse. Plus, you might run into a ‘Chate,’ and that would be really bad!”
Lin Yu frowned slightly.
“What’s a ‘Chate’?”
The uncle looked at Lin Yu in surprise.“You came here to the ‘Extreme Winter Mountain’ to hunt for treasure without even knowing that?”
“Besides the extreme climate, the ‘Chate’ is the scariest thing you’ll face in the mountain.”
He answered seriously.
“Legend has it that various snow monsters dwell in this Extreme Winter Mountain, preying on humans.”
“The leader of these monsters, the strongest one, is called the ‘Chate’!”
“No one knows exactly what the ‘Chate’ looks like. Everyone who’s seen it is dead...”
“Those who haven’t seen it directly have gone insane from fear. Some say it’s ten meters tall, with sharp claws and teeth. Others say it’s a moving block of ice and rock—but one thing is certain, the ‘Chate’ is definitely not something humans can fight against.”
The burly uncle said this, and Lin Yu, surprised and frightened, asked again.
“Snow monsters? The Chate? What should we do then?!”
The burly uncle fell for it.
“Only burning firelight can keep humans safe from the ‘Chate’ at night.”
“Also, it’s not recommended to travel in groups in Extreme Winter Mountain. More than three people increases the chance of being targeted by the ‘Chate’ or other snow monsters. Within one base, it’s best not to have more than two people.”
The burly uncle said this, then looked at Lin Yu with some puzzlement.
“How did you come to Extreme Winter Mountain to hunt treasure without knowing anything?”
Lin Yu said embarrassedly, “Actually, I’m not here to hunt treasure. I just got lost and accidentally entered here... Are there really treasures in this mountain?”
Lin Yu asked sincerely.
Looking at Lin Yu’s earnest and curious face, the uncle was momentarily stunned, then somewhat surprised.
“You got lost all the way into the depths of Extreme Winter Mountain? The wind and snow haven’t stopped here at all. Just one look and you’d know you shouldn’t go any deeper!”
But soon, the uncle relaxed.
“Forget it. You look so dumbfounded, you don’t seem like a very clear-headed person anyway.”
“Every year, during the worst snowstorms in Extreme Winter Mountain, you can dig up a kind of black paste in the snow. That stuff is top-quality fuel, called ‘Black Gold Oil’ by the big shots, and we common folk just call it ‘Black Oil.’”
The burly uncle said this, his eyes full of longing: “With a bit of refining, it can also be made into an ointment that heals all kinds of wounds.”
“No one knows where this black oil comes from. They only know it appears in the snowy areas of Extreme Winter Mountain—and every time it’s found, it’s packed in wooden boxes or chests, which is quite strange.”
“That’s why the process of hunting for black oil is called ‘treasure hunting.’”
“Some say it’s a gift from the gods to mortals; others say it’s a relic of an old civilization brought by the wind and snow; and some say... it might be related to the ‘Chate.’”
“But the origin doesn’t matter. What matters is that a whole box of this stuff can really secure you wealth and glory!”
The burly uncle said this, his expression growing excited.
“Alright, since this base is already destroyed... I need to hurry and find the next one!”
Saying that, the uncle took out a crumpled map from his pocket.
“If you just die here in the mountain, that’d be pitiful. Here, take this map and find a base yourself—just don’t go in the same direction as me.”
“Our current position is the spot marked ‘B6’ in green ink.”
“The more people there are, the higher the chance of being targeted by snow monsters and the ‘Chate.’”
The uncle said this, then waved goodbye to Lin Yu and left in one direction.
Lin Yu unfolded the map and glanced over it.
Although the map was simple, he still understood it.
The map was densely filled with many small codes in different colors.
There was a legend in the bottom right corner.
Red represented areas with frequent snow monster activity.
Green represented temporary bases where one could light fires and rest overnight.
Black represented areas where large amounts of ‘black oil’ had been found before.
The abandoned ‘B6’ base where Lin Yu was located lay slightly left and downward in the middle of the map.
Comparing it to the real terrain, the uncle had gone east to the right.
There were far more bases than expected—almost a hundred on the map.
In contrast, red and black areas were fewer.
There were only eight regions with high snow monster activity. Even though their circled areas were larger than the bases, together they covered less than a quarter of the map.
As for the black areas, there were only three tiny circles—and all were inside the red regions.
However, according to the map’s notes, ‘black oil’ could be found everywhere, and snow monsters were not limited to those marked dangerous red zones.
“So, the first step in this game is to find a base... If you have time, you can look for ‘black oil,’ which probably grants some item rewards after clearing.”
Lin Yu thought, understanding something.
This ‘survival dungeon’... wasn’t that hard.
Although the environment was extremely cold and there was a certain powerful monster that couldn’t be confronted directly,
the abundance of ‘bases’ and the monsters’ movement patterns—where lighting a fire and traveling alone greatly reduced the chance of attack—made clearing this dungeon not that difficult.
However, Lin Yu’s concern was not just about ‘clearing’ it.
He still had two ‘Promotions’ tasks to complete.
“I originally thought the hardest part of the first task was how to lie to everyone without being exposed. But now it seems I was wrong...”
Lin Yu sighed, exhaling deeply.
Although this dungeon had thirteen players, apparently to avoid ‘many hands make light work,’ it deliberately made survival in the extreme environment require division of labor by using the monster called ‘Chate’ to force all players not to stay together too long.
For Lin Yu, although having two people corroborate each other lowered the chance of his lies being discovered,
finding other players had become more difficult—how to find people was a thorny problem.
“I have to find a way to locate the other players!”
If he couldn’t meet anyone, what was the point of lying?
Thinking of this, Lin Yu realized something and hurried after the burly uncle who had just left.
“Hey, uncle, wait a moment!”

chapters.title: Chapter 77: Ability Activated! Searching for Outposts!
chapters.content:
Hearing Lin Yu's voice following him, the burly man turned to glare at him angrily.
"I already told you, following me like this will easily attract snow monsters and Chate!"
"In Extreme Winter Mountain, it's best to travel alone!"
"Besides, it's almost nightfall - we don't have time to waste!"
As he spoke, Lin Yu wiped the ice particles from his face.
"Actually...I'm not here to travel with you. I just have some questions."
"Are there many people like you who come to 'treasure hunt' in Extreme Winter Mountain?"
Lin Yu asked quietly.
"About a dozen or so. Not everyone has the courage to enter Extreme Winter Mountain," the burly man eyed Lin Yu suspiciously. "Why do you ask?"
"Oh, I want to know how to find others. I got separated from my friend and want to get us both out of this damned place quickly," Lin Yu said seriously."Well...people can enter from any direction of Extreme Winter Mountain. As you can see on the map, all four slopes are gentle - the main problem is the blizzard."
"But leaving is much harder than entering...we all wait for the storm to weaken. Trying to leave during strong winds almost guarantees Chate will notice you."
"Even if you survive, the best outcome is being driven insane by Chate," the burly man warned.
"Don't worry, uncle. I'm actually great at climbing and extremely cold-resistant. Chate might not even catch me," Lin Yu said earnestly. "You know, even in this blizzard, I can walk as if on flat ground, moving swiftly at full speed if needed."
The burly man looked at Lin Yu's serious expression with disbelief.
"You're lying. How fast could you possibly run in these conditions?"
Lin Yu spread his hands: "Didn't I just catch up to you as proof?"
The man remained skeptical: "But I hadn't gone far yet."
Seeing his continued doubt, Lin Yu thought for a moment before speaking.
"Alright, I wasn't going to tell you this...but your earlier kindness makes me feel guilty hiding the truth."
"Actually, I was specially hired by the wealthy to 'remap' this area."
Lin Yu picked up the man's map and flicked it lightly.
"As you said earlier, temporary outpost B6 is no longer functional...I'm here specifically to identify which outposts can't be used anymore."
"So in a way, I'm a 'professional' - specializing in extreme environment cartography."
Before the man could react, Lin Yu returned the map to him.
"If you don't believe me, test me. I've memorized this map completely - if I can recite it, you'll have to believe I'm a professional hired by the lords, right?"
As Lin Yu spoke, the man subconsciously took the map.
"Is that really true...?"
Without further thought, he began quizzing Lin Yu.
"Then, what are the nearest temporary outposts to B6...?"
"To the right is C2, above is A7, below is E3. Closer would be A12 to the lower right, then E9 to the left," Lin Yu answered calmly.
The man was stunned.
"You really do remember...then where's B11?"
"Mid-left section of the map, terrain suggests a valley entrance," Lin Yu replied evenly.
Now completely shocked speechless, the man finally said:
"I believe you...you really are here to map the area!"
The burly man didn't realize that Lin Yu's rhetoric had subconsciously linked "memorizing the map" with being a "professional cartographer" in his mind.
Combined with the rarity of someone memorizing the chaotic map - evident from how even this dedicated treasure hunter carried a physical copy - the man had almost completely accepted Lin Yu's story.
"I never thought those lords would be so kind-hearted!"
Hearing this, Lin Yu adopted an expression that said "the waters run deep here, don't ask" and shook his head.
"No, it's not for your benefit. The lords are just dissatisfied with Black Gold Oil production rates."
The burly man nodded, convinced.
"I see...but this information you've shared is invaluable."
He looked at Lin Yu gratefully.
"Your earlier kindness moved me," Lin Yu said seriously. "But since you understand this information's value, keep it quiet."
The man nodded vigorously.
"Absolutely, absolutely! I know how to keep secrets!"
He mimed zipping his lips, giving a "rest assured" expression.
Lin Yu waved him off.
"Alright, go about your business. I need to check several more outposts."
"Though I walk quickly, the distance still needs covering."
With that, he turned and disappeared into the blizzard.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
Once alone, Lin Yu immediately felt his steps lighten.
His frozen joints became more flexible.
His uneven footsteps steadied.
It was as if he'd suddenly mastered a technique for swift snow travel.
Lin Yu marveled:
"As expected, abilities work on NPCs too."
His newfound speed came from the burly man believing Lin Yu's story.
That belief made Lin Yu's words "true" - after all, walking quickly in snow wasn't particularly unbelievable.
Lin Yu had deliberately circled back to talk with the man precisely to gain enhanced mobility for finding other Players.
Moving swiftly through the snow, he soon reached the next outpost using his mental map.
"Upper A7...got it."
Pushing through the blizzard, Lin Yu spotted a small but sturdy wooden hut.
The unlocked door resisted before slamming open under his push.
Inside was simple: a stove and a pot.
The stove held unburned charcoal; the pot was empty.
"I see...food and fuel must be gathered separately," Lin Yu mused.
The map noted most outposts had buried firewood and signs of mountain wildlife nearby - factors considered when establishing them.
Of course, one outpost's resources couldn't sustain someone for seven days.
But Lin Yu wasn't planning to settle here for Day One.
Though the darkening sky and the man's warning about time weighed on him, Lin Yu intended to keep searching.
Seven days to find twelve Players.
That meant finding at least one per day!

chapters.title: Chapter 78: Encountering Another Player
chapters.content:
"Running fast is one thing, but damn it's freezing!"
Trudging through increasingly thick snow, Lin Yu could feel his body temperature steadily dropping.
He had already checked three outposts near the initial abandoned base but found no traces of anyone having been there.
According to Lin Yu's reasoning, other players should have started the game under similar circumstances.
Therefore, they would likely prioritize finding shelter to make fire first.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
Searching for people in this vast snowy mountain was like looking for a needle in a haystack, but judging from the current situation...
Systematically checking each outpost might actually improve efficiency!
Although there were nearly a hundred outposts, this approach was still better than scouring the entire mountain range.
Yet after three consecutive failures, Lin Yu began developing an unfavorable suspicion.
"Could it be that the thirteen players in this dungeon were initially placed far apart from each other?"Lin Yu pulled out the map again.
Though already quite familiar with it, he couldn't help but double-check.
If he treated his starting point "B6" as the center of a fan-shaped area and divided the entire map equally...
Lin Yu quickly noticed something peculiar.
Exactly twelve "outposts" could form an approximate perfect circle.
These twelve outposts evenly divided the circle into twelve 30-degree sectors, each located precisely at the sector's midpoint!
Including the center point, that made exactly thirteen locations!
Most importantly...
These twelve sectors perfectly distributed all remaining outposts.
Each sector contained exactly eight outposts - no more, no less.
Ninety-six outposts total, plus the center point made ninety-seven.
If assuming each player started at an "abandoned" outpost, the remaining seven would correspond exactly to the "seven days" option!
Lin Yu exhaled sharply.
"Coincidence?"
Probably not.
The game providing a "map" as initial hint was likely intentional design to lead players to this discovery.
Lin Yu felt he was gradually piecing together something significant.
But regardless...
"Let's check the nearest sector first."
Having been ascending continuously, Lin Yu had reached the edge of the next sector.
Quickening his pace, he approached the central outpost of this area.
Before reaching it, however, Lin Yu spotted a figure vigorously sweeping snow with their feet searching for firewood at the outpost nearest to this "central" location.
Approaching closer, he saw it was a slightly plump middle-aged woman wearing a colorful padded jacket and permed hair.
"Hello there."
Lin Yu walked up and greeted her.
Startled by his voice, the woman turned to look at him.
"Oh heavens! You scared me half to death! Why you creeping up so quiet-like?"
Then realization dawned on her.
"You're a player?"
"Yes, I'm a player. My forum ID is 'A-Long', class is 'Soldier'. And you are...?"
The auntie sized Lin Yu up skeptically.
"Soldier? You look too clean-cut for that! Don't seem the type!"
Lin Yu smiled.
"Born this way. Plus I was in clerical work in the army, but the game still classified me as 'Soldier'."
His warm, friendly smile and tone made his lie instantly believable to the rosy-cheeked woman.
"Ohhh, so you really are military! Such handsome eyes... must be from the cultural troupe, eh?"
The auntie studied Lin Yu with growing interest.
"You got a girlfriend? My daughter's about your age, quite pretty too, just graduated from our local polytechnic..."
Lin Yu hurriedly interrupted:
"Whoa there, auntie, let's pump the brakes! We're in the 'Death Game' here... save the matchmaking for later!"
He couldn't help feeling exasperated.
Ever since enrolling at Jiangcheng Media University, Lin Yu's good looks had made him prime target for neighborhood matchmaking aunties.
Though he always declined with "I'm just a sophomore, not thinking about that", their persistent "just try dating first" enthusiasm never waned.
Who'd have thought even the Death Game couldn't spare him this script.
And this auntie was more enthusiastic than all previous ones combined - probably due to his fake "military" identity!
At Lin Yu's reminder, the auntie finally snapped back to reality.
She smacked her forehead regretfully.
"Oh dear, you're just too handsome young man, got me all flustered forgetting where we are!"
"Being in the Death Game does make you rather unsuitable for my daughter!"
Lin Yu facepalmed internally.
"Auntie, that's not what I meant... I was suggesting we focus on the game first."
"What's your class?"
Finally refocusing, the woman replied:
"Ah yes, my apologies young man..."
"My forum ID is 'Flourishing Flowers', cleared five dungeons already. Folks in my organization call me 'Sister Hua' - you can too."
"My class is 'Vendor'."
Lin Yu quickly recalled the Vendor class abilities.
Another common 'Information Type' class.
'Vendors' could obtain intel about 3-5 'non-exclusive items' existing within each dungeon.
Most Vendors made excellent support players since finding several dungeon items right from the start provided significant advantages.
Most obtainable items directly aided dungeon clearance - like Lin Yu's [One-Statement Lie Detector].
Naturally, Lin Yu asked:
"Sister Hua, mind sharing what items you've discovered?"
Hearing this, Sister Hua grew cautious.
"Oh now, A-Long... that's rather forward of you!"
Lin Yu maintained his pleasant smile:
"This dungeon clearly seems 'Survival' type - no player versus player elements..."
"Can't be sure," Sister Hua shook her head.
"Some NPC just told me it's better not to team up this run!"
"So those items probably can't be shared... we may not be enemies, but that doesn't mean we're allies either."
Lin Yu disagreed:
"Sister Hua, you're misunderstanding!"
"You're taking that NPC's words too literally!"

chapters.title: Chapter 79: The Strategy to Complete the Mission
chapters.content:
Hearing Lin Yu's words, Sister Hua looked puzzled.
"What do you mean by that?"
Lin Yu turned to Sister Hua and asked, "Sister Hua, did you get the 'map'?"
"No, what map are you talking about?" Sister Hua replied, clearly confused.
Lin Yu understood now.
Indeed, the map item given by that burly man wasn't something every player had received.
"I got a map from the initial NPC," Lin Yu said as he pulled out the map from his pocket. "It shows the number of 'strongholds'."
He showed the map to Sister Hua.
"There are almost 100 strongholds marked here... you see? So although the monsters restrict us from 'acting together', the abundant supplies mean there's no absolute competition between us."ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
Lin Yu spoke seriously."I know you might think items should be kept for personal use first... but since you haven't retrieved any yet, those items must be difficult to obtain, right?"
"As a Soldier with enhanced physical abilities, if you trust me, why not share information about one or two items! If I get the chance, I'll retrieve them for you!"
His sincere attitude and reasoning moved the naturally warm-hearted Sister Hua.
"Young man, you make a good point—alright, I'll tell you about one that should be most useful to you."
Sister Hua pointed directly north.
"About three kilometers that way, there's an item called [Black Oil Torch] buried under a rock. That thing never goes out no matter what and provides constant warmth and light."
"With that item, it seems you won't be targeted by monsters even when active outside at night."
Once Sister Hua made her decision, she became much more forthcoming.
She shared detailed information about one item with Lin Yu.
Lin Yu nodded understandingly.
"Got it. If I obtain it, I'll come back to help gather some supplies as repayment."
He smiled as he spoke.
Then, Lin Yu waved goodbye to Sister Hua.
"Well then, Sister Hua—since the NPC already emphasized this point, we shouldn't stay together too long!"
As Lin Yu said this, Sister Hua nodded.
"Alright, A-Long, be careful on your way!"
Sister Hua waved back.
Then, Lin Yu walked into the snowstorm.
With the fivefold physical enhancement from being a 'Soldier', plus the lingering effects of deceiving the burly man, Lin Yu's movement speed had increased further.
His vastly improved stamina and endurance left him feeling no fatigue.
Even in the mountainous blizzard, Lin Yu moved as effortlessly as "walking on flat ground".
Having successfully found Sister Hua earlier, Lin Yu also believed his analysis of the map was correct!
So without delay, he headed straight for the next "sector area".
After searching two strongholds around the "central point"...
Lin Yu wasn't surprised to find a young man sweeping snow with a large broom.
Seeing a figure approaching rapidly through the snowstorm, the young man assumed the same defensive posture as Sister Hua.
"Whoa! Who's there?!"
Looking at the slightly pudgy man dressed like the Michelin tire mascot in a white down jacket, Lin Yu cleared his throat.
"Player—I'm a player!"
Even after Lin Yu identified himself as a player, the man in white remained wary.
"A player? Are you here to steal my firewood?"
"Not at all, brother. Why would I steal your firewood?" Lin Yu said with a smile. "I'm just looking for 'strongholds'—my forum ID is 'ForeverLoveAi', and my class is 'Otaku'."
"What threat could an 'Otaku' possibly pose? Besides, since I'm an 'Otaku', doesn't that prove how harmless I am?"
Hearing this, the man in white visibly relaxed.
"Ohhh, so you're an 'Otaku'," he nodded. "You scared me... seeing you run so fast through the snow, I thought you were a monster... My ID is 'Dolphin', class is 'Student', cleared six dungeons—how many have you done, ForeverLoveAi?"
Casually, Lin Yu replied,
"One less than you, Dolphin. This is my fifth dungeon."
"By the way, Dolphin, where'd you get that broom?"
Lin Yu asked enthusiastically.
Dolphin scratched his head, "I asked the NPC for it at the start. Makes it easier to find things buried under snow. He also gave me some food and water, and pointed out a few stronghold locations."
"Since I'm a 'Student', I got all these after using my ability."
Lin Yu acted surprised, "Dolphin, you're so decisive! Using your ability right away and getting so much—this is the first time I've seen someone use the 'Student' ability so effectively!"
"You're definitely set for this dungeon."
Flattered by Lin Yu's praise, Dolphin looked embarrassed.
"Ah, it's nothing really. I was just worried the NPC might leave and I'd never get to use the ability..."
As he spoke, he couldn't help but feel pleased with himself.
"Actually, you 'Otaku' types should do fine too," Dolphin said kindly to Lin Yu. "Pure survival dungeons like this suit 'Otakus' well... If you're looking for strongholds, I suggest heading east."
"The NPC pointed out a few strongholds that way—there should be two more. Go check them out!"
Then Dolphin sighed regretfully.
"Too bad the monsters in this dungeon seem to target 'groups'. Otherwise I'd really team up with you."
Hearing this, Lin Yu agreed,
"Yeah, Dolphin, what a shame!"
"I shouldn't linger. Neither of us has any combat ability—if we encounter monsters, we're done for."
Speaking sincerely, Lin Yu turned and walked back into the snowstorm.
Feeling the "belief" flowing in and his deception becoming 'real', Lin Yu exhaled.
"Hah, as expected. This 'Promotion Mission' is practically an advanced tutorial for the 'Fraudster' class."
Now Lin Yu recognized another strength of his Unique Class 'Fraudster'.
Because...
right now, he simultaneously possessed abilities from both the 'Soldier' and 'Otaku' classes.
Just by stopping movement, his stamina would rapidly recover.
Two completely "contradictory" lies could coexist as long as neither was exposed!
This was precisely Lin Yu's strategy to complete his first Promotion Mission.
He simply needed to claim different "identities" to each person!
If successful, this wouldn't just mean completing the Promotion Mission...
He could potentially gain twelve different identity classes in this game!

chapters.title: Chapter 80: The Torch and Unexpected Findings
chapters.content:
The blizzard continued, and the sky grew increasingly darker.
It was only a matter of time before night fully fell.
Yet Lin Yu, who hadn't found a base or begun gathering firewood, remained calm.
After bidding farewell to Sister Hua earlier, he had headed north...
This meant he was now closer to the "item" Sister Hua had mentioned.
Of course...
Most importantly, Lin Yu currently had the 'Soldier' class enhancement and held a map in hand. Even if he needed to find a base and gather firewood now, time was still ample.
But Lin Yu didn't want to waste the night.
Precisely because 'Chate' and the snow monsters appeared at night, he didn't want to delay.
His "Promotion Task" conditions explicitly stated that he must tell different lies to "every player participating in each game."But what if a player died beforehand?
Lin Yu suspected that given the difficulty of the Promotion Task, failure would likely be declared in such cases.
Thus...
Hidden within his first Promotion Task was a critical challenge.
He had to race against time to meet everyone and successfully lie before any deaths occurred!
Though the information Sister Hua obtained about the [Black Oil Torch] was vague, Lin Yu could roughly guess its location by cross-referencing the map.
On the map, several kilometers due north of the base Sister Hua mentioned—which was northwest of Dolphin's previous location—
Lay a red-marked zone with high snow monster activity.
Without a map, Sister Hua would indeed have struggled to retrieve this item.
Fortunately, Lin Yu was now a Soldier and also possessed the [Guaranteed-Hit Revolver].
Though it had only one bullet, Lin Yu believed it would suffice.
Since the monster named 'Chate' was explicitly described as invincible,
It implied that ordinary "snow monsters" under Chate's rule could likely be killed.
With the Soldier's physical prowess and the revolver, taking one down shouldn't be an issue.
Still...
It'd be best to avoid encountering them altogether!
With this thought, Lin Yu quickened his pace, breaking into a full sprint across the snow.
Soon...
Lin Yu realized he had entered the "red zone."
On the ground, beneath the fresh layers of snow swept up by the blizzard, appeared a trail of heavy footprints—compacted snow turned to ice.
The prints were three to four times larger than a human's, with distinct edges and only three toes.
These clearly didn't belong to any "human."
They undoubtedly belonged to...
A snow monster.
Lin Yu exhaled sharply.
"Just looking at these footprints tells me this thing won't be easy to deal with," he muttered.
Any primate or primate-like creature larger and stronger than humans was inherently dangerous.
As the sky darkened further, the howling wind took on a mournful tone.
Lin Yu observed the direction of the footprints, then deliberately chose a perpendicular path.
"Hope I find that 'rock' soon."
He stepped over the prints, maintaining speed but lightening his footsteps.
Though unsure if snow monsters tracked by sound, caution never hurt.
Just as visibility began deteriorating noticeably, making Lin Yu consider abandoning the search—
A dark, protruding silhouette emerged faintly through the distant snowfall.
Its shape was unusually regular, resembling a boulder.
Despite traversing mountainous terrain, the Extreme Winter Mountain had been relatively flat, likely due to wind and snow erosion, with no prominent rocks—
Except for this sudden, massive outcrop.
"This must be it!"
Lin Yu hurried forward, reaching the boulder's side.
The rock appeared diagonally embedded in the ground, leaving an area beneath it with noticeably thinner snow cover.
Lin Yu stepped beneath it, shuffling his feet until he felt something solid.
Kneeling, he brushed away the snow and soon uncovered a torch forged from black metal.
The torch head was exquisitely crafted—far more intricate than Lin Yu expected—a hollow cylinder adorned with flame-like engravings.
Upon touching it, a prompt appeared:
[Black Oil Torch: A torch capable of burning in any environment, providing constant warmth and light. Effective at repelling fire-fearing monsters.]
[Note: Particularly effective against "snow monsters" in this game.]
Sister Hua had been truthful—the description matched her account almost verbatim.
Lin Yu bent to pick up the torch but found it stuck.
Recalling the sensation underfoot, he frowned and cleared more snow.
"Tch... figures."
The torch was clutched in a frozen hand.
The fingers had fused with the torch's base, making it impossible to lift directly.
Fortunately, as a Soldier, Lin Yu had strength to spare.
With a sharp tug, a crisp snapping sound followed.
*Crack!*
Several fingers broke off, which Lin Yu then peeled from the torch's base.
The pitch-black metal torch felt icy and smooth, almost painfully cold to hold.
Lin Yu scraped it against the rock, grinding away the remaining frozen skin fragments.
Next, he examined how to ignite it.
"Don't tell me I need my own fire starter..."
If so, that'd be rotten luck.
However, given the description mentioned "burns in any condition," the ignition method probably wasn't primitive.
Sure enough, Lin Yu soon discovered a thin seam at the torch's base.
It was nearly invisible, save for a few ice crystals lodged inside.
After brief inspection, he understood.
"Ah!"
Rotating the black cylinder below the seam produced a faint *pop* from within the torch!
A white flash flickered through the hollow torch head, followed by...
Pale flames erupting silently from the top, casting a soft, cool glow that illuminated the surrounding blizzard.
The torch grew warm, radiating comforting heat into Lin Yu's hands.
Lin Yu was pleasantly surprised.
"What a gem! Really owe Sister Hua for this one!"
Then he glanced at the severed fingers.
"And thank you too, brother... though with such a handy torch, how'd you end up dead here?"
Curious to investigate the "cause of death" for his own safety, Lin Yu crouched with the torch and cleared the snow shrouding the corpse.
As the snow fell away, his expression sobered.
The cause of death remained unclear—no visible wounds, just a frostbitten, pallid face frozen in terror.
And this face... Lin Yu recognized it.ᴛhis ᴜpdated by
It was the burly man he'd met earlier.
Even the clothing matched exactly!
"Well, ain't this a fucking unexpected bonus," Lin Yu murmured, staring at the corpse.

chapters.title: Chapter 81: The Third Profession, Teacher!
chapters.content:
The "corpse" before him appeared frozen solid, clearly dead for some time.
Considering the fact that the 'Vendor' information was obtained right at the game's start, there was no doubt this corpse had died before Lin Yu ever met that burly man.
This realization sparked new thoughts in Lin Yu's mind.
"So what exactly was that NPC I encountered earlier?"
A chilling sense of retrospective fear crept over him.
Simultaneously, he developed deep suspicions about whether that NPC had been benevolent at all.
That thing might not even have been human. Even if most of its information was helpful, it could have mixed in one or two deadly lies.
Connecting these dots, even the second "Promotion" task now seemed like a hint.
"The 'Fraudster' might not be a player at all... but rather 'something' within this game itself..."
Lin Yu massaged his temples in frustration.The fear quickly dissipated, replaced by a sense of helplessness.
"'Competition', 'Puzzle', 'Survival'... I've encountered three of the four dungeon types now, and in every single one I'm locked in mental combat with the game itself! Even the rules require verification!"
Without the forum it might be different, but Lin Yu had seen the guides there.
He knew most players encountered NPCs or in-game rules that rarely contained deception.
'Puzzle' dungeons might have slightly more misleading elements, but not every single time.
Yet in his case...
"Apparently everything except the initial game introduction requires suspicion," Lin Yu sighed.
But he quickly adjusted his mindset.
Regardless of what mysteries this dungeon held...
Whether he'd initially encountered a disguised monster, wandering spirit, doppelganger or clone...
His immediate plan remained unchanged.
Overanalyzing wouldn't help now.
Raising his torch, Lin Yu turned and disappeared into the snowstorm, leaving the frozen corpse behind.
The night was long - no time to waste.
"Just wait until I collect all twelve professions... whether you're Chate or Buffett..." Lin Yu muttered as he trudged forward through the darkness.
Though visibility decreased in the snowstorm, Lin Yu wouldn't get lost.
Years of theater performance had given him precise spatial awareness, and the map showed safe houses weren't too far apart...
He could constantly adjust his direction based on distance traveled and whether he encountered shelters.
At least based on what he'd seen so far, that mysterious burly NPC's map appeared untampered with.
Soon, Lin Yu reached another "sector."Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
But this time...
He found no signs of human activity near the sector's central safe house.
Instead, right at the sector's edge, he spotted a wooden cabin with lit windows.
Torch in hand, Lin Yu quickly approached the door.
"Knock knock!"
He rapped on the door.
A muscular man soon cracked the door open slightly.
"Who's there?"
Through the gap, Lin Yu saw the man gripping an iron rod while eyeing him warily.
Seeing the man's caution, Lin Yu quickly reassured him.
"Relax, I'm a player - a player!"
"And why should that make me relax?" the man said coldly. "Didn't you get the NPC warning? Wandering at night and partnering up are dangerous!"
The dark eyes behind the door remained vigilant.
"I got it - don't worry, I just have some information to share!"
"Regardless of your profession, I'm a 'Teacher' - in real life I teach English too!"
"What possible harm could a 'Teacher' profession do?"
"I've obtained crucial information that benefits all players - information you really should know!"
Lin Yu spoke calmly.
But given the late hour, the man remained skeptical.
"'Teacher'?"
"Yes, 'Teacher' - my forum ID is 'Old Xu,' you can call me Xiao Xu!"
The man scrutinized Lin Yu.
"You look too young, and your demeanor doesn't match!"
Lin Yu hastily explained: "I'm not a regular schoolteacher - I work at a tutoring center specializing in spoken English!"
"Lord, what fools these mortals be!"
He quoted a famous line from Shakespeare's "A Midsummer Night's Dream."
It was an extremely classic quote, one Lin Yu had recently reviewed before entering this dungeon.
Delivered with perfect pronunciation and emotional cadence, it instantly convinced the man.
"Excellent Cockney accent... and that was from William Shakespeare's 'A Midsummer Night's Dream,' right? Your tutoring center must have high standards."
As he spoke, the door opened wider, revealing the slender face of a man in his early thirties.
He wore professional snow goggles and an expensive down jacket from a premium brand.
Lin Yu had glimpsed these details earlier and deliberately played the English teacher angle.
The clearly affluent man continued:
"Xiao Xu, right? You can call me 'Karen.' I'm with the 'Player Mutual Aid Association,' profession 'Lawyer.'"
"What information did you want to share?"
Lin Yu smiled.
Now that the 'Teacher' profession was confirmed, game information appeared in his mind:
"'Chate' is not 'alive.' Being alone only reduces chances of 'Chate' detection."
Though shocked internally, Lin Yu showed no reaction.
He addressed Karen:
"Brother Karen, did you encounter a scruffy-bearded NPC at the start claiming to be 'treasure hunting'?"
Karen nodded slightly.
"Yes... what about it?"
He looked puzzled.
From Karen's response, Lin Yu confirmed something:
They'd all likely encountered the same NPC.
So Lin Yu explained:
"That's the thing, Brother Karen - we all met similar NPCs, and their initial information contained falsehoods!"

chapters.title: Chapter 82: The Fourth Profession, Ruffian!
chapters.content:
Lin Yu had no intention of telling Karen the real information he obtained through the 'Teacher' profession.
The reason was simple.
The information obtained from 'Teacher' wasn't substantial enough to "justify" his behavior of braving the snowstorm with a torch in the middle of the night to deliver warnings.
Especially since the man before him carried himself with the arrogant demeanor of a seasoned social operator, indicating he wasn't stupid.
Moreover, such people were often self-serving and conceited...
So to maintain Karen's "belief," Lin Yu had to provide a "reason" that Karen would accept.
Of course, Lin Yu didn't consider himself to be lying either.
Since even that burly man might not be human, his initial words couldn't be fully trusted!
As expected, upon hearing Lin Yu's words,
Karen frowned slightly."So there were false hints in the initial NPC's prompts..."
Then, Karen looked at Lin Yu.
"This information is crucial—if you encounter difficulties during the game, I'll help you too."
Karen said solemnly.
Lin Yu smiled.
"Thanks, Brother Karen!"
He said, then took a step back.
"Brother Karen—since that's the case, I'll take my leave first."
"It's nighttime now. Staying too long might attract that monster."
After Lin Yu finished speaking, Karen slammed the door shut with a "bang."
Lin Yu turned around, his expression turning cold.
"Phew..."
"Got another 'profession'."
Although this 'Teacher' profession wasn't like the previous 'Soldier' or 'Otaku,' which provided continuous movement assistance,
the information obtained from 'Teacher' was equally critical!
In this mystery-laden "Extreme Winter Mountain," the 'Teacher's' information sent another chill down Lin Yu's spine.
'Chate' wasn't alive.
Being alone only reduced the probability of being discovered by 'Chate.'
These two pieces of information, while enlightening, also made Lin Yu's scalp tingle.
'Chate' wasn't alive?
Once something was inherently "dead," the sense of security Lin Yu derived from the Soldier's physique and his pistol diminished greatly.
Combined with that burly man who might have been a corpse from the start... it was hard to say whether 'Chate' even had a physical form!
The second hint from 'Teacher' troubled Lin Yu even more.
"'Reduces probability' rather than 'prevents'...?"
This meant that even when alone, there was still a chance of being found by 'Chate'!
Lin Yu realized...
He had to hurry now.
What if someone fell victim to 'Chate' tonight?
With this thought, Lin Yu quickened his pace again.
Soon...ᴛhis ᴜpdated by ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
Lin Yu arrived in front of the next cabin.
Seeing light through the window,
Lin Yu spat, put on a menacing expression, wiped the snow off his face, and pushed open the cabin door.
Inside, a slightly plump woman eating roasted potatoes by the fireplace stood up.
"W-what do you want?"
Like everyone else before her, the woman spoke nervously.
But this time, Lin Yu didn't choose to appease or reassure her.
Instead, he spat again, adopting a thuggish demeanor.
"Damn luck! Finally found a hideout, and it's already taken!"
He glared at her with undisguised hostility.
"Hey, you! Give me some food!"
The plump woman looked at Lin Yu, then pulled out a brick and raised it.
"I warn you, don't try anything—don't force me to fight you to the death!"
Her voice trembled as she spoke.
Lin Yu watched her with amused cruelty.
"Oh? What's your profession? Think you can fight me to the death?"
"My profession is 'Soldier'..."
The woman stammered.
Lin Yu burst into exaggerated, grating laughter.
"Soldier? Hahahaha! You expect me to believe that?"
The woman bit her lip, both angry and afraid.
"Fine—my profession is 'Otaku,' but this brick is real! Don't push me!"
"And I've already cleared seven dungeons—this isn't my only item... You better watch out!"
Lin Yu nodded slightly.
The 'Otaku' and 'Otaku (female)' professions were essentially the same.
The only difference was that male 'Otaku' recovered stamina and injuries slower but had reduced consumption when stationary.
In other words, while female 'Otaku' recovered faster, they still needed to gather food and water like ordinary people.
The pile of roasted potatoes by the fireplace was proof—this woman had likely spent most of her time scavenging for food!
Lin Yu coldly retorted,
"Fight to the death? You think I'm scared?"
"Ask around the forum—when has 'Sixth Master' ever backed down?"
"You, a mere 'Otaku,' dare challenge me, a 'Ruffian'?"
"I'll bash your head in with this torch—have you ever even fought? Do you even know how to use that brick?"
Lin Yu waved the torch menacingly.
The woman paled and stepped back, her bravado fading.
"You... you..."
She stammered incoherently.
Lin Yu spat on the ground.
"Enough whining. I'm not here to take your cabin or kill you."
"I just want some of those damn potatoes. What's the big deal?"
Hearing Lin Yu relent, the woman was momentarily stunned.
Then, hesitantly, she asked,
"R-really? You're not here to take my cabin or... kill me?"
"Psycho. What good would killing you do?" Lin Yu sighed.
"I'm a 'Ruffian,' not a maniac... Goddamn it!"
After emphasizing his profession again, Lin Yu sensed her belief solidify.
Soon, he felt the 'Ruffian' ability unlock.
The fourth profession—acquired!
Lin Yu exhaled and held out his hand.
"Food. Now."
"Give me some, and I'll leave immediately."
The woman snapped out of her daze and hastily tossed two potatoes at him from a distance.
She asked uncertainly,
"You'll really leave? But it's dark outside... won't you encounter monsters?"
"Two people together attract monsters more easily," Lin Yu snapped.
"And you idiot, I already told you I'm a 'Ruffian'—I straight-up ignored the rule about increased danger at night!"

chapters.title: Chapter 83: The Great Detective Furbollo
chapters.content:
After bidding farewell to the plump woman, Lin Yu munched on his potato while hurrying to the next location.
"Got a 'Rule Exemption'... but I'm not even clear what rules exist in this game yet, so I'll save it for now," Lin Yu muttered to himself before arriving at two more bases in quick succession.
*Knock knock.*
"Hello, I'm a player. You can call me 'Summer.' My profession is 'Veterinarian'—I wanted to use my ability to see if I could communicate with those 'snow monsters.'"
...
"Hey, bro, my ID is 'Old Yao,' and my profession is 'Thief'... Hey, man, relax, I'm not here to steal anything. I'm just looking around for food. I spent the whole day gathering firewood and I'm starving."
...
The next two players Lin Yu encountered had the IDs 'Flying Cloud' (profession: 'Reporter') and 'Level 8 Hurricane' (profession: 'Programmer'). Neither had much combat capability.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
The 'Reporter' ability was 'Enhancement Type,' specifically boosting movement speed—and this speed increased further when moving toward humans.
Meanwhile, the 'Programmer' was 'Skill Type.' Activating the skill granted a temporary surge in stamina and mental energy, eliminating the need for food or sleep while drastically enhancing cognitive speed—though prolonged use resulted in severe exhaustion afterward.Lin Yu briefly chatted with them using different tones and expressions, then left after obtaining the 'Veterinarian' and 'Thief' professions.
"Whew... That's all six fake identities based on the first instance used up," Lin Yu rubbed his temples as he walked. "For the second instance... 'Craftsman' and 'Student' aren't very useful, but 'Doctor' might be worth taking in case I get injured or something."
Surprisingly, all six professions from the first instance turned out to be quite useful in this one.
But... should he imitate 'April' when playing the doctor?
That woman had mostly interacted with her boyfriend in the last instance, so Lin Yu wasn't sure how to portray her solo demeanor.
"Guess I'll just improvise this role."
Lin Yu slowed his pace slightly.
By now, the blizzard had weakened, and the night had deepened into the late hours.
Lin Yu soon found the seventh base!
Faint firelight seeped through the window of the seventh base.
He knocked lightly on the door.
Soon, a lazy voice responded from inside.
"Coming!"
Lin Yu steadied his nerves, exhaled, and prepared to roleplay as a medical student when—
The door opened, revealing the face of a young man.
The man wore a knitted sweater, cotton pants, and a fluffy red beanie. He had a slender build, a high nose bridge, deep-set eyes, and strikingly sharp features.
"Ethnic minority? Mixed race?"
Lin Yu thought to himself, but before he could speak, the beanie-clad man impatiently cut in.
"Yo, whatcha knockin' at this hour? Ain't ya got no sleep to catch? Damn it!"
The thick Henan dialect short-circuited Lin Yu’s brain for three full seconds.
After a long pause, he finally managed to recite his prepared lines.
"Uh, hello, my forum ID is 'May,' and my profession is—"
Before Lin Yu could finish, the man interrupted him.
"Hold up, bro," the previously drowsy man raised a hand, his eyes suddenly sharp as lightning. "Don’t tell me yet—lemme guess as a 'Detective'!"
Lin Yu blinked in surprise.
"Your profession is 'Detective'?"
A 'Detective’s' ability wasn’t about uncovering secrets from someone’s mind.
Though it was still 'Skill Type,' the actual function was to provide players with a 'clue' related to their current question.
"Damn right," the beanie man declared proudly. "I’m the most famous rookie 'Detective' player on the forums—ID 'Furbollo'—undefeated through sixteen instances, destined to become the greatest 'Detective' player ever!"
"If you’d lost even once in those sixteen instances, I wouldn’t be seeing you now," Lin Yu sighed.
Still, the name 'Furbollo' did ring a bell—probably an active forum user.
Ignoring Lin Yu’s remark, 'Furbollo' pushed up his imaginary glasses and spoke in a low voice.
"Judging by your refined looks but cheap clothes, you’re probably not well-off... Running around alone in the snow at night without fear suggests you’re used to staying up late..."
"I’ve got it—your profession is 'Security Guard'!"
"In real life, you must work security at some high-end place, right?"
Furbollo delivered his analysis with full Henan accent conviction.
Lin Yu exhaled deeply.
"What nonsense... That’s completely wrong."
"Are you even a real detective? You’re just some guy who read too many detective novels, aren’t you?"
Furbollo’s face twisted in offense.
"Moron, what I do in real life don’t matter! My in-game profession really is 'Detective'!"
Lin Yu nodded.
"I believe you’re a 'Detective,' but I’m definitely not a 'Security Guard.'"
"My profession is 'Doctor'!"
He said firmly. Furbollo’s eyes lit up in realization.
"See? I was right! Doctors work night shifts, so you’re active at night!"
As Furbollo spoke, 'Trust' immediately manifested, and Lin Yu gained the 'Doctor' profession.
To which Lin Yu could only reply—
"Yeah, yeah, sure."
At first, hearing the man was a 'Detective,' Lin Yu had braced himself for the most troublesome, hardest-to-fool opponent yet.
He’d almost given up on playing 'Doctor' and considered switching to 'Actor' instead!
After all, if categorized by conventional standards, Lin Yu would most likely be an 'Actor.'
He knew far more about 'acting' than 'medicine.'
If this 'Detective' suddenly asked, "Pop quiz—how do you treat trigeminal neuralgia?" Lin Yu would’ve been sweating bullets on the spot.
But... this 'Detective' turned out to be the most naive and trusting of all seven players he’d met so far.
Apparently, profession awakening really was tied only to life experience, not personal capability.
"Anyway, Doc, why you runnin’ around in the middle of the night?"
"Oh, well—I’ve got this torch, so monsters won’t notice me at night," Lin Yu said casually. "Figured I’d check on people in case anyone got hurt on the first day."
"Respect, bro! A true healer’s heart!"
Furbollo nodded solemnly, utterly impressed.

chapters.title: Chapter 84: Twelve Professions! The Cabin at the Center Point!
chapters.content:
After bidding farewell to Furbollo, Lin Yu continued forward as dawn broke and the snowstorm weakened considerably. Having gained experience throughout the night, Lin Yu's progress became increasingly smooth.
He quickly located the remaining five people at various outposts and successfully negotiated with them. The five additional professions he obtained were:
Enhancement Type 'Postman': The ability to maintain rapid movement regardless of terrain or environmental conditions.
Enhancement Type 'Enforcer': Improved reaction speed and combat technique bonuses.
Information Type 'Chef': Reveals locations and edible preparation methods for ingredients within the dungeon.
Skill Type 'Corporate Drone': Upon activation, enters a calm state that forcibly eliminates all negative emotions.
Rule Type 'Official': Can interpret and supplement a single "rule," altering its effective scope and implementation method.Follow current novels on N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
None of the five people Lin Yu encountered questioned him too severely. Now possessing a full twelve 'Professions,' Lin Yu felt his survival pressure significantly reduced as he bid farewell to the last individual while holding his torch.
With the 'Postman' ability, Lin Yu could run more than twice as fast as before. Combined with the 'Chef' ability, he could directly spot edible items buried beneath the snow. The potatoes buried below... were actually already "cooked" and ready to eat!
There weren't just potatoes but also tomatoes, corn... and even extremely rare finds like biscuits and chocolate. However, while all these foods were ready-to-eat, Lin Yu noticed something peculiar about this dungeon through the 'Chef's ingredient prompts - all these foods were "alive."To confirm, he observed carefully - whether vegetables or biscuits buried in snow, they all moved slowly, crawling beneath the snow's surface. This suddenly reminded Lin Yu of the initial hint from the map: "Near outposts are signs of wood and biological activity that will provide fuel and food."
Originally, Lin Yu thought this might be some "mislabeling" on the map. Now it appeared... even processed foods like these were actually living creatures! Of course, Lin Yu no longer found this particularly frightening - he'd grown immune to such things.
"At any rate, the first task is mostly complete." Now he just needed to avoid being exposed. Lin Yu didn't anticipate much difficulty here either. When impersonating each different 'Profession' during his deceptions, he had crafted distinct personas and demeanors tailored to each role!
This wasn't just to enhance persuasiveness and make them quickly believe his professional claims. Information exchange between people relying solely on language is inefficient and vague. Even if two people met and discussed the player they encountered last night, they likely wouldn't realize they were talking about the same person.
"A very friendly otaku" and "a teacher with excellent English" wouldn't be connected in their minds. The only common points would be generic traits like being somewhat handsome or not short. Lin Yu would absolutely avoid appearing before two people simultaneously - though given the game's inherent mechanics, this was already something to avoid anyway.
Unless some situation forced everyone to gather together, Lin Yu couldn't imagine how he might be exposed! With these thoughts, Lin Yu returned to his starting point and pulled out the map again. "Next, I should focus on completing the second promotion task."
This second promotion task... undoubtedly connected to all the "suspicious aspects" of this game itself. The unnaturally symmetrical distribution of "outposts" and the perfectly divisible map. NPCs who had "died" long ago yet all seemed identical. Similarly "dead" monsters named 'Chate.' And now, living food.
While other players didn't seem to have noticed yet, treating this as just a 'Survival' dungeon requiring only endurance against cold and caution against "snow monsters," Lin Yu knew better. This dungeon was profoundly abnormal. Though classified as 'Survival,' it seemed to conceal some "bizarre" underlying rules.
"Anyway..." "I should check the center point first." Lin Yu exhaled and looked at the map's "central point," where there happened to be an "outpost." Like the central star point on a Go board, it was impossible to ignore. Though extreme danger might lurk there.
Now bolstered by twelve professions, Lin Yu didn't feel particularly afraid! Moreover, it was daytime with reduced snowfall. Before the second night arrived, Lin Yu wanted to investigate quickly. Such places were best visited early when fully prepared!
After all, knowing something was wrong yet leaving it alone would make sleep impossible. He'd already stayed up all night traveling through snowstorms. Without the 'Otaku's stamina recovery and 'Soldier's enhanced physique, Lin Yu felt he should have collapsed by now.
"Ha—" Lin Yu yawned. "The sooner I uncover the truth, the sooner I can rest..." he muttered, trudging through snow toward the central point.
Comparing the map's terrain markings with other outposts, Lin Yu soon approached the central area. As he neared the center, snow accumulation grew deeper, nearly reaching his waist. Without the 'Postman' ability, he'd be completely immobilized now! But combining 'Postman' with 'Soldier' abilities, plus the ongoing deception effects on NPCs, allowed Lin Yu to maintain decent speed even in heavy snow.
Soon— Lin Yu spotted a small cabin almost completely buried in snow. "Huh..." He exhaled, squinting his eyes. "Definitely different."
After seeing about twenty outposts yesterday, Lin Yu had noticed they all looked basically identical - simple, aged, even somewhat dilapidated wooden cabins containing only basic stoves as furnishings. But this snow-buried cabin, while similarly small with wooden exterior, had some broken planks revealing what lay beneath - some kind of black matte metal.
If the others resembled temporary "wooden shacks," this one... might qualify as a shelter!

chapters.title: Chapter 85: The Strange House, The Visiting Detective, and 'Chate'
chapters.content:
After clearing the snow at the entrance, Lin Yu pushed open the heavy wooden-clad metal door and entered the small house.
The furnishings inside were distinctly different from all previous "safe houses."
A workbench-style desk and chair, a spacious single bed with bedding, a single wardrobe, wall-mounted bookshelves...
There was even a dedicated wine cabinet and a cooking range with pots, on which many metal cans were placed.
Though most furniture was covered in dust, it was clear...
Someone had genuinely lived here.
Unlike those "temporary safe houses" that weren't meant for human habitation at all!
What proper house would just have a stove as its main feature.
From observing this house, Lin Yu could draw some conclusions.
"The person who lived here was probably a rather serious and disciplined intellectual," he muttered to himself.After all, the bed was neatly made, the desk and chairs arranged with meticulous precision—almost obsessive-compulsive.
Even the books on the shelves and the wine in the cabinet were arranged by height.
Moreover, though long unused, the metal handle on the wine cabinet door was relatively new, while the metal handle on the bookcase had been worn to a smooth shine.
It wasn't hard to deduce that drinking was an occasional indulgence for him, but reading was likely a nightly ritual.
And...
Upon approaching the bookshelf, one could see English titles on the spines.
The 'Death Game' was ultimately connected to reality...
At least the language was the same.
Though those English titles were rather puzzling when translated directly:
"The Principle of Happy Machinery," "The Particularly Good Angry Gear," "The Crazy Wrench," "The Stupid Tire"...
Opening the bookcase and pulling out those books revealed large sections blacked out.
Anywhere that seemed to originally contain "illustrations" had been completely obscured with black ink.
Lin Yu could only piece together from the remaining fragments and the book layouts...
These seemed to be some kind of academic works.
All these books pointed toward a "discipline" that Lin Yu couldn't yet comprehend.
This made Lin Yu ponder again.
"So, the owner of this room read these things every night?"
"And... these black bars are so neat and straight—it's highly likely the book's owner deliberately blacked them out."
"But why would he do that... Was this his way of destroying these books?"
Lin Yu exhaled.
But there were better ways to destroy a book—like burning it.
Lin Yu ran his fingers over the books' smooth page edges, thinking.
These books had clearly been frequently read, yet showed no missing pages or dog-eared corners.
This indicated...
The owner not only valued tidiness but likely cherished books deeply—a true bibliophile at heart.
An increasingly clear image formed in Lin Yu's mind: a young male scholar living alone in this snowy wilderness.
As for why male...
The wardrobe contained men's overcoats, all in muted colors—but with fitted styles, and trousers with stiff, straight cuts more suited for younger men.
Lin Yu then shelved all the books back in the case.
Next, he turned his attention to the workbench.
On the wooden surface, the table's edges bore traces of pencil dust.
Though the owner had clearly wiped it down, pencil residue lodged in the seams and grain wasn't easy to fully remove.
From the pencil marks being concentrated around the edges, Lin Yu inferred:
"Was this table used for drafting?"
If it were just for writing, pencils wouldn't be commonly used... let alone leave marks specifically around the edges.Thɪs ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
Lin Yu lightly tapped the tabletop, checking if this conspicuously sturdy desk concealed any hidden compartments.
Just then...
"Thud!"
The door was pushed open.
In the doorway stood a handsome young man with sharp features, wearing a red knit cap.
Seeing Lin Yu inside, he looked momentarily startled before recovering.
"Oh—you're that 'Doctor' I met earlier, May!"
The newcomer was none other than the 'Detective' Furbollo.
Rubbing his hands together excitedly, he looked at Lin Yu.
"Zhin didn't expect to meet you here... Seems you're quite sharp too, May!"
Furbollo marveled: "You also noticed something odd about this place and came, right..."
Lin Yu regarded Furbollo, swiftly switching back to the persona he'd used with this 'Detective' last night—the diligent night-shift doctor.
Clearing his throat, he said: "More like coincidence in my case..."
Lin Yu then asked:
"How did you realize there was something unusual here?"
"Because today I followed your example and explored around, then noticed these safe houses are too 'regular,'" Furbollo waved his hand. "Though they seem randomly placed, there's a clear pattern—I checked three spots, and each abandoned safe house had exactly seven others nearby!"
"If viewed from above, you'd see... all safe houses form a perfect circle!"
"And by my deduction... this current location is the circle's center!"
Lin Yu looked at Furbollo in surprise.
He was impressed by Furbollo's "spatial reasoning" ability.
Lin Yu pulled out the map.
"You've got some skills, Detective."
"I only noticed the anomaly because I got this map from an NPC."
As he spoke, Lin Yu showed the map to Furbollo.
The detective glanced at it and casually waved:
"No big deal, basic stuff—though not bad for a 'Doctor' to spot patterns on a map!"
Lin Yu nodded: "But with the map, I noticed something you missed—see how all safe houses not only form a perfect circle, but that circle can be evenly divided into twelve 30-degree sectors?"
Lin Yu said earnestly. Furbollo looked and nodded in surprise.
"True! That's an interesting find!"
Lin Yu exhaled, then said: "Though I'm a 'Doctor,' I'm no worse than you as a 'Detective.'"
"In fact, aren't 'Doctors' and 'Detectives' natural partners?"
Hearing this, Furbollo laughed: "With that logic, since 'Doctors' can heal anyone, they should be 'natural partners' with everybody."
Lin Yu smiled at his response.
"I see..."
Suddenly, Lin Yu produced the [One-Statement Lie Detector], saying: "I have this item—it functions as a lie detector."
With that, he tossed the detector at Furbollo.
"Clatter!"
It hit Furbollo before falling to the floor.
Furbollo instinctively dodged, then stared at the device in bewilderment.
"Huh? What was that for?"
"Checking if you have physical form."
Lin Yu already held another item in his hand.
As Furbollo looked down, Lin Yu aimed the [Guaranteed-Hit Revolver] at "Furbollo."
"Anyone named 'Furbollo' would definitely know the classic detective-doctor duo reference..."
"But I'm glad you have physical form, impostor."
"Or should I say..."
"'Chate.'"

chapters.title: Chapter 86: The Map's Omission and the Emerging Deception
chapters.content:
Initially, Lin Yu hadn't doubted Furbollo's identity at all.
After all, Lin Yu had easily discussed profession-related information about the Death Game with him.
Although this detective had completely misanalyzed Lin Yu's profession during their first meeting...
He was indeed a genuine Detective.
The Death Game would never assign professions randomly.
Moreover, the Detective profession's abilities naturally allowed one to quickly obtain "clues."
But...
The "explanation" Furbollo provided happened to be the least credible one possible.
Because there wasn't enough time.
No matter how talented a Detective was, reaching the conclusion that "each abandoned stronghold happens to have seven adjacent strongholds" would require visiting at least sixteen strongholds.Yet...
He couldn't have moved that fast!
Even so, Lin Yu might not have completely ruled out the possibility that this "Furbollo" had used some rapid movement or enhanced observation tool.
Therefore, Lin Yu chose to take out the map for further testing.
After traveling all night, Lin Yu had confirmed one thing...
This map had "omissions."
There were 13 players in this game.
But on this map... even including the central point, there were only 97 strongholds—plus 12 abandoned ones.
Yet throughout the night, Lin Yu had indeed encountered all twelve other players.
At first, after noticing all the strongholds could form a twelve-sectioned circle, Lin Yu suspected a player might be spawning at the central point.
But after actually traversing the area last night, Lin Yu confirmed...
When drawing this map, each sector's area had been slightly expanded.
After dividing it into twelve equal parts...
An entire sector had been concealed.
The hidden sector happened to be where Furbollo was located.
Lin Yu hadn't noticed when passing through—because Furbollo's area was almost identical in structure to the next sector!
When Lin Yu pointed his gun at him, Furbollo raised his hands in panic.
"I... I'm not Chate! I'm a Player!"
Seeing Furbollo's genuine terror, Lin Yu could tell.
This wasn't an act.
But... that didn't prove he was "real."
After all, the burly man they'd encountered earlier hadn't been acting either.
Both the burly man and this Furbollo were utterly convinced of their own identities.
Otherwise, Lin Yu's earlier deception against the burly man wouldn't have been believed and actualized.
So...
Lin Yu looked at Furbollo and didn't hesitate to fire his bullet.
A veteran player on the forum had once posted a guide noting that statistically, whether in Survival or Slaughter dungeons, the most fatal moment when encountering "monsters"...
Was always during the first encounter.
Thus, Lin Yu didn't rely on his Soldier-enhanced physique or Enforcer combat skills to engage directly.
He simply fired.
"Bang!"
After the gunshot.
"Furbollo" collapsed in shock, his dying expression still frozen in disbelief.
Even Lin Yu, who had been certain this was an imposter, now felt a twinge of doubt.
Had he actually killed the wrong person?
Well, even if he had... better him than me, right?
But two subsequent events confirmed Lin Yu's judgment had been correct.
First was Furbollo's "corpse" on the ground.
It rapidly "melted."
His entire body first faded to black, then softened in texture before becoming a viscous non-Newtonian fluid.
Soon, this black liquid seeped into the ground.
The entire process took mere seconds.
However, Lin Yu had been closely observing "Furbollo's corpse" and missed no detail.
The second confirmation was...
Lin Yu still retained his Doctor abilities.
"So the Furbollo I first met was real, this one was fake."
"While I can't confirm this was Chate in disguise... whatever it was, its disguise method involves creating replicas that 'mimic' behavior."
"And judging by Furbollo's reaction earlier, these replicas can't copy memories... probably only mimicking what they've already observed."
Lin Yu exhaled and pulled up a chair at the workbench.
"So the actual number of strongholds isn't 97, but 105..."
Pondering this, Lin Yu spread out the map on the workbench.
Beside it stood a pencil holder containing an unused pencil.
Lin Yu took it out and drew two dotted lines on the map, marking the "erased" thirteenth sector.
This sector should be due north on the map.
"If there's an unmarked sector here with the starting point at 'center,' Furbollo's stronghold was here last night, and I passed one..."
Lin Yu marked three points.
Then he froze.
Lin Yu suddenly realized all previous strongholds followed a naming convention of letters A to E combined with numbers 1-12.The source of this content ɪs ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
But—if Furbollo's current location was labeled A13...
Connecting A1 to A13 like a childhood dot-to-dot puzzle...
Formed a perfect arc.
Next was connecting B1 to B12—though missing two points initially, adding them in the omitted 13th sector would form...
A cursive lowercase "h."
The C connections... shaped like an "e."
The D section formed an "a."
The E section—a cursive "t."
Though these letters overlapped, if the initial arc was considered a "c"...
Arranging them from A to E spelled a word:
c, h, e, a, t—cheat.
Which in Chinese means...
Deception, fraud.
Lin Yu exhaled deeply.
"I see. Hiding this sector prevents people from connecting these letters."
With this word revealed on the map, everything clicked into place.
"That monster 'Chate' the burly man mentioned—perhaps its real name is also 'cheat.'"
"So if the map's strongholds are hinting that this is all a 'deception'... then my Fraudster's Promotion Task must involve whoever set up this scam."
Lin Yu murmured to himself.

chapters.title: Chapter 87: Rest
chapters.content:
"Although I still can't determine exactly who the 'Fraudster' refers to... at least the second 'Promotion Task' isn't completely without clues now." Sitting in the room while looking at the map in his hands, Lin Yu let out a long sigh.
Moreover, after shifting his focus away from the puzzle of the "Promotion Task"...
Lin Yu realized he now held considerable advantages regarding this mission. "At the very least, this should be the warmest cabin available—and I don't need to gather additional fuel or food supplies."
"Not to mention, this cabin likely contains other hidden 'clues' as well." Thinking this, Lin Yu couldn't help feeling some regret.
"I should've chosen 'Detective' as my profession from the start," Lin Yu muttered with a sigh.
Had he been a 'Detective,' he could've identified anomalies within this cabin. This thought suddenly sparked a realization.
"Wait a minute..."
Although that imposter "Furbollo" lacked any genuine 'Detective' abilities...
There was actually a real 'Detective' in this dungeon!
As this thought surfaced, Lin Yu began weighing the pros and cons.First, if he brought "Furbollo" here to utilize his 'Detective' skills for investigating the cabin...
They'd inevitably have to spend extended time together.
The man seemed decent, but appearances could be deceiving.
While Lin Yu had maintained a "friendly" facade toward all twelve players encountered so far, he understood one fundamental truth:
This dungeon wasn't designed for cooperation.
Though there were no explicit competitive mechanics or rewards for eliminating other players...
In extreme environments, having one less person to share "resources" with became its own reward!
He had to stay guarded.
Furthermore, even if "Furbollo" remained completely harmless toward him...
Simply letting Furbollo observe his actions required careful consideration of whether it was worth the risk.
After all, the more "Furbollo" learned about him, the higher the chances of arousing suspicion.
