And if subsequent puzzles involved this dungeon's truth—especially if it related to his "Promotion Task"—
Any possibility of revealing his potential "Fraudster" profession...
Was absolutely unacceptable to Lin Yu.
As for two people being more likely to attract 『Chate』... that hardly concerned Lin Yu anymore.
That barely qualified as an issue at this point!
Lost in thought, Lin Yu absently tapped the table.
"Tap. Tap. Tap."
After prolonged deliberation, Lin Yu suddenly chuckled.
"What an idiot... completely trapped by conventional thinking!"
Feeling mentally unshackled, he arrived at a simple solution:
"I could just eliminate him after using his abilities, couldn't I?"
This realization instantly lifted Lin Yu's mood.
This way, even if "Furbollo" harbored ill intentions, it wouldn't matter!
Of course, thoroughly searching the cabin himself remained an option.
But that would...
Consume an unpredictable amount of time!
For Lin Yu, this was utterly unacceptable.
Though seven days seemed ample...
With no idea what subsequent puzzles awaited him, Lin Yu couldn't afford to gamble on having "plenty of time."
Exhaling deeply, Lin Yu prepared for his next move.
After eating some food to replenish energy, Lin Yu decided to...
Take a short nap first.
Sheer exhaustion weighed on him—the prolonged trek followed by that direct encounter with 『Chate』 had taken its toll.
Most critically, his mind had been operating at maximum intensity, leaving him mentally fatigued.
Mild "brain fog" had even set in.
Thus, Lin Yu deemed a brief respite necessary.
"Haa—"
While "time pressure" was one factor, "physical condition" was another.
Lin Yu understood priorities clearly.
Given the seven-day duration, conserving energy while ensuring minimum rest was essential—he couldn't possibly forego sleep entirely.
Lying on the wooden bed, Lin Yu appreciated one cabin feature particularly:
A small wooden-cased clock beside the bed.
Initially, Lin Yu assumed it was broken.
But upon closer inspection—
"It's actually working..."
Lin Yu checked the time: approximately 3 PM.
"A fifteen to twenty-minute nap should suffice."
Yawning, Lin Yu planned to depart around 3:30 PM to locate the 'Detective' Furbollo and "recruit" him by nightfall.
With his schedule set, Lin Yu closed his eyes without worrying about oversleeping—he'd always possessed an internal alarm clock.
Since childhood, he could wake up within ten minutes of his intended time simply by deciding beforehand.
No failures so far.
Lying down, Lin Yu relaxed his muscles and practiced diaphragmatic breathing.
"Haa—"
Within seconds...
Lin Yu fell asleep.
And soon...
Lin Yu reopened his eyes to find himself standing in a frozen wasteland.
Shivering slightly from cold, Lin Yu felt puzzled.
"Why am I outside?"
"Wasn't I sleeping in bed?"
His thoughts remained crystal clear as realization struck:
"Oh wait—this is a dream!"Follow current novᴇls on NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
"Must be dreaming!"
Testing his limbs, Lin Yu noted this was perhaps the most "lucid" dream he'd ever experienced.
Stranger still, the environment matched his current dungeon.
Something felt off.
Yet before Lin Yu could ponder further...
Distant voices caught his attention.
"Hah! Finally made it to 'Extreme Winter Mountain'..."
"This time I'm getting enough Black Oil for sure!"
"Prices have never been higher—the nobles are really splurging!"
"A golden opportunity indeed. Can't let it slip away."
A group of rugged men in tattered fur clothing chatted cheerfully while trekking through snow.
Most faces were unfamiliar except...
The burly man he'd met earlier walked among them, laughing with the others!

chapters.title: Chapter 88: Dream, Death, and Clues
chapters.content:
In the dream, the burly men who had come to the mountain to "search for treasure" walked past Lin Yu while chatting and laughing, as if he didn't exist at all.
Lin Yu stood still, deep in thought.
"Is this just a dream caused by my excessive focus on this dungeon puzzle?"
"No... probably not."
Having suddenly experienced such a "lucid dream" related to the current game under these circumstances, Lin Yu absolutely couldn't treat it as just an ordinary dream.
"My perspective seems to be that of a detached observer, and at this time the burly man appears to still be alive..."
"Is this a fragment of the past?"
Lin Yu pondered as he followed the group through the snowstorm.
He counted their numbers - exactly thirteen people.
These thirteen men quickly split up after entering Extreme Winter Mountain."We can't travel together here!"
"Right, it would be bad if we attracted that monster called Chate."
"But we should actually thank that monster. If not for it, the rich folks wouldn't be offering such high prices for black oil!"
"True enough, haha... Let's hope we all make it back alive!"
"Wishing everyone good finds."
The thirteen men headed in different directions, their figures soon swallowed by the snowstorm.
After some thought, Lin Yu chose to follow the familiar burly man he had first encountered.
At the very least, he wanted to see how this guy had "died."
After all, from examining the corpse earlier, Lin Yu couldn't determine the exact "method of death."
Following the burly man, Lin Yu soon witnessed the complete process of searching for black oil.
The man took out a broom-like tool that Lin Yu had previously seen with the player called Dolphin, and began moving around while consulting a map.
When he reached areas with particularly deep snow accumulation, he would use the tool to sweep aside the snow.
Occasionally he would uncover some firewood or food, though Lin Yu hadn't seen him find any black oil yet.
Soon, night fell, and the man carrying firewood took out a torch from his backpack.
"Need to find a place to make a fire and rest."
Muttering to himself, he then examined the map by torchlight and seemed to choose a direction.
Watching the man's actions, Lin Yu felt something was odd.
"So he doesn't plan to go to a 'base,' but intends to make his own fire?"
As Lin Yu considered this, a belated realization struck him.
"Wait, in this 'time period' when the man was still alive, it seems there were no 'bases' in this mountain yet!"
Following the man all this way, Lin Yu hadn't seen any wooden cabins or similar structures.
Those man-made bases didn't exist at this point.
This realization made Lin Yu even more curious.
"So where is this man planning to go now?"
After following him just a few more steps, Lin Yu froze.
Because the burly man walked up to a massive rock that provided shelter from the snowstorm, arranged the collected firewood into a campfire, and began warming himself while eating the food he'd found during the day.
Lin Yu was astonished.
Because the rock where the man was currently staying...
If Lin Yu remembered correctly, this was exactly where his corpse had been found!
This filled Lin Yu with intense curiosity.
After eating his fill, the man extinguished his torch, hugged it to his chest, and fell asleep leaning against the burning campfire.
Then...
The night deepened.
Observing the man, Lin Yu saw he had fallen into deep sleep.
And then...
In the middle of the night, an expression of terror suddenly appeared on the man's face!
As if he was having a nightmare!Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn
But instead of waking up, the man seemed unable to rouse himself, his mouth opening in a silent scream!
A few more minutes passed...
After maintaining this terrified expression for a while, it suddenly froze on his face.
Lin Yu was stunned.
Several more minutes passed before he realized.
This burly man... had just died.
The passing of life could be so simple.
Although the lives encountered in this game were called "NPCs" by players...
Based on countless players' experiences, they were definitely not pre-programmed entities.
All these "NPCs" were essentially living beings.
Lin Yu sighed.
"This game is truly cruel."
He crouched down to carefully examine the man's corpse.
"So Chate's method of killing is to murder people in their sleep without leaving traces?"
"It seems this monster, despite boasting about how terrifying it is, actually specializes in 'mental attacks'... But that makes sense. When it was disguised as Furbollo earlier, its actual combat ability seemed nearly nonexistent - it shattered completely after being shot once."
As Lin Yu pondered, he reached a conclusion.
"So Chate kills people by doing something in their 'dreams,' creating fear and inescapable nightmares, right?"
At this thought, Lin Yu suddenly realized something extremely, extremely bad.
"Oh no, I seem to be dreaming right now!"
An indescribable terror instantly sprouted in his heart.
But the moment this "fear" emotion emerged, Lin Yu immediately activated his Corporate Drone skill.
Even in this "dream," the Corporate Drone's professional ability could take effect.
Lin Yu immediately felt himself calm down, his thoughts becoming clear and stable.
"This skill might seem weak, but as I suspected... it's actually god-tier."
"Emotions" themselves could already affect judgment in many situations.
And in the Death Game, life and death could be decided by the most minute judgments!
Moreover...
Many dungeons' difficulties might inherently lie in "emotions"!
Just like the current dungeon.
Whether the "fear" on the man's face before death was the cause of his demise or the result of what killed him, Lin Yu couldn't tell.
But he would absolutely avoid letting himself feel any "fear" emotion as much as possible.
The Corporate Drone skill had a cooldown of once per day, lasting one hour after activation.
So Lin Yu didn't hesitate to use it now.
Having forcibly calmed himself, Lin Yu exhaled and stated his conclusion.
"So Chate can only kill people in their dreams, right?"
Then, through the snowy dreamscape, a voice spoke.
"Your guess is correct."
The sudden voice seemed to come from far away, yet rang clearly in Lin Yu's ears.
If not for the "emotional stability" provided by his Corporate Drone ability, Lin Yu would probably have jumped in fright.
But now, he remained perfectly calm.
He looked around but saw no one.
After some thought, Lin Yu directly asked,
"Who are you?"
The voice indeed responded.
"Who I am isn't important. What matters is that you remember my clue."
"You're the smartest among this group... I hope you can escape - or perhaps, end all this."
As the voice spoke these words...
Lin Yu opened his eyes in bed.
He had woken up naturally, and looked to the side.
The clock by his bedside showed 3:35.

chapters.title: Chapter 89: Kidnapping the Detective!
chapters.content:
After pushing open the door and seeing that the sky still hadn't darkened, Lin Yu swallowed the food in his mouth and felt completely relieved.
When he first woke up and saw the alarm clock's time, feeling unprecedentedly energetic, he had thought he'd slept until 3:35 AM.
But now it seemed...
"I must have underestimated the stamina recovery efficiency of the 'Otaku' class," Lin Yu muttered, gripping his torch as he prepared to go find "Furbollo."
However, stepping onto the snow, Lin Yu encountered a new surprise.
The 'Postman' ability had disappeared.
This gave Lin Yu a small shock.
"Was my lie about being a 'Postman' seen through by that guy?"ᴛhis ᴜpdated by ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
"Impossible, it's very difficult for him to see through my lies..."
Lin Yu recalled the person he had deceived into believing he had 'Postman' abilities.It was a man whose profession was 'Security Guard,' someone who had only cleared four dungeons.
He didn't seem particularly sharp, alert, or intelligent—more like a real night-shift security guard, taciturn and listless.
Lin Yu didn't think that guy could suddenly see through the lie on his own.
"Unless he met someone else... but in that case, it shouldn't be just one ability disappearing."
Lin Yu checked and confirmed that the other eleven 'profession' abilities were still active.
"So it's more likely... the first death has already occurred."
Lin Yu exhaled in relief.
If someone died, then at least his first promotion task wouldn't count as a failure.
After all... the completion condition for the first promotion task was as follows:
[During this game, tell each participating player a different, mutually contradictory lie and activate the 'Fraudster' profession ability to make it 'come true.' Until the game ends, none of the lies must be exposed or seen through.]
"'Coming true' is required upon activation, but 'coming true' doesn't need to last until the game ends—what must last until the end is the lie not being exposed or seen through."
"In other words, if someone who believed my lie dies, it doesn't make my task fail."
Lin Yu let out a breath.
So, the optimal solution to ensure completion of the first promotion task in this game would actually be to kill everyone who believed his lies after deceiving them.
However, Lin Yu wouldn't do that.
Not because he was kind-hearted and unwilling to kill for his promotion task.
Mainly because...
Lin Yu didn't just have one promotion task to complete.
To survive this dungeon, it was better to have as many other players alive as possible.
For every living player, Lin Yu had one more usable 'profession' ability.
Like right now...
After that 'Security Guard' died, Lin Yu's movement through the snow was noticeably slower than before.
Of course, with the 'Soldier's' physical enhancement still active, while slower, it wasn't by much.
Lin Yu quickly cross-referenced the map with his memory and found the outpost where he had previously encountered "Furbollo."
However, Lin Yu didn't spot "Furbollo" anywhere near the outpost.
The outpost's door was wide open, and the stove inside had gone out.
The nearby snow clearly showed signs of having been thoroughly rummaged through, and though a thin layer of fresh snow had fallen over it, the area could still be described as "a complete mess."
"This detective is really something, clearing out all the supplies here in just half a day."
Lin Yu idly kicked at the snow on the ground and activated his 'Chef' ability.
The food had basically been completely scavenged.
Combined with the open door and the absence of the 'Detective' nearby...
"Must have relocated, right?"
Lin Yu pondered, then headed for the nearest outpost.
Sure enough, after trekking through the snowstorm for a while, Lin Yu spotted Furbollo at the nearest outpost, diligently digging for firewood in the snow.
The tall, foreign-looking 'Detective' had changed hats, no longer wearing the bright red knitted cap from before but instead a furry winter hat with ear flaps.
This made him instantly transform from Santa Claus into a Soviet political commissar.
The Henan Province version, of course.
"Hey, Detective," Lin Yu greeted Furbollo.
Hearing the voice in the snowstorm, Furbollo looked up, arms full of firewood, and smiled.
"Oh, it's May... what a coincidence! We meet again!"
"Seems our 'outposts' aren't too far apart, huh?"
Furbollo spoke, but Lin Yu shook his head.
"No, actually they're quite far apart," Lin Yu approached him and said, "I came specifically to find you."
"Find me?" Furbollo seemed surprised.
"What do you need?"
"Of course, I need to borrow your abilities as a 'Detective,'" Lin Yu said naturally. "I've discovered some puzzles related to this game dungeon, but I can't investigate them alone. Could you come with me to check them out?"
Hearing Lin Yu's words, Furbollo became somewhat interested.
"Puzzles? If the place isn't too far, I can go take a look!"
"I don't want to go too far—it's freezing out here, my toes are about to fall off."
"And if two people travel together for too long, they might get targeted by that 'Chate'..."
Listening to Furbollo's words, Lin Yu didn't lie but spoke honestly: "No, the place is actually quite far."
"Then I won't go. I don't want to freeze and risk getting killed by monsters," Furbollo said. "After all, I'm more of an 'armchair detective.'"
He hugged the firewood and politely declined.
Lin Yu smiled and said, "You don't need to worry about that."
"Did you find some way to stay warm and avoid getting killed by monsters?" Furbollo asked curiously.
"No," Lin Yu pulled out his revolver and pressed it against Furbollo's head. "If you don't go, I'll shoot you dead."
"So, rather than worrying about those 'risks'... maybe think about whether I'll pull the trigger instead."
Lin Yu's gaze was unwavering.
The revolver's only bullet had already been fired—at Furbollo's impostor.
But Furbollo didn't know that.
So, with a gun to his head, Furbollo instantly froze up.
He dropped the firewood and raised his hands to his head.
"Not cool... Brother May, what's this about?"
"You could've just persuaded me more! I'm a 'Detective,' I love solving puzzles, I really, really love solving puzzles!"
Furbollo's voice trembled as he spoke.
"Monsters or no monsters, cold or no cold, nothing can outweigh my passion for puzzles!"
"So... Brother May, could you put the gun away first?"
"I'm a bit worried about accidental discharge."

chapters.title: Chapter 90: The Detective's Discovery
chapters.content:
"Speak up, have you found anything?"
Lin Yu sat on the chair gripping his gun, watching as Furbollo circled the room three times before asking.
The so-called 'Detective' turned to face Lin Yu with a solemn expression.
"Indeed, I have made a discovery."
"This room... is warmer than I expected!"
Lin Yu sighed at Furbollo's words.
"Respected 'Detective Furbollo,' my time is precious, and so are my bullets."
"Either activate your Detective abilities immediately, or I'll take matters into my own hands."
Hearing this, Furbollo stopped dawdling and spoke quickly.
"Alright, I've actually already found the most suspicious thing in this room!"He pointed at the workbench.
"That table contains a hidden mechanism."
Lin Yu frowned slightly. "A mechanism? I didn't notice anything."
It was worth noting that Lin Yu had thoroughly inspected that very table.
He had tapped every part of it but found nothing unusual.
After all, it was while examining this table that Lin Yu had encountered Chate - giving him reason to suspect Chate didn't want him investigating further.
Yet repeated inspections afterward still revealed nothing amiss, making Lin Yu think it might just be coincidence.
But Furbollo shook his head.
"It's normal you didn't find it - the mechanism is extremely well hidden..."
Then he looked at Lin Yu.
"What do you think is most important for being a Detective?"
Lin Yu thought for a moment before answering:
"Is it reasoning ability and observational skills? Being able to find clues and deduce their hidden meanings?"
"Wrong," Furbollo shook his head.
"The most important thing for a detective... is knowledge."
He pointed to his head:
"You don't need deep expertise in any one area, but you need to know a little about everything."
"Nighttime constellations, herbal scents, rock hardness, martial arts styles... Any great detective must be a jack-of-all-trades."
"That way, when seeking 'truth,' environments that seem like meaningless fog to others become talkative friends."
"Therefore, I don't even need to activate my Detective ability yet."
Furbollo approached the table and gave it a slight push:
"This workbench's material is wrong - straight grain, brittle texture, easily stained. It's balsa wood."
"Normally used for small boxes or panels, rarely for tables."
"And even if used for a table, it shouldn't be this heavy - the weight when pushed felt like the elm tables from my hometown."
"So it's not solid wood throughout."
"I suspect it's like this cabin - wood covering metal construction."
Furbollo looked confidently at Lin Yu while scratching his butt.
"My suggestion? If you're looking for what's 'off' in this house, either chop it open... or burn it."
Hearing Furbollo's confident words, Lin Yu exhaled.
He picked up a black torch and without another word, lit it.
Pale flames scorched the wood, creating a black mark before quickly igniting the entire board.
Furbollo, watching Lin Yu's decisiveness, seemed surprised.
"You trust me that much?"
He said in astonishment as flames soon engulfed the entire table in quiet combustion.
"Your reasoning made sense. Why wouldn't I believe you?"
Lin Yu calmly observed the burning table.
Furbollo shook his head:
"Normally when I don't announce using my ability, convincing people is difficult."
He sighed:
"Whether in the Death Game or real life, people are stubborn, impossible to persuade..."
Lin Yu looked at Furbollo and couldn't help but comment:
"I think you should reflect on your own shortcomings."
While Furbollo's analysis was logical, everything from his attire to accent to demeanor made him inherently unconvincing!
He looked completely unreliable.
What kind of detective spoke with a Henan accent while wearing earflap hats?
If not for Lin Yu's fascination with human observation that minimized appearance's influence on judgment, even he would doubt Furbollo.
Soon, the entire table burned away.
As flames threatened to spread, Lin Yu grabbed a bucket found under the stove and doused it with snowmelt.
"Sizzle!"
The fire extinguished amidst billowing steam and smoke.
Behind the dying embers, a metal box was revealed where wood had burned away, bringing a pleased smile to Furbollo's face.
"Ha—I knew there was something inside!"
He stepped forward to brush off ash and charred remnants from the box's surface.
But upon touching it, Furbollo shrieked in pain.
"Damn, that's hot!"
He rushed outside screaming, plunging his hand into snow to cool it.
Lin Yu sighed and walked over.
"Oh wise polymath, great detective who knows astronomy and geography, didn't you know embers stay hot after fires?"
Tears of pain in his eyes, Furbollo looked up:
"I got too excited..."
Lin Yu shook his head again:New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
"Honestly don't know how you survived sixteen dungeons..."
He fetched another bucket of snow, pouring most over the metal box.
After this snow melted, the box's surface had cooled enough.
Lin Yu calmly brushed off residue with a book, then wiped his hands with snow.
The metal box stood about as tall as a six-year-old child, perfectly rectangular with a locked door on top secured by an old-fashioned rotary combination lock requiring a four-digit code.
Lin Yu crouched before it, pondering.
"The password then..."
Furbollo shuffled over, his right hand swollen red with whitened burns on palm and fingers that would soon blister.
"Brother May, could you heal me with your Doctor ability?"
"It hurts so damn bad!"
Lin Yu chuckled.
"Absolutely not. I don't compensate for stupidity."
"Besides, it's not life-threatening."
Furbollo eyed the lockbox.
"How about this - I'll solve the code, you heal my hand?"
Lin Yu gave him a strange look.
"When did you get the illusion you could bargain with me?"
"You solve the code, and I promise not to chop off that hand - that's more like it."

chapters.title: Chapter 91: Password, Dinner, and Puzzle
chapters.content:
Lin Yu still helped Furbollo heal that hand.
After all, the 'Doctor' ability wasn't limited to one use per game, but rather once per day.
Of course, the main reason was...
Furbollo had found "clues" about the password.
To save his own skin, Furbollo directly activated his 'Detective' ability.
Then, according to the 'Detective' ability's prompt...
The password clues for this metal box were hidden among the pile of books on the shelf.
There were eight books in total.
Naturally, Furbollo and Lin Yu began searching these books for password clues.
To improve Furbollo's book-flipping efficiency, Lin Yu casually healed his hand while at it.The two sat around the room's fireplace, flipping through these books covered in blacked-out sections, momentarily stumped.
Soon, dusk fell.
Furbollo closed his book and looked at Lin Yu.
"Boss May, any chance of dinner? I'm starving!"
Lin Yu looked at Furbollo helplessly. "Didn't you gather a bunch of food? Can't you just eat when hungry?"
As he spoke, Furbollo sheepishly rubbed his nose.
"Boss, I was thinking... this place has a stove, right?"
"Eating cold stuff keeps upsetting my stomach - I want something hot."
Lin Yu flipped through The Stupid Tire in his hands without looking up. "Go ahead then, just cook normally."
Furbollo looked embarrassed: "Well... actually I'm not great at cooking..."
Lin Yu finally looked up and sighed.
"I'm getting hungry too."
After spending this time together, Furbollo's initial fear of Lin Yu had faded considerably.
Perhaps the recent "hand healing" incident, combined with Lin Yu's 'Doctor' profession and his pretentious speech when they first met, had led to some misjudgment.
But Lin Yu couldn't be bothered to correct it.
Having Furbollo treat him with goodwill wasn't a bad thing after all.
Seeing Lin Yu set his book aside and head toward the kitchen, Furbollo quickly stood up.
"Boss May, don't worry, I won't freeload."
Furbollo took out an eco-friendly shopping bag from his pocket.
He opened it and produced peanut oil, a slab of pork belly, a box of eggs, plus various greens and seasonings.
Lin Yu was stunned.
"What the hell is this?"
"Oh, this is an item I got from my twelfth dungeon - [Discounted Shopping Bag]," Furbollo said proudly. "It provides discounted ingredients from supermarkets each time - 48-hour cooldown."
"If I don't take things out, they stay preserved inside."
"That thing's practically divine," Lin Yu remarked. "Why didn't you bring it out earlier?"
"Because I can't cook," Furbollo said matter-of-factly. "It only provides raw ingredients, never cooked ones - and usually near-expired stuff."
"I only eat from it when absolutely starving."
"Last dungeon I ate raw eggs from it - had diarrhea so bad I could barely stand by dungeon's end!"
Lin Yu resignedly took the ingredients.
"All thumbs and can't tell wheat from beans."
He commented.
However, according to his 'Chef' professional ability, these ingredients were indeed edible.Nᴇw ɴovel chaptᴇrs are published on
Having suffered through days of biscuits and barely edible roasted food himself - even with the canned food available here - Lin Yu's quality of life hadn't improved much.
Faced with proper cooking now, he naturally wouldn't refuse.
Soon, Lin Yu prepared braised pork belly with green beans, scrambled eggs with tomatoes, and spinach rice porridge.
After turning off the stove, they ate directly from the pots in the kitchen.
Furbollo couldn't help praising: "Damn, you cook like a restaurant chef - just how I like it, heavy on oil and salt... You must cook often at home?"
Lin Yu shook his head while eating the eggs: "No, I barely enter the kitchen at home."
After all, his elder sister Lin Zhao usually handled cooking.
Furbollo looked impressed: "Then you're a natural! Ever considered quitting medicine to open a restaurant?"
Lin Yu smiled: "That's exhausting work... my family's actually in that business."
"Though I don't cook much, whatever skill I have comes from family influence."
Furbollo studied Lin Yu's slender fingers thoughtfully: "Hmm... I see."
After dinner, Furbollo enthusiastically washed the pots before resuming book searching.
Perhaps the full meal stimulated their thinking.
When Lin Yu returned to the books, he suddenly realized something.
"Wait, I always thought blacking out these books seemed unnecessarily elaborate."
After all, for whatever purpose...
Complete destruction or hiding would be simpler.
Why would the young scholar who lived here painstakingly black out every book?
A possibility struck Lin Yu.
He examined the page numbers in The Stupid Tire.
Though numbered normally, each had an added "." symbol.
"Give me The Crazy Wrench from your side!"
Lin Yu called to Furbollo, who blinked before handing it over.
This book's page numbers...
Also followed "1.", "2." patterns.
Lin Yu checked another book - The Particularly Good Angry Gear.
Here, page numbers appeared as "-1-", "-2-".
Soon...
Lin Yu realized these eight books' page numbers fell into four categories:
Dotted, hyphenated, wavy-lined, and underlined.
After categorizing them, Lin Yu recalled the earlier map connections.
He tore out the first five pages from both The Stupid Tire and The Crazy Wrench.
Ignoring margins, he began arranging combinations.
Five pages' blacked portions could connect seamlessly end-to-end.
Lin Yu laughed at the assembled image on the floor.
"This guy's spatial visualization skills are impressive..."
"And he really loves these 'connect-the-dots' style hints."
As Lin Yu spoke, Furbollo had an epiphany too.
"So the blacked parts weren't for hiding - they form a puzzle!"

chapters.title: Chapter 92: Researcher's Notes and the Truth
chapters.content:
After tearing out all the pages and eliminating the "distracting options," Lin Yu and Furbollo quickly pieced together all the "puzzle pieces." The entire wooden floor was covered with the torn-out pages. This task was extremely time-consuming and laborious, and it was now well past midnight.
The scattered pages formed four large numbers on the floor: "9," "4," "5," and "7." Seeing these four numbers, Lin Yu nodded with satisfaction. "Good, the password should be some combination of these four digits. We just don't know the correct order yet..."
With four digits, there were 4! (24) possible permutations. Trying all 24 combinations one by one would be time-consuming but feasible. However, Lin Yu hesitated to gamble—what if the box had some self-protection mechanism that would destroy its contents after too many wrong attempts?Thɪs updatᴇd by NovᴇlFirenᴇt
As Lin Yu squatted pondering this, Furbollo suddenly spoke up. "The correct sequence should be either 5497 or 7945... with 5497 being more likely."
Lin Yu looked at him in surprise. "How did you deduce that?"
Furbollo shrugged. "Simple. These books weren't randomly paired. Their contents are strongly related—they seem like textbooks from the same academic course. Adjacent books usually share similar difficulty levels, which increase in the order of 5497. The publication dates follow the same sequence."
Lin Yu was astonished. "You can tell that despite the blacked-out pages?"
"Of course," Furbollo replied calmly. "The amount of blacked-out area reflects the quantity and complexity of the formulas. Plus, there are obvious hints in the content." He squatted down and pointed at one page forming the "4." "See this footnote? It references content from book 5. Section 7 is also an extension of 5—but since 9 mentions both 4 and 7, with an 'Additionally' before describing 7, I suspect 7 supplements 4."
Lin Yu stared at him, impressed. Despite his eccentric demeanor, Furbollo's detective skills were undeniable. Lin Yu was starting to believe he really was a professional detective. "You remember all these minute details?"
"Piece of cake," Furbollo boasted. "I can even tell what these books are about from fragments. They discuss using 'emotions' as fuel and raw materials—"*Click!* The sound of the lock opening interrupted Furbollo.
"Hey!" Furbollo glared at Lin Yu indignantly. "Can't you let me finish?"
While Furbollo had been monologuing, Lin Yu had already gone to try the combination. "Sorry," Lin Yu said without looking up as he opened the box. "I'm more interested in what's inside than the books' contents. We can discuss the dungeon's backstory later."
Furbollo sighed and joined him. "Fine, I'm curious too."
Inside the box was a transparent file containing three items: a black notebook, a white ID card, and a key—someone's personal belongings.
Lin Yu unceremoniously opened the file and examined the ID card. Its back bore a black logo of a burning book, while the front displayed basic information:
[Name: Vale Valetti]
[Gender: Male]
[Position: Independent Researcher]
[Clearance: B-3]
[Region: Extreme Winter Mountain]
A photo showed a gloomy young man with curly hair wearing a white dress shirt, his face partially scratched out.
"So this is the cabin's owner," Lin Yu muttered.
He then opened the notebook. Only the first third contained writing—research diary entries:
"August 7, Blizzard. Sensors detected a 'leak' here. Damn it, there's not a living soul around! How could there be a leak?"
"August 10, Blizzard. Slept poorly... Scouted the area today—nothing. Nearby settlements have been abandoned for years."
"August 15, Blizzard. Having constant nightmares—this place is awful. Why bother noting the weather? It's always snowing! Still no leads. One more week and I can leave."
"August 16, Blizzard. Dug up something disturbing... So many deaths here? And not a trace of residual souls on the bodies—highly abnormal!"
"August 17, Blizzard. There's a monster called 'Chate' in these mountains? My dreams grow more chaotic! Calling for backup once comms are restored!"
"August 25. What the hell is happening here? Why such terrifying creatures? My condition's deteriorating. Taking risks tomorrow!"
"August 26. Now I understand... No wonder it's called a 'leak.' Never imagined it would manifest this way. Our own mistakes caused this! So horrific!"
"August 27. I've figured out how to deal with 'Chate'!"
The diary ended abruptly, the remaining pages blank. The deteriorating handwriting mirrored the writer's worsening mental state. Lin Yu rubbed his temples. "Complicated indeed."
He exhaled deeply. The dungeon's "truth" was coming into focus—but it only gave Lin Yu more headaches. His goal wasn't solving the dungeon's mystery but finding the 'Fraudster.' Who had set up this 'scam' at Extreme Winter Mountain? He still had no leads.
Beside him, Furbollo suddenly spoke earnestly: "Thank you, May! Thank you for bringing me here!"
Lin Yu turned, puzzled by the detective's sincerity. "Why are you thanking me?" Hadn't he forced the 'detective' here at gunpoint?
Furbollo's eyes shone with fervor. "I initially thought this was just another survival dungeon, so I assumed any 'hidden puzzles' wouldn't be worth solving. I was wrong—this mystery is fascinating! Had you not discovered this place and forced me to come, I might have missed such an excellent puzzle!"
His face lit up with fanatical excitement. "Now, whether it's 'Chate' or this mysterious researcher... I'll uncover everything! The truth behind Extreme Winter Mountain!"

chapters.title: Chapter 93: Vale Valetti
chapters.content:
After Furbollo made his bold declaration of "getting to the bottom of this truth"...
The next thing they did was prepare for sleep.
After all, it was already late into the night, and both of them could barely keep their eyes open.
Though dawn wasn't far off, even two hours of sleep would provide some rest.
Lin Yu lay on the bed while Furbollo very considerately took out a sleeping bag. He replaced his dog-fur earflap hat with a wool nightcap before crawling inside.
"Tomorrow I'll definitely investigate this dungeon from top to bottom until everything's crystal clear! Then we'll both get the 'Threading the Needle' reward together!" Furbollo declared optimistically.
"Threading the Needle" was an achievement that, like "Master of Control," provided extra rewards on the [Settlement Interface].
Typically earned by uncovering hidden "truths" in non-puzzle type dungeons.
Listening to Furbollo's words, Lin Yu responded:
"Then I'll leave it to you."Having this so-called 'Detective' around did save him considerable trouble.ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
Though he wasn't particularly concerned about the "Threading the Needle" reward, he certainly wouldn't refuse it if offered.
Moreover...
His second Promotion task would most likely be completed in the process!
Of course, this didn't mean Lin Yu planned to completely hand over the reins.
He'd begun trusting this 'Detective' slightly more, but he still needed to keep puzzling through the dungeon's various mysteries himself.
Which was precisely why Lin Yu chose to sleep now.
Based on previous dreams... Lin Yu suspected sleep might be another means of gathering information.
Soon, Lin Yu drifted into slumber.
And sure enough...
When Lin Yu opened his eyes again, he found himself amidst howling winds and snow.
In the vast blizzard, a young man with long curly hair—wearing professional equipment and carrying a backpack—was digging into the frozen ground with a shovel.
Circling to face him, Lin Yu recognized the curly-haired youth's appearance.
It matched the researcher on the ID card he'd seen earlier: "Vale Valetti."
Soon, the young researcher unearthed several corpses from the frozen earth.
His expression turned grim as he knelt, using gloved hands to clear away more frozen soil before retrieving a device resembling an ammeter from his backpack.
"Zero soul readings again... Damn it! It's really true!"
As if realizing something, Vale took out a transparent case from his backpack.
The container held some squirming, semi-liquid black paste. Vale pointed the case at the corpses and took another reading with his device.
"Beep beep beep!"
The instrument emitted sharp alarms.
Vale seemed to completely break down, sitting in the snow with his face in his hands.
"So it really was our fault—the 'leak' caused these deaths!" Vale Valetti muttered painfully, tugging at his own hair.
Lin Yu quietly observed the young man's anguish while calmly analyzing:
"So... combining this with the notes from earlier, these deaths weren't caused by 'natural disasters,' and the monsters here aren't native to this place..."
"Rather, they resulted from something leaking from some 'organization.'"
"The Black Oil seems connected to these deaths too."
As Lin Yu pondered, Vale Valetti on the ground seemed to reach some resolution. He stood up and trudged into the snowstorm.
Lin Yu quickly followed.
Vale soon arrived before a cave entrance—not natural, but sealed by a metal door.
Producing a metal key, Vale unlocked the door and entered.
Lin Yu tried following, but an invisible force repelled him at the threshold.
Then...
A voice spoke behind Lin Yu.
"If you're seeing this, you've found what I left in the cabin."
The gentle voice belonged to a faint, translucent figure of the curly-haired young man standing behind him.
His identity needed no explanation.
"You're Vale Valetti?" Lin Yu asked, turning toward him.
The figure nodded in confirmation.
"Yes, I'm Vale Valetti, B-3 clearance researcher."
"Though... more accurately, I'm a consciousness fragment Vale Valetti left behind."
Lin Yu nodded. "I read your notes... What were you trying to accomplish?"
"What really happened inside Extreme Winter Mountain?"
"What is 『Chate』? What's this 'leak' about? How does Black Oil connect to those deaths?"
"And who built all these outposts in the mountain?"
Vale shook his head at Lin Yu's rapid-fire questions.
"Sorry, I can't answer those directly."
"My current existence is intrinsically linked to 'that thing.' If I answer here, my 'answers' and 'thoughts' will be detected."
"Then... you'd lose any chance of ending this."
"You might not even escape alive."
Vale's answer didn't surprise Lin Yu.
If solutions could be handed out in dreams, Vale wouldn't have made everything so convoluted initially.
"So you can only give me various 'hints'?"
"And only after I've discovered certain things first?"
Lin Yu asked.
"Yes, hints," Vale murmured. "With your intellect, I believe you'll deduce what must be done."
"I'm starting to understand," Lin Yu said, eyeing the metal door. "Find this cave, open that door."
"Using the key left with your ID and notebook."
As Lin Yu spoke, hope glimmered in Vale's eyes.
"Yes, yes—I can't reveal more."
"But... whether you seek truth or survival, trust me, this is your best path!"
"You're clever enough to end this."
Lin Yu sighed. "Understood... Though I should correct you—I'm not the smartest one here this time."
"There's a far more professional 'Detective' with me."
Vale stubbornly shook his head. "No, no... You're absolutely the cleverest."
"After all, your wisdom has earned divine recognition."
Pointing at Lin Yu's wrist, Vale continued:
"Even the God of Change who governs truth and void left his mark approving you..."
"So I believe in you too!"

chapters.title: Chapter 94: New Death, Accelerated Time
chapters.content:
"Huff—"
Lin Yu woke from his slumber and sat up on the bed.
Furbollo was still sound asleep in his sleeping bag on the floor, drool trickling from the corner of his mouth, looking utterly content.
Lin Yu walked over and kicked Furbollo.
"Time to wake up."
Startled from his dreams, Furbollo panicked and rolled twice across the floor.
"What the—? Who's ambushing me? Aah!"
He shouted while clumsily disentangling himself from the sleeping bag before jumping out in alarm.
Lin Yu sighed helplessly at Furbollo's antics.
"Furbollo, it's me."Recognizing Lin Yu, Furbollo calmed down.
"Oh, it's you, May."
He exhaled and looked outside.
Dawn had just begun breaking. Furbollo frowned.
"How long did we sleep?"
Lin Yu checked the bedside clock: "About three hours. We slept around 4 AM, and now it's almost 7 AM."
As Lin Yu spoke, Furbollo's frown deepened.
"That's not right. My head doesn't hurt at all."
"Whenever I sleep less than eight hours, I always get headaches!"
Hearing this, Lin Yu suddenly realized something.
"Something is definitely wrong!"
He muttered under his breath.
Now Lin Yu discovered he'd lost three more abilities!
The powers of [Ruffian], [Chef], and [Corporate Drone] had vanished!
This meant...
Either three people had seen through his lies last night.
Or...
They were dead.
Neither possibility was good.
Thinking this, Lin Yu grabbed a torch.
"Hey, Furbollo... we need to hurry."
"To confirm something!"
Without looking back, Lin Yu strode out the door.
Still half-asleep, Furbollo blinked before scrambling after him.
"Wait for me, May!"
He called out, catching up to Lin Yu.
"Where are we going? What are we checking?"
Lin Yu didn't answer, instead leading them to one of the zones from memory.
The area where the player who believed he was a [Chef] had been staying.
After some searching, Lin Yu found him in one of the outposts.
The outpost door stood wide open, the furnace inside extinguished as snow blew inward.
The player was a slightly balding middle-aged man.
He lay curled by the furnace, long dead.
Furbollo hurried over, pressing the corpse's skin before frowning.
"Excluding temperature factors, time of death... roughly 12 hours ago."
"No obvious external wounds or signs of poisoning. Possibly froze to death, or... unnatural causes."
"Judging by his expression—might have been scared to death."
Hearing Furbollo's accurate estimation, Lin Yu exhaled.
He'd thought they'd need to examine more bodies, but now... probably unnecessary.
"Likely killed by [Chate]. Probably 'dream murder'... literally scared to death."
"Also, based on his death and my 'known information', I can deduce one more thing."
Lin Yu said, looking at Furbollo.
Furbollo met his gaze: "What are you getting at?"
"Furbollo, what day do you think it is?"
"Day three?"
"No, it's day five," Lin Yu stated seriously. "Every time we sleep... we're out for over 24 hours."
"That's how the monster called [Chate] kills... I found the corpse of the NPC we first met earlier. Same death pattern."
Furbollo's expression shifted.
"Seriously? Bro, why didn't you say so earlier!"
"I didn't fully trust you before."
Lin Yu replied calmly.
"That explains everything. No wonder my head doesn't hurt," Furbollo's face darkened briefly before breaking into a grin, "Heh, damn... this is actually kinda fun!"
Gritting his teeth, excitement flashed in his eyes: "So this dungeon isn't just about hidden 'truths' and 'puzzles'—it's properly difficult too."
"Time to get serious."
Furbollo yanked off his woolen hat and stuffed it into his coat, revealing messy lead-gray hair.
He carefully smoothed it back before producing a black bowler hat from his coat.
Lin Yu watched curiously.
"Is that hat some powerful item? Blocks mental attacks? Stops oversleeping?"
"Nah, purely decorative," Furbollo's ears and nose were bright red from cold, "But it symbolizes my resolve—means I'm now playing this dungeon at 70% effort!"
Lin Yu blinked before retorting:
"Why not go all-out 100%?"
Furbollo shook his head: "I don't think... it's necessary yet."
"Give me 100% right now!"
As Lin Yu insisted, Furbollo opened his mouth to argue, then—
Meeting Lin Yu's piercing gaze in the snowstorm, he shrank back.
"Fine, fine! 100% it is!"
Grumbling, he swapped the bowler for a woven straw hat.
"Maximum power mode, activate!"
Lin Yu sighed at the hat exchange.
"What kind of weird habit is this?"
"So the wool hat means 'hibernation mode' and those heavy earflap hats are 'power-saving mode'?"
Furbollo looked shocked.
"How did you know?!"
Lin Yu sighed louder.
"It's completely obvious!"
Furbollo pondered this before studying Lin Yu.
"Impressive, May. Doctor's observational skills... you must be great at surgery, right?"
"I know squat about surgery—just a med student. Haven't even done residency."
Lin Yu deflected.
Better not claim expertise... what if he got exposed later?
Claiming to be a student was safest.
After all, "April" they'd met earlier was also a med student who got the [Doctor] profession.
Furbollo nodded thoughtfully.
"I see..."
"So, where next? You've got a plan, right?"Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs
"Since... you seem to get revelations in your dreams."
"Some special item doing that?"
Furbollo inquired.
Lin Yu looked surprised at the [Detective]'s insight.
He nodded: "Correct, I do receive dream hints."
"Our notebook's owner, 'Vale Valetti', has been sending me visions these past days!"

chapters.title: Chapter 95: This Must Be Chate's Illusion!
chapters.content:
Lin Yu hadn't initially planned to tell Furbollo all the information he possessed.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ
Though he'd resolved to eliminate this 'Detective' if suspicions arose, Lin Yu found Furbollo surprisingly useful as a tool during their interactions.
This 'Detective' genuinely had skills - he was even sharper than Lin Yu had anticipated.
Thus, Lin Yu became somewhat reluctant to kill him.
Therefore...
Lin Yu changed his strategy.
He decided to be more "honest" with Furbollo.
Regarding anything unrelated to his promotion mission, Lin Yu could afford complete transparency.
As for the dungeon information...
Lin Yu decided to process and reveal everything to Furbollo.After omitting the "motives" and the reasons Vale Valetti trusted him, Lin Yu shared all currently known intelligence with Furbollo.
Trekking through the snowstorm, Furbollo examined the metal key while piecing together the situation's context.
"I understand... Combining this with the notebook we found, the events at 'Extreme Winter Mountain' represent a textbook case of technology-induced tragedy," Furbollo mused. "Some organization possessing 'advanced technology' had an accident here, creating a monster called 『Chate』 that caused numerous deaths..."
"Then some poor low-level employee from that organization was sent to investigate, discovered the truth, and unfortunately died here too."
"But he was luckier - he retained his consciousness. He's been warning you through dreams."
"This might also be protective, since that 『Chate』 creature's killing method is dream-related."
Lin Yu largely agreed with Furbollo's analysis.
"Exactly my thoughts... So now we need to reach that 'cave'."
Hearing this, Furbollo frowned.
"But are you certain 'Vale Valetti' is trustworthy, Doctor?"
"Remember... It's not just Players we need to guard against. Sometimes NPCs require caution too."
"Currently, both 『Chate』 and the deceased 'Vale Valetti' possess dream-invasion abilities. Even if he was kind in life..."
Furbollo trailed off meaningfully.
Lin Yu nodded. "I understand, Furbollo. I haven't fully trusted him either."
"But even if it's deception, even if it's a trap, I still want to investigate," Lin Yu exhaled softly. "Because we're running out of time."
"This is already our fifth day... But considering humans can't maintain 72 hours without sleep under such stress, we'll likely need to sleep once more."
"So this might be our 'second-to-last' period of consciousness."
"Of course... To simply clear the dungeon, we could ignore it and gamble that 『Chate』 won't kill us during our final sleep."
"But would you be satisfied with that, Furbollo?"
Lin Yu stared directly at him.
"Your will to survive is undoubtedly tied to 'uncovering the truth,' isn't it?"
"Same here - not understanding the truth would haunt me forever!"
He declared with contagious conviction.
Furbollo's expression twisted conflictedly at Lin Yu's words.
Finally adjusting his straw hat, he conceded: "You've convinced me, Doctor. I entered this 『Death Game』 precisely because of an unsolved 'cold case.'"
"That's just how I am - any sufficiently complex mystery left unsolved makes me physically uncomfortable."
"I'll take this risk with you - besides, such an intricate, deeply-hidden dungeon must offer fantastic rewards for 『Threading the Needle』!"
"Damn it all, if I can't solve this mystery after bringing out the 'Straw Hat,' that'd be downright embarrassing!"
Furbollo growled determinedly.
Lin Yu regarded him with understanding.
"I knew it - we're cut from the same cloth!"
He laughed.
Furbollo joined in the laughter.
"Never expected a doctor... to be just as crazy."
"But encountering a 'kindred spirit' does feel incredible."
As he watched Furbollo laugh, Lin Yu secretly sighed in relief.
"Success."
Furbollo was indeed brilliant.
When he'd produced the "Straw Hat" and claimed to enter "full-power mode," it wasn't empty boasting.
This 『Detective』 who'd cleared sixteen dungeons hadn't even been 70% serious about this one before.
But...
Precisely because of this, Lin Yu's current "performance" worked so effectively.
He understood exactly what this "genius" Furbollo desired.
For Lin Yu, deceiving "geniuses" became easier than fooling ordinary people once he comprehended them.
Because geniuses believe what they choose to believe.
"Might even use him to investigate the Psychological Society after escaping."
Lin Yu considered, though his focus returned to the current dungeon.
"Let's go, Furbollo - time to uncover the truth!"
"To that cave we go."
As Lin Yu spoke, Furbollo flashed a confident grin.
"Agreed. Based on my geological knowledge, this 'Extreme Winter Mountain' features typical folded terrain. Any cave capable of housing metal doors... was likely a large natural formation."
"Such caves usually form between two peaks... and within this dungeon's 'boundaries,' there are only two high points."
Furbollo declared triumphantly. Lin Yu nodded.
"Lead the way then."
"No problem, May - when I enter full-power mode, clearing dungeons becomes child's play!"
"That's precisely why I usually hold back - at full mental capacity, any dungeon loses its challenge!"
Furbollo boasted, then...
After trekking through the snowstorm for hours, Furbollo guided Lin Yu to the convergence point of two mountain peaks.
Standing amidst endless snow, staring at two exposed, barren cliff faces, Furbollo fell deep into thought.
Lin Yu looked at Furbollo and sighed.
"Not very impressive for 'full-power mode,' great Detective."
"Where's this cave of yours?"
Furbollo scratched his head vigorously.
"What the hell? This can't be right... This must be 『Chate's』 illusion!"

chapters.title: Chapter 96: The Truth of Extreme Winter Mountain
chapters.content:
The snowstorm intensified.
Lin Yu and Furbollo stood silently before the cliff face in the midst of the swirling snow for a long time.
Finally, Furbollo broke the silence.
"This is just the most probable location for a cave entrance, but there's no guarantee it's definitely here."
"That said, weren't you given this information in a dream—do you remember roughly where the cave was positioned in your dream?"
Hearing Furbollo's words, Lin Yu rubbed his temples.
"That's exactly the problem—according to my dream memory, the cave should indeed be right here."
Lin Yu pointed directly at the cliff face before them.
"Moreover, I can't shake the feeling this place seems... unnatural."Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
The two had already spent time knocking and probing the rock surface earlier, but found nothing unusual.Furbollo furrowed his brow.
"Is that so..."
After a long moment of contemplation, he exhaled sharply.
"If we assume your intuition is correct, then it seems... we'll have to use abilities!"
With that, Furbollo murmured quietly: "I want to know the locations of any hidden 'doors' and 'caves' nearby."
As he spoke, Furbollo activated his Detective class ability.
Moments later, Furbollo turned back to Lin Yu as if seeing some prompt.
"My Detective ability indicates the key to finding the hidden 'door' and 'cave' nearby... lies with you."
"With me?"
Lin Yu looked puzzled.
Furbollo circled Lin Yu once before exclaiming in realization: "Got it—it's the torch on your back."
"The torch?"
Lin Yu remained confused.
"Does this thing have some hidden function I don't know about?"
He removed the torch from his back and waved it around, feeling nothing unusual.
Amidst the snowstorm, Lin Yu lit the torch.
Pale flames leaped forth, instantly melting the surrounding snow.
Furbollo moved closer to warm himself.
"Honestly, why don't you keep this lit all the time... At least it would make us less freezing!"
"It's cumbersome," Lin Yu answered succinctly, watching Furbollo huddle near the flames. "Are you sure this is really the clue, or are you just saying that to hog the torch?"
Furbollo shook his head.
"What nonsense—do I look like that shameless of a person? I have dignity!"
"Do you really?"
Lin Yu countered.
Furbollo, rubbing his hands for warmth, found himself speechless at Lin Yu's retort: "Alright, fine, I might discard pointless pride when necessary... but I'm absolutely not joking about the clue."
"This torch genuinely is the key to 'finding' the cave."
As Furbollo spoke, Lin Yu turned his attention back to the torch.
"What's the deal then? Do we need to return to where I found it?"
"But that doesn't make sense—there was just a rock there, nothing resembling the cave entrance from my dream."
Lin Yu muttered while Furbollo pondered.
"Hmm... Let me think. A torch's functions are basically warmth, illumination, and ignition... Maybe we need to examine things closely with it?"
Following this suggestion, Lin Yu brought the torch closer to the cliff face.
"Well... doesn't seem any different."
But seconds later, as both stared at the completely unchanged rock surface, realization struck them simultaneously.
"Wait!"
The problem wasn't that the cliff face changed when near the torch—it was that it didn't change at all!
The rock surface had minor protrusions and cracks filled with accumulated ice.
Yet this ice...
Showed absolutely no signs of melting when exposed to the torch's flames.
As if someone had pressed a "pause" button.
Furbollo exclaimed excitedly: "The cliff face is definitely abnormal... though we still don't know how exactly!"
"It seems completely unaffected by external conditions."
Unlike Furbollo, Lin Yu had already figured out the truth.
"I understand now... this is a 'cliff face from the past.'"
"This thing really does require the torch to deal with!"
Saying this, Lin Yu pressed the flaming torch directly against the rock surface.
He twisted the torch's base—first extinguishing the pale flames...
Then reignited it!
"Fwoosh!"
Flames burst forth, scorching the cliff face.
Soon, the previously immutable rock surface began fading under the sustained heat!
The stone patterns blurred and melted, the bluish-gray surface transforming into an increasingly dense black mass!
The angular surfaces smoothed out, losing their solid form.
Until it became flowing black paste.
This was why Lin Yu understood the cliff's nature better than Furbollo.
Because he'd seen this phenomenon before.
Only last time, what appeared before him wasn't an inanimate rock wall.
But a living, breathing Furbollo.
Soon...
The melted black paste caught fire too, bursting into pale flames!
Lin Yu stepped back as the flames spread rapidly, engulfing the entire cliff face in roaring fire.
"Just as I suspected, this shares origins with 'Black Gold Oil.'"
Lin Yu exhaled sharply.
"Not only is it excellent fuel... but it can also transform into various people or objects that previously existed."
Furbollo had his epiphany too.
"So that's it... this must be the 'technology' recorded in those books."
He turned excitedly to Lin Yu: "That researcher's organization developed technology to extract human emotions and transform them into some kind of 'miraculous substance'!"
"This extracted substance serves as both premium fuel and highly malleable material!"
"Exactly what we're seeing now!"
As Furbollo spoke, the entire cliff face burned fiercely.
The pale flames melted all surrounding snow, creating a rare calm area on Extreme Winter Mountain devoid of wind or snowfall.
Soon...
The false cliff face of black oil burned away completely, revealing the truth behind it—an almost identical layered rock face now stood before Furbollo and Lin Yu.
Except at its exact center was a carved cave entrance with a towering circular metal door!
Exactly matching what Lin Yu saw in his dream after Vale Valetti's clue...
Every detail identical!
"Let's go, time to enter!"
Lin Yu said, producing the key while looking at Furbollo.
Furbollo rubbed his hands together eagerly.
"Alright, let's proceed..."
"To uncover the truth of Extreme Winter Mountain!"

chapters.title: Chapter 97: I Thought You Were From the Psychological Society!
chapters.content:
Lin Yu inserted the metal key into the door's keyhole and gently turned it.
Then...
The entire metal door emitted a dull sound.
"Clank—"
As if some extremely heavy mechanism had been activated, the metal door slowly swung open, revealing a deep, long, and wide passageway inside.
Lin Yu instinctively raised his torch higher and gave Furbollo a push.Thɪs updatᴇd by novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
"Go on, inside!"
Furbollo looked at Lin Yu helplessly, about to protest.
"I mean, why..."
But seeing Lin Yu's free hand already holding the revolver, Furbollo swallowed his words."Alright, it's only natural for me to scout ahead."
Furbollo stepped into the passageway behind the cave entrance first.
The two proceeded cautiously one after another, gradually advancing deeper into the cave hidden within the blizzard.
To Lin Yu's surprise...
Although the passageway inside the cave appeared naturally formed, there were far more signs of artificial modification than expected.
The floor was paved with smooth, unidentifiable metal plates emitting an eerie blue glow.
"This is way too sci-fi..."
Lin Yu muttered before couldn't help complaining: "That NPC's outfit, manner of speaking, and the cabin's furnishings all made me think this dungeon had a relatively low-tech setting."
"Never expected it to be this advanced."
Furbollo laughed heartily.
"Aha, May, have you ever encountered 'cyberpunk' works?"
"Sometimes the more technologically advanced a society becomes, the greater the disparity in living standards between different classes and regions... In such settings, the upper class might live near-futuristic lives while the lower class regresses to feudal or even primitive conditions."
Hearing Furbollo's words, Lin Yu nodded slightly.
"I've heard of this concept. So you're saying Extreme Winter Mountain follows this pattern?"
"Exactly."
Furbollo continued walking as he spoke: "Any organization that masters and monopolizes technology capable of materializing 'emotions' as fuel and raw materials would gain godlike powers."
"So this is why you instinctively distrust—even oppose—Researcher Vale Valetti and his organization, isn't it?"
Lin Yu casually asked.
Furbollo responded just as casually: "Of course, Doctor, that organization..."
Then Furbollo suddenly realized something was off.
"Wait, are you probing me?"
Furbollo had never expressed any attitude toward this organization before.
His only skepticism about the NPC Vale Valetti emerged when Lin Yu brought it up.
Lin Yu burst into laughter, his unrestrained mirth echoing through the passageway.
"Hahaha, you caught me, 『Detective』."
"So you do recognize that organization—you identified their logo, their 'symbol,' and their 'technology' from the start, didn't you?"
As Lin Yu laughed, Furbollo clicked his tongue.
"Scary how perceptive you are, May the 『Doctor』. No wonder you said we're alike... I acknowledge you now."
"But when did you spot my slip-up?"
Lin Yu shook his head: "When you analyzed those books' contents—frankly, while I'm no genius, I don't believe anyone could determine what kind of technology they described when over 80% of each academic book's content was missing."
"What I found impossible, you accomplished effortlessly—that's not genius, that's 'cheating'—C, H, E, A, T."
"Later I became certain you already knew some truths about this dungeon."
"Maybe due to your professional abilities, or perhaps... you've encountered this organization before."
"After all, while dungeons in the 『Death Game』 aren't necessarily connected, many share common elements."
Lin Yu spoke softly as Furbollo stopped walking.
Standing in the spacious passageway, Furbollo turned around with a pained expression: "Dang it, bro, how're you so sharp?"
"I admit I've encountered this 'organization' before—I've dealt with them across three different dungeons."
"I hid this because I didn't want you deeply involved—most in this 'organization' are cold-blooded, profit-driven exploiters devoid of humanity."
Seeing Furbollo's sincerity, Lin Yu shook his head.
"No, that's not it..."
"What really puzzles me is you don't seem to fully trust me either—you've been testing me this whole time."
"You don't seem to believe I'm actually a doctor or medical student, yet you accept my 『Doctor』 profession."
"Why is that?"
Furbollo put on an ingratiating smile.
"The truth, Mr. Furbollo—no more jokes masking your real thoughts."
Lin Yu's cold tone made Furbollo pause before he sighed with a wry smile.
"Fine, fine... I admit I recognized your identity."
"At first I pretended not to know—your 『Psychological Society』 is too extreme, actually sending someone of your caliber to approach me."
"I didn't mean to expose you..."
Furbollo's words left Lin Yu utterly bewildered.
"What?!"
"Wait, hold on—" Lin Yu pulled out the lie detector and pointed it at Furbollo, "Say that again. Who did you think I was? Use the phrase 'I thought you were...'!"
"Huh?"
After a confused pause, Furbollo complied: "I thought you were an executive-level member of the 『Psychological Society』."
The lie detector's green light activated—Furbollo truly believed this.
Lin Yu exhaled deeply.
"Haah..."
"How did you reach that conclusion?"
Furbollo answered matter-of-factly: "Your profession is 『Doctor』, but judging by your hands and how you treated my burn directly with abilities... you don't seem like an actual doctor."
"Yet you awakened as a 『Doctor』 and observe people with exceptional acuity—I figured you might be a 'psychiatrist' in reality... and nearly all real 'psychiatrists' are 『Psychological Society』 members."
"Being able to enter others' dungeons freely requires at least 'executive-level' clearance—aren't you one?"
After Furbollo finished, Lin Yu remained silent for a long moment before sighing.
"While I know it's not your fault... you're such an idiot, Furbollo!"
"I fucking thought you were from the 『Psychological Society』!"

chapters.title: Chapter 98: The True Nature of Chate
chapters.content:
Logically speaking, Lin Yu completely understood why Furbollo suspected him of being a member of the Psychological Society. After all, he had been hiding many things and appeared highly suspicious. Combined with Furbollo's earlier analysis, Lin Yu realized that from Furbollo's perspective, he did seem like someone from the Psychological Society.
However...
Emotionally, being mistaken for a Psychological Society member still irritated Lin Yu somewhat. "Do I really look that mentally unstable?" he asked Furbollo helplessly.
Furbollo cautiously observed Lin Yu. "To be honest, you do tend to overreact sometimes... But it seems you really aren't from the Psychological Society after all."
"Why the sudden certainty?" Lin Yu countered curiously.
"Because Psychological Society members never bother hiding themselves," Furbollo sighed. "In some ways, they're quite open about their activities. Among the three recognized 'anti-Order' organizations, the Psychological Society is actually the most transparent one."
Lin Yu nodded as Furbollo spoke. "You're right, I have no connection to that organization. In fact... I have grievances against them."The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the
This time Lin Yu didn't perform or conceal his true feelings, directly expressing his hostility toward the Psychological Society.
Furbollo noticed Lin Yu's animosity. "I can tell those lunatics are quite annoying... Anyway, since you're not one of them, I can relax." Furbollo exhaled in relief, adjusting his cotton pants before continuing: "Let's return to the dungeon topic... The organization behind this setup at Extreme Winter Mountain is called 'Truth Corporation' - their activities appear in many Death Game dungeons."
"Moreover, once you interact with their NPCs... they seem to add you to their database. If you oppose them, you'll need to be extra cautious when encountering them in future dungeons," Furbollo warned.Lin Yu suddenly understood. "So that's why you kept this hidden?"
"Yes, initially I thought you were from the Psychological Society and considered setting you up," Furbollo admitted, hiking up his pants again. "But since it was a misunderstanding... I should make things clear now. Are you sure you want to wade into these troubled waters?"
Lin Yu exhaled slowly while looking at Furbollo. "We've come this far - why not? I'm genuinely curious about the truth behind all this, not to mention... there are extra rewards to gain, right?"
This statement was half-truth again. Furbollo likely thought Lin Yu referred to the "Threading the Needle" achievement bonus, but actually... Lin Yu meant his Promotion mission.
Furbollo gave a thumbs up. "Great, May, my good brother! I knew I wasn't wrong about you! In that case, I'll risk my life to accompany a true gentleman!"
Lin Yu felt speechless at Furbollo's words. 'Not wrong about me'? When did we become 'good brothers'? Weren't you the one suspecting me as Psychological Society all along?
But one shouldn't attack someone offering friendship, so Lin Yu didn't want to dampen the mood. The two continued down the passage until... a faint light appeared ahead.
By Lin Yu's estimation, although the downward slope was gentle, they had been walking for over ten minutes and were now at least fifty meters underground.
"What do you think we'll find ahead, having encountered Truth Corporation before?" Lin Yu asked.
Furbollo shook his head. "I don't know - I've only interacted with them three times. But I do hear water sounds."
Lin Yu nodded slightly - he too detected faint water sounds from the lit area ahead. Both unconsciously slowed their pace. Finally, they emerged from the passage onto a platform at the top of stairs.
Looking down, beyond the already spacious passage lay an even vaster space - a natural cavern large enough to contain an entire factory. High-tech cold light strips embedded in circular patterns along the rock walls illuminated the entire area.
And here... there was indeed an entire factory!
Tall metal tanks and various instruments stood everywhere, interconnected by smooth metallic pipes that appeared quite advanced. Yet this sophisticated factory complex now lay abandoned, with most equipment and pipes submerged in pitch-black oil that formed a small lake.
At the center stood the only still-functioning massive device - a structure resembling a metallic heart that pulsated rhythmically like a real one. Two large holes at its top gushed black oil with each beat, producing the water sounds they'd heard.
"So it's literally a 'leak' in the physical sense," Lin Yu exhaled. "Which brings the question - what's Chate's connection to all this?"
Furbollo looked grave. "I don't know, but these things... give me a very bad feeling. Nothing from Truth Corporation is ever simple... especially this technology that materializes emotions."
"If I had to guess, this 'black oil' likely represents 'fear'."
Lin Yu nodded. "I agree it symbolizes fear..." Suddenly he recalled the hint he'd received as a Teacher: 'Chate is not alive.' This could mean Chate was dead, or alternatively... that Chate wasn't a living creature to begin with.
Lin Yu looked up at the machine. "I remember a childhood animated movie with similar concepts - monsters using human 'fear' as energy, scaring children to collect it."
"We've heard NPCs mention 'snow monsters' and 'Chate', but... no one has actually seen them. Even Chate's killing method involves frightening people to death in their sleep!"
As Lin Yu spoke, Furbollo had an epiphany. "You mean Chate might not be an actual creature, or even a physical entity!"
"Exactly."
A gentle voice spoke behind them. The flowing black oil had crept onto their platform, coalescing into the form of a curly-haired young man in a white lab coat - Vale Valetti appeared before Lin Yu and Furbollo.
"As you've correctly deduced - 'Chate' is the name of a project by my employer, Truth Corporation."

chapters.title: Chapter 99: The Truth Corporation and Ville Valetti’s Request
chapters.content:
Fifty years ago, the "Truth Corporation" rose to become one of the newest giant companies in the "Sleepless City" through a new type of alchemical technology called "Emotion Conversion."
"Emotional energy" gradually became the most commonly used energy source throughout the "Sleepless City."
At first, the "Emotion Conversion" technology was very simple, only capable of extracting human "joy" and "sorrow."
The "Truth Corporation" created one emotional collector after another and provided the citizens of the "Sleepless City" with a large amount of entertainment products.
Soon, this technology evolved rapidly, able to convert more and more types of "emotions," and the extraction technology became increasingly advanced.
The extracted "emotions" were found not only usable as "fuel," but also as various materials to craft machinery and buildings.
As the "Truth Corporation" grew larger, it began conducting deeper experiments that were previously forbidden.
For example...
They developed a substance called "Fear Oil" from the emotion named "Fear."
This was the most "universal" kind of emotional creation. As fuel, it was the most efficient, and as a raw material, it could transform into almost any "substance."It could even disguise itself as "life."
It seemed to confirm the saying:
"Fear is the most instinctive and primal emotion deep within the human soul."
But because of this, the extraction and storage of "fear" were also the most difficult, and a slight mistake could drive people insane or even directly kill them.
Moreover, these solidified fears had another function that no other materials possessed...
They could "store souls."
Rather than "store," it was more like "imprison."
The principle behind this "Fear Oil" disguising itself as life was that it could perfectly simulate human consciousness.
Therefore, although the other two oligarch companies in "Sleepless City" united to suppress the "Truth Corporation" for the first time, forcing it to promise to abandon the development of "Fear Oil,"
However...
How could they truly give up?
Such an alluring technology with infinite possibilities was impossible for the Truth Corporation to abandon.
Thus...
Outside of the "Sleepless City," beyond the federation, in the endless "Great Wilderness," at those backward human settlements, the "Truth Corporation" began secretly constructing experimental bases.
"Extreme Winter Mountain" was one of them.
Originally, several human towns surviving by hunting existed nearby.
The "Truth Corporation" targeted them.
After all, most residents in the Great Wilderness were foolish and short-sighted.
So, several senior executives and A-level researchers of the Truth Corporation built a complete set of "Fear Oil" conversion equipment under the perpetually snow-covered Extreme Winter Mountain next to the towns, falsely claiming it was ordinary emotion conversion equipment.
Then, disguised as nobles, they tricked the townspeople by saying there was a precious resource called "Black Gold Oil" in the mountains that could be exchanged for money with them.
The townspeople, believing the rumor, entered the mountain, only to be terrified by the executives using pre-spread "snow monster rumors" and the company's unique "Dream Manufacturing Device," providing a huge amount of "fear" and refining a large quantity of Fear Oil.
This was the plan named "Chate."
But...
Even those executives did not anticipate that although Fear Oil as a raw material was almost universal, due to insufficient data, it had a fatal flaw no one had discovered before.
It had a strong tendency to destroy life and devour souls!
The ability to "store souls" was not its feature but its kind of "instinct"!
Although Fear Oil was not life, it was a creation originating from human emotions and followed almost life-like patterns.
The initial "fright" created fear that only terrified those poor innocent townspeople into madness.
But later, as the quantity of Fear Oil accumulated... things got out of control.
These "solidified" fears even began to affect the operation of the instruments themselves.
Among those frightened people...
There began to be victims who died directly in their sleep, scared to death.
And their souls were taken by the Fear Oil—these occasional appearances of the dead souls further deepened the fear of others entering Extreme Winter Mountain!
All these changes happened so quickly, almost within a few days.
So much so that the senior researchers and executives of the Truth Corporation did not react in time.
They simply assumed it was "equipment failure," only considering "how to fix the malfunction" with technical adjustments.
Thus, this arrogance made these "culprits" pay a price—in one dream, they too remained forever in the base beneath this snowy mountain.
But this "evil begets evil" was not a good thing.
Because without maintenance personnel, the machines eventually malfunctioned and leaked—
All the emotions and the souls of the devoured people fused together, forming a certain consciousness, almost capable of controlling the entire Extreme Winter Mountain—this was the "Fear Oil" or the monster called "Chate."
This "monster," for the purpose of self-replication, continuously released portions of Fear Oil onto the surface, maintaining the "scam" fabricated by the Truth Corporation, attracting innocent people to Extreme Winter Mountain.
It was clever, even allowing a few people to safely leave with the Fear Oil—
Even without buyers, those small pieces of "Black Oil" that could sustain one through an entire winter were enough to attract more people here.
After years of such cycles, Fear Oil grew stronger and stronger.
Given time, it might eventually grow to a completely uncontrollable extent!
...
On the underground steps, the Fear Oil-condensed Vale Valetti—also the soul and consciousness trapped inside the Fear Oil—told Lin Yu and Furbollo the "truth" of Extreme Winter Mountain.
"What a story fitting the style of the 'Truth Corporation,'" Furbollo sighed, "No wonder we didn't see any real monsters along the way."
Lin Yu also nodded slightly.
It seemed that the promotion task wanted him to find the "scam" and the "fraudster"…
It should correspond to the plan called "Chate" and the entire "Truth Corporation."
But...
Lin Yu still had questions.
He looked at Vale Valetti before him and asked.
"You told us all this and guided me here—what exactly is your purpose?"
Vale Valetti looked at Lin Yu, his gaze burning as he spoke.
"I said before... you are very clever, the smartest person I've seen come to Extreme Winter Mountain."
"So, I believe you have hope to 'end' all of this!"

chapters.title: Chapter 100: The Deal
chapters.content:
"Me? 'End' all this?"
Lin Yu frowned upon hearing this.
"But what exactly do you want me to do?"
He asked softly.
Before Vale Valetti could respond, Furbollo started shouting.
"Why are you only talking to May? And saying he's the smartest..."
"Am I not qualified enough?!"
Furbollo complained indignantly.
Vale Valetti glanced at Furbollo with a slight frown.
"You? You do have some intelligence... but to end this 'monster' created by the company, you can't do it. Only he can!"Hearing this, Furbollo's expression softened slightly but still couldn't hide his irritation.
"Of course I'm intelligent—but your condescending attitude is definitely suspicious!"
Furbollo looked at Lin Yu with a serious expression.
"May, I think this guy might not be trustworthy—he's also a Truth Corporation employee, and B-3 isn't a low rank... There are four clearance levels: A, B, C, D, each with three sub-levels!"
"He's practically management already. We can't trust his words!"
"This guy might just be trying to trick you into dying!"
As Furbollo spoke, Lin Yu nodded.
Though there was some emotional bias in his words, Lin Yu understood...
Furbollo's reasoning was logical and based on rational analysis.
In truth, Lin Yu didn't completely trust Vale Valetti either.
He looked at the researcher and sighed.
"Honestly, I do have doubts about you..."
Vale Valetti wasn't surprised: "I understand. After all, I appear to share origins with this monster—even coming from the 'company' that created this tragedy. Whether I side with the monster or the company... there are many possibilities that I might be 'malicious'."
"But I can only beg you to trust me!"
He said earnestly.
"Time... is truly running out!"
Vale Valetti's words left Lin Yu and Furbollo confused.
"What do you mean time is running out?"
Furbollo asked urgently.
"It has grown to a 'terrifying' degree. Your arrival here has already alerted it," Vale Valetti explained. "Soon, it will forcibly activate the 'Dream Manufacturing Device'... Now, it can already control some instruments here!"
"Once that starts, you'll all be trapped in the nightmares it creates—including the other survivors who appeared with you on Extreme Winter Mountain!"
"We have at most two or three minutes before activation begins!"
As Vale Valetti spoke, Lin Yu's expression changed.
"So this monster has basically come to life already?"
Hearing this, Vale Valetti looked at Lin Yu again.
For the first time, the researcher's face showed hesitation.
Finally, as if making up his mind, he spoke.
"Fine, I'll tell you—it hasn't truly come to life yet. It's just acting through a collective consciousness formed from 'devoured souls'... but you're right about its goal—to obtain 'true life'!"
"This thing wants to digest and integrate all souls to create its own true soul and life."
"To achieve this, it needs to devour more souls!"
"And once it truly 'comes to life,' transitioning from simulated consciousness to a real biological entity... it can completely detach from these instruments and—most likely gain 'intelligence' from the consumed souls!"
"At that point, none of us can predict what it might do!"
As Vale Valetti spoke, Furbollo and Lin Yu exchanged glances.
"This is insane!"
Furbollo muttered.
"I see," Lin Yu exhaled. "That explains everything!"
"But I still have one final question—why must it be me? And what exactly do I need to do?"
"Is it just because of 'that thing' on me?"
Lin Yu asked.
Vale Valetti nodded.
"Yes. What you need to do next... is find this monster's true form within the 'dream.'"
"Destroying it in reality isn't simple. Now, it's bound to the underground base beneath Extreme Winter Mountain. To destroy it, you'd have to destroy the entire base!"
"But in the dream, what manifests are the consciousness forms of the devoured and imprisoned souls."
