Lin Yu pretended to startle defensively, standing up while maintaining a guarded posture even after recognizing Li Nian.
He proactively took out the Bone Crusher and placed it by the riverbank.
"You can have the hammer... Will you let me go?"
Li Nian seemed genuinely surprised by his action.
Then she spat in annoyance.
"Tch! I lost!"
Seeing her reaction, Lin Yu acted even more nervous.
"What? Are you going to kill me here?"
Li Nian tilted her head. "Huh? I wasn't planning to kill you!"
"Then how did you find me here?!" Lin Yu shouted agitatedly.
Li Nian grinned and said breezily, "Well... intuition!"
Hearing this, even veteran actor Lin Yu—who had orchestrated this entire scenario—almost burst out laughing.
Of course Li Nian had found the location—he'd sent it as Zhu Ming.
"Heavenly Artisan will appear here—now's the best time to negotiate with him. Want to bet he'll hand over the [item] voluntarily?"
That's why Li Nian had spat in frustration after Lin Yu's first line.
Though she hadn't replied to Zhu Ming, she'd tacitly accepted the wager in her heart.
"What kind of intuition is that?" Lin Yu continued playing Heavenly Artisan on the verge of a breakdown.
"I've never offended your Free Alliance... Why won't you or that veterinarian leave me alone?!"
"I came to Jiangcheng just to negotiate with you—you weren't even my main target! Why are you doing this to me!"
His hysterical performance even made Li Nian feel somewhat guilty.
The Master Thief scratched her head and offered a weak excuse:
"Well... actually that 'veterinarian' isn't officially one of us yet."
"A reserve member? That's what she called herself too—this isn't funny!" Lin Yu said indignantly in Heavenly Artisan's voice.
"I've never heard of the Free Alliance having peripheral members or reserves!"

chapters.title: Chapter 130: Scriptwriter, Director, and Actor All in One
chapters.content:
As Lin Yu, playing the role of Heavenly Artisan, displayed extreme indignation with an attitude of "do whatever you want to me," even the usually malicious Li Nian found her imposing manner weakening somewhat.
Especially since from Heavenly Artisan's statements, she had indirectly deduced what had happened to him.
It seemed many of the Marauders who came from Zheng City had died or been injured—nearly wiped out?
This inevitably made Li Nian inwardly suspicious while also marveling at Zhu Ming's strength.
"That 'Veterinarian' sister said she offended two organizations at once—seems she wasn't joking."
"And...to actually track me down at my doorstep, her skills are indeed extraordinary."
To have killed so many people without even undergoing Promotion, and even pushed a First-Tier like Heavenly Artisan into a corner!
According to Heavenly Artisan's account, it wasn't just him—another First-Tier member of the Marauders had even died.
This was enough to show just how formidable and ruthless this "Veterinarian" was.
Moreover, even though Li Nian herself hadn't gained any substantial benefits, with Heavenly Artisan now accusing her with an attitude of "you local gangs have absolutely no manners," she couldn't say much in response.She was in the wrong here—Li Nian had given Zhu Ming the nod to "handle" this matter.
And Zhu Ming was indeed a reserve member of the Free Alliance.
Li Nian had simply underestimated Zhu Ming's ferocity—she'd thought the Veterinarian would go to negotiate.
Who could have guessed she'd just straight up slaughter them all!
Thus, not wanting to completely sever ties with the Marauders, Li Nian could only laugh it off awkwardly.
"Ah, you know how it is—we Free Alliance members don't interfere with each other's actions."
"How about this: I won't take the hammer—let's each take a step back, and you keep this quiet, alright?"
Li Nian said with a grin, "After all, it wouldn't sound good for your Marauders to have been taken down single-handedly by one of our Free Alliance members, would it?"
"What do you mean single-handedly? She colluded with your local Jiangcheng organization—and that damn 'Doctor' who came to Zheng City to mess with me!"
"Heavenly Artisan"—that is, Lin Yu—interrupted Li Nian again, speaking indignantly.
Li Nian was startled once more, her evaluation of Zhu Ming rising another notch.
She cleared her throat lightly, "Well...whether you believe it or not, she technically hasn't officially joined the Free Alliance yet."
"How about this: I'll arrange compensation through organizational channels for your fallen comrades. Sound good?"
Li Nian took another step back.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NovᴇlFirenᴇt
Then, she added a veiled threat: "I don't want to escalate this, but...the only reason I'm being so polite right now is precisely because I don't want things to escalate."
After she finished speaking, Lin Yu's expression softened slightly.
"Fine, we'll do it your way."
"This...was simply a case of our skills being inferior!"
Having said this, Lin Yu turned and walked toward the riverside street, taking out his phone.
A short while later, a business car quickly reversed back down the road.
Almond rolled down the window, speaking urgently.
"Get in quick—if you'd messaged any later, I'd have been on the highway already."
"Didn't expect you to still be alive!"
Heavenly Artisan said nothing more. After getting in the car, he slumped into the passenger seat, his clothes still damp.
"I underestimated how dangerous Jiangcheng is," Lin Yu murmured. "They're all dead...that woman was like a monster."
Hearing this, Almond's expression turned grim as well.
"I also ran into someone in a white coat...claimed to be a Free Alliance reserve member."
"That's her," Lin Yu said bitterly. "The most cunning and treacherous opponent I've ever faced—but at least I escaped."
"And just now, I met Master Thief!"
Almond looked even more surprised. "You met Master Thief too?"
"Is this some Free Alliance scheme?"
Lin Yu gave a pained smile. "Probably not, since she let me go and seemed unaware of the whole thing...I didn't see any other Free Alliance members on the boat either."
"Instead, I ran into a local Jiangcheng 'Thief' and that 'Doctor' who attacked me before."
Having said this, Lin Yu closed his eyes.
"Drop me off somewhere up ahead."
He exhaled deeply as he spoke.
Almond was astonished. "You want to stay in Jiangcheng? Have you lost your mind?!"
"I was the one who brought them here—Red Fuji, Little Ice, A-Kang, Ming-Zai," Lin Yu said, guilt flashing across his face. "Red Fuji...he was one of the few people I could call a friend, like you."
"I wasn't as close with Little Ice, A-Kang or Ming-Zai before, but...they died right in front of me, Almond. Do you know—when Little Ice died, Ming-Zai went mad trying to avenge her."
"That kid must have liked her, huh?"
Lin Yu took a deep breath, then let it out slowly. "I thought after joining the Death Game, I'd become numb to death...how ironic. I even joined the Marauders and killed indiscriminately for revenge."
"But when they died before my eyes, I couldn't just remain cold and detached."
He spoke with self-mockery.
Almond stayed silent for a moment before giving Heavenly Artisan a gentle pat.
"It's not your fault. From the moment we joined the Death Game, we were all just struggling to survive anyway."
"I know, but precisely because of that...thinking how they fought tooth and nail to survive dungeon after dungeon, it makes it even harder to accept."
Lin Yu's voice grew quiet. "During my talk with Master Thief just now, she said...they'd offer compensation."
"Probably through organizational channels."
"But...I can't just let this go. I'm staying in Jiangcheng."
Almond stepped on the brake.
The car came to a smooth stop by the roadside.
Almond hadn't been driving fast to begin with.
At this speed, even with a sudden stop, the high-end business car remained perfectly stable.
"I won't stop you—we're not close enough for me to interfere with your decisions. But what exactly can you do staying in Jiangcheng?"
"Get revenge?"
Almond asked.
"I only joined the Marauders for revenge in the first place," Lin Yu said, opening the car door. "Now with this new grudge...I actually feel motivated again."
"Those three—I've already memorized them."
"The debt for burning down the house, the debt for killing my friends—I'll repay every last bit someday."
After Lin Yu finished speaking, Almond in the car let out a long sigh.
"Fine, I respect your choice."
"I'll report everything here truthfully to the boss...honestly, he probably won't blame you either."
"After all, the Free Alliance got involved..."
Then, the business car's taillights disappeared into the night.
Lin Yu watched Almond drive away, then exhaled in relief.
"Finally over..."
"Scriptwriter, director, and actor all in one—playing multiple roles is exciting, but damn exhausting!"

chapters.title: Chapter 131: Gains and Investigations into the Psychological Society
chapters.content:
After bidding farewell to Almond, Lin Yu deactivated the effects of [False Face] and returned to his original appearance. At a street corner in Jiangcheng's urban area, Lin Yu retrieved a black plastic bag from a red bucket outside a closed milk tea shop. Inside was a notebook containing an anonymous cryptocurrency account provided by the [Hunters' Association].
Lin Yu sold the cryptocurrency from that account and transferred out 1.04 million yuan as payment. Next, he went to a food delivery locker outside an upscale residential complex. Entering the pickup code from the [Hunters' Association] backend system, he retrieved what appeared to be a food delivery bag - but inside were four gold bars worth 120,000 yuan in total.
The 1.04 million belonged to Zhu Ming, while the 120,000 was Old Yao's share. With the heavy gold bars in hand and his bank balance updated, Lin Yu genuinely felt for the first time... "A loss may turn out to be a gain." Perhaps the [Death Game] wasn't so bad after all—at least it truly could make money.
The series of performances starting from Zheng City weren't just Lin Yu indulging his theatrical impulses. There were real, tangible benefits involved. But... Lin Yu wasn't solely motivated by money or equipment. While wealth was undoubtedly important, Lin Yu understood clearly...ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ
Even a sum like one million yuan—an "astronomical figure" to ordinary people—wasn't worth the tremendous risks he'd taken. If money were truly his only goal, he could have simply lured those people to Jiangcheng under the identity of [Heavenly Artisan] and killed them. There would have been no need to make separate impressions on Tycoon and A Nian.
Ever since learning he was being watched by both the [Psychological Society] and [Free Alliance], Lin Yu had maintained a strong sense of crisis. Therefore, to quickly enhance his strength and gather more information, Lin Yu chose to join as many organizations as possible while creating different false identities.
But Lin Yu didn't plan to just lurk quietly with each identity. So... whether it was [Old Yao], [Zhu Ming], [May May], or even the now-established [Heavenly Artisan] persona, Lin Yu intended to further elevate their visibility. Admittedly, this somewhat increased the risk of exposure... but the potential rewards were equally high.
As time passed with him maintaining the [Fraudster] Unique Class, Lin Yu gradually discerned the patterns behind [Manifestation]. This ability required [Belief] to activate [Manifestation]—and [Belief] could disappear not just through lies being exposed. Beyond [Exposure], there was also [Forgetting].
This explained why most [Manifestations] had time limits. Because [Belief] wasn't permanent—he had deceived Li Nian and Tycoon into believing his class was [Soldier], but these two wouldn't constantly remember "Lin Yu is a Soldier." They needed to see him again and be "reminded" to recall it.
This was something Lin Yu discovered after selling counterfeit equipment. Because Lin Yu could sense that the [Belief] about those fake props he'd sold never completely disappeared. Whenever the players who purchased those items used them, they would see the "fake equipment," effectively continuously maintaining belief in Lin Yu's lies.From this, Lin Yu developed a hypothesis about the [Fraudster] ability: When a lie was frequently recalled by many people and became akin to [Truth], could he then obtain a permanently effective [Manifestation]? Based on this, Lin Yu formed a fundamental understanding regarding his "false identities."
He needed to make many useful false identities "widely renowned." By leaving deep impressions on everyone who encountered them, whenever he used those identities, he could still access their class abilities even when alone. And the best way to leave lasting impressions on organizations and other players... was through performances.
A spectacular performance that connected all his current false identities. Now, it wasn't just Li Nian remembering Zhu Ming, Almond gaining deeper understanding of Heavenly Artisan, Tycoon developing more trust in Old Yao, or [Order] taking slight notice of May. Beyond their direct interactions with specific false identities, these people now had impressions of Lin Yu's other personas too.
Take Li Nian—she had now met Lin Yu's version of Heavenly Artisan and knew about both the Old Yao and May identities. Tycoon had also learned about Zhu Ming and May, forming preliminary impressions. As for Almond, while developing deeper connections with Heavenly Artisan, she probably wouldn't forget Zhu Ming either.
When these people recounted events from their respective perspectives to members of their organizations... The distinctive traits Lin Yu performed through these identities would leave memory imprints in those members' minds. After future cross-referencing... Even those who hadn't witnessed Lin Yu's performances firsthand would likely become utterly convinced of these fictional or deceased "players'" existence!
Moreover, Lin Yu had deliberately revealed that his various identities had "connections" with each other. This way, if anyone noticed similarities between his personas, they would be guided toward these pre-established "facts." "You mean Zhu Ming and Old Yao? Oh, I heard they actually knew each other! Even collaborated once!" Though no one had actually witnessed their collaboration, once such "facts" circulated repeatedly in rumors, everyone would develop an impression that "they definitely appeared together before."
This was another layer of insurance Lin Yu created for himself—making it nearly impossible for anyone to uncover his false identities. Even if one was exposed, the others would remain secure. "What's next is accumulating strength... and..." "Attempting to investigate the [Psychological Society]."
Carrying the gold bars, Lin Yu returned home. It was already late at night. Lin Zhao had gone to sleep—she'd recently started getting somewhat accustomed to Lin Yu frequently not coming home. Lin Yu had provided reasonably convincing excuses: "The advertising business has been picking up lately." Though Lin Zhao was his elder sister, her mentality in certain aspects mirrored that of typical Chinese parents.
While normally insisting on curfews, once "career" or "studies" were involved, overnight absences became acceptable. Especially after Lin Yu handed over part of his earnings, prompting Lin Zhao to remark "Little Yu has really grown up" without further questioning. After some thought, Lin Yu quietly left another 20,000 yuan in cash on the dining table for his sleeping sister.
Then he retreated to his bedroom, opened the phone registered to May, and sent a private message through the [forum] backend to user ID [Furbollo]: "I heard you were previously investigating the [Psychological Society]?"

chapters.title: Chapter 132: The Psychological Society, Fluoxetine
chapters.content:
Normally, it would be impossible for Lin Yu to get Fu Luo's help in investigating the 'Psychological Society'.
But since the identity of 'May May' was now considered a "trustworthy" partner in Fu Luo's eyes...
Lin Yu obtained the information he wanted from Fu Luo two days later.
The data on the 'Psychological Society' wasn't actually hard to find. These people didn't seem to operate discreetly or make particular efforts to conceal themselves.
Within 'Jiang'an Hall', Lin Yu could already find basic introductions about the 'Psychological Society's situation.
The organization's structure matched its name—it resembled an "academic society".
Like some university-affiliated scholarly group.
Its highest leadership consisted of a five-member "Council", with three subordinate divisions: the "Professional Committee", "Regional Branches", and "Execution Department".
Members of the "Professional Committee" were restricted to those with the professions 『Doctor』, 『Nurse』, 『Scholar』, and 『Student』. Most members had real-world experience or academic backgrounds in psychology.
The "Regional Branches" comprised local members without profession restrictions, most of whom seemed to conduct surveillance operations for the 'Psychological Society'.As for the "Execution Department"... it functioned similarly to squads in the Order, primarily handling operations and combat.
Currently, three known high-ranking representatives in the 'Psychological Society's Council had codenames:
『Jung』, 『Lacan』, and 『Wundt』.
This portion of Jiang'an Hall's records came from the Tycoon himself—six months ago, he had a direct encounter with 『Lacan』 in a dungeon.
The other party didn't conceal his identity, openly announcing his codename.
That dungeon had twenty participants, making it exceptionally large-scale.
Moreover, those capable of participating alongside the Tycoon and Lacan were far from novices or rookies.
Yet in the end...
Only the Tycoon and Lacan survived.
The Tycoon provided an assessment of Lacan's strength:
"Absolutely ranked within the top thirty on the leaderboard."
He didn't elaborate in detail about what happened inside the dungeon.
But he clearly stated that Lacan had deliberately—without necessity—directly and indirectly caused the deaths of every other player in what should have been a cooperative 『Slaughter』-type dungeon.
The motive was...
"Screening and Cultivation."
This was also the 'Psychological Society's creed.
Just as they had killed Lin Yu—these lunatics' goal seemed to be using near-coercive methods to produce more powerful players.
In reality, they collected data through their "Regional Branches" and delivered it to the "Professional Committee". The Committee used certain "assessment methods" to screen individuals with "potential".
The 'Psychological Society' would then send invitations to those who had already become players—regardless of whether they belonged to other organizations.
As for those who weren't players yet...
The 'Psychological Society' would dispatch members to kill them. Only after confirming their entry into the 『Death Game』 would they extend an invitation.
Such insane methods were enough to make many players seethe with hatred.
Within the game, inside dungeons...
Members of this organization were universally despised!
Because there was a high probability they would intentionally increase other players' difficulty.
In 『Competition』 dungeons, they attacked both allies and enemies alike... In normal dungeons, they would outright assist monsters or game rules in killing players.
Typically before a dungeon concluded, they would reveal their identities—and invite outstanding 『Players』 from that session to join their organization.
But...
Whether the invitees joined or not, these people didn't seem to care.
Of course, there was also a very, very small chance that 'Psychological Society' members might help other players.
But the conditions were extremely stringent—apparently only when they believed a "high-potential" player encountered challenges or predicaments far beyond their current capabilities that would stifle their growth would they stand on the player's side.Google seaʀᴄh NovᴇlFirenᴇt
Thus, what most players least wanted to encounter in dungeons...
Was neither the 『Marauders』 nor members of the 『Free Alliance』, but people from the 『Psychological Society』.
Most 『Marauders』 members only coveted your items and employed ruthless methods—in cooperative dungeons, as long as you didn't flaunt wealth or obstruct them, surface-level peace could be maintained.
The 『Free Alliance』 had few members, and currently known members were eccentric—though they might inexplicably target you sometimes, the odds were fifty-fifty.
Only the 『Psychological Society』—if encountered in a dungeon, there was a 99% chance they were there to harm others.
Apart from the Tycoon's personal experience, the above information was compiled from the blood and tears of numerous 'Psychological Society' victims. It wasn't just publicly known within 『Jiang'an Hall』—most righteous organizations were also aware.
In fact, many 'Psychological Society' members, though their codenames were unknown, had their basic information recorded in files.
Yet Lin Yu still chose to have Fu Luo investigate...
Naturally because what he sought wasn't among the known information.
Lin Yu combed through all relevant documents but found no records of that beautiful girl who claimed to be his junior.
Fortunately, Fu Luo's reputation as the 『Detective』 was well-deserved.
What Lin Yu provided him were only a sketch based on memory and vague keywords like "young", "female", and "uses a Beretta M9".
"I don't know why you're investigating this, but buddy, she's really dangerous."
"She's more dangerous than your average 'Psychological Society' member!"
"If it weren't for your request, I'd never look into this—you're just a fucking First-Tier, I suggest not provoking monsters of this caliber."
Ignoring Fu Luo's stream of warnings, Lin Yu sighed and opened the encrypted file sent to him.
"I didn't provoke her... she came after me..."
After decryption, a brief document appeared before Lin Yu:
"Codenamed 『Fluoxetine』, Profession 『Assassin』, 'Psychological Society' Execution Department S-Class Specialist."
Execution Department S-Class Specialist...
Lin Yu instantly understood why her information was so hard to find and why Fu Luo was so nervous.
This truly wasn't data ordinary players should access.
Members of the 'Psychological Society' at this level could be considered equivalents to the Order's "Regional Administrators"—they didn't participate in organizational decisions, but...
They were extremely mysterious and exceptionally formidable.
Currently, the 'Psychological Society' might only have three S-Class Specialists—even fewer than their highest Council members.
The attached photo of the hooded girl seemed extracted from some surveillance footage, extremely blurry.
But that beautiful, sharply-defined, delicate yet cold face...
Lin Yu would recognize it even through the fuzziness.
"So that's it... your name is 『Fluoxetine』..."
Lin Yu murmured.
Now he knew her codename, profession, and rank.
Though this was all he had, for Lin Yu, it was enough.
Next—
He would personally verify these details and uncover more about this girl.
"I hope you're strong enough."
"Otherwise... the next performance prepared for you will be terribly boring."

chapters.title: Chapter 133: New Dungeon, Trembling Heights!
chapters.content:
Tuesday night.
After several days of brewing, just as Lin Yu had anticipated...
His various fake identities had gradually sparked discussions among the player community.
Especially 'May May'.
Upon opening the forum, posts about 'May May' could be directly found among the relatively high-traffic recent discussions.
"Who exactly is this new 'Doctor' player in Zheng City who made the 'Marauders' suffer heavy losses?"
To distinguish him from a somewhat famous 'Assassin' in 'Order', forum players affectionately nicknamed Lin Yu "Doctor May".
"Brothers, I have inside info from 'Order'—this guy came to Zheng City from another province specifically to target Heavenly Artisan and claim the bounty!"
"So reckless! I heard Heavenly Artisan was severely injured by him! The 'Marauders' lost several experts!"
"That's just a rumor. I'm from 'Central Plains' in Zheng City—basically all Zheng City players know Heavenly Artisan escaped.""Right, because of this, 'Marauders' and 'Order' in Zheng City almost went to full-scale war."
"Upstairs, I'm not talking about Zheng City. Later, Heavenly Artisan went to Jiangcheng for revenge and apparently got wrecked!"
"Yeah, he's from Jiangcheng. He teamed up with local organizations and wiped out all the 'Marauders' from Zheng City."
"This madman... I wonder which organization he'll join eventually?"
"Most likely 'Jiang'an Hall'—hasn't he already cooperated with them?"
"With how unorthodox he is, he might join one of those illegal organizations."
"Maybe he's already in one!"
"Hey, stop talking nonsense! May is my good buddy. He hasn't joined any org yet, but he's very interested in 'Order'. I was there when he took down Heavenly Artisan—later, 'Order' members who arrived spoke highly of him. Do you understand the weight of that? After a few more dungeons, he could probably join 'Order' directly!"
"Furbollo at it again with his know-it-all act."
"Furbollo, you're buddy-buddy with him again? Such a clout-chaser!"
"F*ck you all, jealous of my connection with him? I was the one who helped him track down Heavenly Artisan's location!"
"Admin Warning: User 'Furbollo' has used inappropriate language. 10 reputation points deducted, 1 point penalty!"
The discussion continued, with everyone speculating which organization this berserk 'Doctor' would join.
Amid the chaos, they also took the opportunity to insult a certain 'Detective' who came to lecture everyone.
Lin Yu sighed, feeling Furbollo didn't deserve this.
After all, Furbollo was telling the truth.
"Still, this guy's an idiot. Couldn't he just screenshot our private chat as proof?"
He'd just privately messaged him a few days ago to investigate 'Psychological Society' members.
Even if worried about exposing that, he could've blurred sensitive parts.
Lin Yu couldn't help but lament.
Though Fu Luo was extremely sharp and perceptive in certain aspects...
Most of the time, he was a complete moron.
However, thanks to Fu Luo, the post's popularity soared higher.
Those sparse strands of 'belief' from distant sources continuously gathered, ultimately allowing Lin Yu to confirm his hypothesis.
He could now indeed freely use the abilities of the 'May May' identity.
Not just the professional skills of a 'Doctor'—by using [Counterfeit] to transform into a [Syringe], he could even access advanced professional abilities.
It was foreseeable... as his various identities grew more renowned, the number of abilities he could use would likely increase.
Regarding this, Lin Yu couldn't help but remark:
"How is this balanced?"
He turned off his phone—it was almost midnight.
Lin Yu stood up, tightening his hoodie as the night wind seeped through, bringing a slight chill.
Summer was approaching in Jiangcheng, and even nights weren't too cold on clear days.
The main reason Lin Yu felt cold now was...
He stood atop one of Jiangcheng's tallest buildings.
"Shengjiang Tower"—completed five years ago, reaching 400 meters in height—was a multifunctional office building housing numerous companies.
Unlike this year's trend of oddly shaped skyscrapers, Shengjiang Tower had a simple, square design with glass curtain walls, giving it an imposing presence.
Its top-floor rooftop featured a public garden, observation deck, and helipad.
Of course, none of these were open at midnight.
But money talks.
By booking an expensive suite at the tower's luxury hotel, Lin Yu obtained an elevator card granting direct rooftop access.
After all, the floor below the rooftop housed the hotel's 24-hour restaurant and bar.
Once at the bar, finding the emergency stairwell to the rooftop and unlocking the fire exit door wasn't difficult.
Lin Yu hadn't come here at midnight for fun, sightseeing, or thrills.
He approached the rooftop edge, effortlessly vaulting over the chest-high railing.
Outside was a sturdy metal mesh structure wide enough to stand on—Lin Yu looked down.
The 400-meter drop made the ground nearly invisible, only revealing Jiangcheng's brightly lit streets bustling with traffic below.
Lin Yu took a deep breath.
"This does make me curious... how exactly will the 'Death Game' keep me 'safe and sound'..."
He murmured, staring at the vivid blood-red text before him:
『Less than 24 hours remain until the latest possible start time for the next game!』
『Before midnight tonight, between 11:50 PM and 12:00 AM, perform free-fall from a height exceeding 100 meters above ground to enter the game.』
The height beneath his feet, the cold wind against his skin, and the trembling metal grid all sent shivers through Lin Yu.
Even after "dying" many times, he still felt faint traces of fear.
The clock struck 11:59—
Lin Yu stepped forward, spreading his arms as he plummeted toward the ground below.
During the fall, Lin Yu felt his adrenaline surge.
The roaring wind, the approaching ground, and the weightlessness made him reflect:
"This is definitely the most thrilling near-death experience yet."
He swept his hands across his face—[False Face] activated, rapidly altering his features and physique.
Just as Lin Yu was about to hit the ground—Follow current novels on
【Entering game—】
【Game Title: Banquet in the Skies】
【Clear Condition: Survive until the banquet concludes.】
【Current game players: 7】
"Whoosh—"
Everything went black, and the ground that should've shattered his body vanished.
In its place appeared even greater heights!

chapters.title: Chapter 134: The Banquet Begins, Self-Introductions
chapters.content:
The fall continued!
Lin Yu opened his eyes and looked around.
The icy wind was several times stronger than before, and below was a vast expanse of pitch-black, churning ocean.
Falling alongside him were six other figures—likely the other players.
"What's the deal with this dungeon?"
Lin Yu thought rapidly.
Just as he was pondering...
"Thud!"
The descent abruptly stopped!
He landed on a chair—more accurately, a chair caught Lin Yu!The soft leather-cushioned wooden chair miraculously absorbed almost all the impact of the fall, leaving Lin Yu feeling no pain whatsoever!
Then, he surveyed his surroundings once more.
They were still suspended hundreds of meters in the air—besides him, the other six figures were also seated on different chairs.
These chairs swayed mid-air, each tied at its four corners with ropes that extended upward, seemingly reaching the heavens.
Then...
A white round table tied with seven ropes descended from the sky, coming to a steady halt before the group.
On the table were porcelain bone plates, and...
In the central pool on the table stood a massive red octopus emerging from the water.
The red octopus wore a chef's hat, its eight tentacles spread out.
"Welcome! Welcome—welcome, honored guests! Welcome, visitors and players from other worlds!"
"Welcome to this banquet hosted by my supreme master, the 'God of Banquets, Wine, and Revelry'!"
The red octopus spoke in a cheerful yet solemn voice, its deep tone resembling a resonant bass, like a radio host delivering holiday greetings.
"I am the host of this banquet, the head chef, the banquet manager, and the security chief—Ka!"
"Honored guests, dear guests, I hope you all enjoy this banquet, and..."
One of the octopus's tentacles lifted its tall white chef's hat, while the remaining seven tentacles grabbed utensils from beneath the hat and flung them toward the seven!
"Swish!"
The sharp knives and forks embedded precisely into the table before each person, mere centimeters away from them.
Lin Yu examined the still-quivering utensils before him and realized one thing.
"This cooked-looking octopus is pretty strong..."
Then, the red octopus "Ka" adjusted its chef's hat.
"...and I also hope you can survive until the banquet's end."
After saying this, its tentacles reached beneath the pool and retrieved a piece of cardboard.
"Anyway, to help you all survive this revelrous banquet, I have some small banquet rules I hope you'll follow!"
At this point, Lin Yu straightened his posture.
The main event was here.
This was the game's rule segment.
The octopus then began reciting the rules.
"First—you are all here as honored guests chosen by my master. Unless permitted by my master, no attacks are allowed between you."
Hearing this rule, Lin Yu nodded slightly.
No attacks allowed? That likely meant this wasn't a 'Competition'-type dungeon.
Even if it were a 'Competition' type, it probably didn't involve direct player slaughter.
After the octopus finished this rule, Lin Yu heard a soft "Tch" from beside him.
Lin Yu glanced sideways and saw a gaunt man in a Tang suit with tortoiseshell-framed glasses wearing a displeased expression.
Not just him—directly across from Lin Yu, a girl with light yellow hair, adorned with bright accessories and dressed flamboyantly, also muttered in disappointment.
Judging by her lips, it was probably "What a shame."
After "Ka" finished speaking, it paused briefly before continuing.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
"Second... since this is a banquet, though some dishes might not suit your tastes, I hope you won't waste food and will finish each course seriously. Otherwise—you might face some penalties."
Hearing this, Lin Yu narrowed his eyes.
"Seems like a 'Survival'-type dungeon. Probably some dishes will be challenging to eat or something."
"Finally, the most important rule—please follow the dining etiquette I remind you of while enjoying the food and banquet, doing what's required at each stage... otherwise, I'll have to do things none of you will enjoy."
"Of course, as the banquet host, aside from punishing impolite guests, I'll also provide timely assistance and rewards to those who perform well."
By the time "Ka" finished, Lin Yu had already pieced together the dungeon's premise.
Basically, eating various challenging foods under bizarre requirements.
Whether those foods were extremely hard, scalding hot, or disgustingly awful...
Lin Yu didn't know yet.
And "Ka" showed no intention of revealing that yet.
It tossed the cardboard back into the pool, rotated its head 360 degrees to observe each player's face, then said:
"Alright, everyone... I must go prepare the ingredients now—next is your self-introduction and mingling session."
"I hope you all get along!"
With that...
"Ka" gathered its eight tentacles and sprang like a coil from the pool at the table's center, soaring into the sky.
After it left...
The gaunt thirty-something man in the Tang suit and tortoiseshell glasses to Lin Yu's left spoke.
"Well, everyone... though I know some of you, since the octopus said no attacks and wants us to introduce ourselves... let's maintain peace for now."
"Shall we introduce ourselves in order, starting from me and going clockwise?"
As the man spoke, the light-haired girl across from Lin Yu propped her feet on the table: "Whatever."
Ignoring her prickly tone, the Tang-suited man adjusted his glasses with his middle finger: "Let me introduce myself. I'm a member of 'Order' from Haicheng, also Haicheng's Game Master—codename 'Gambler' Li Hua, profession also 'Gambler'."
Hearing this, Lin Yu was surprised.
Normally, people wouldn't reveal their city or real name.
But this man had the right to!
Haicheng's Game Master, 'Gambler' Li Hua...
Even within 'Order', he was top-tier!
'Gambler' wasn't a Unique Class, just rare.
To use a non-Unique Class as his codename and boldly reveal his real name...
Li Hua's strength spoke for itself!
After speaking, Li Hua gestured to the man on his left.
The man beside Li Hua had the simple, honest appearance of a farmer—dark-skinned with some wrinkles.
He spoke unhurriedly: "My profession is 'Farmer', from the 'Player Mutual Aid Association'. You can call me 'Radish'."
Lin Yu was shocked again.
This "Radish" said he was "from" the 'Player Mutual Aid Association', but in truth—he was one of its founders.
Next, a fair-complexioned man with peach-blossom eyes, resembling a Peking opera female lead but dressed in a tailcoat, smiled.
"Pardon my intrusion..."
He snapped his fingers, and a top hat appeared in his hand, which he placed lightly on his head.
"My humble profession is 'Magician', codename also 'Magician', but you may call me 'Phantom'..."
"From the 'Free Alliance'."

chapters.title: Chapter 135: The Stage of Fate, The Most Suitable Identity
chapters.content:
After the 'Magician' introduced himself, Lin Yu maintained a calm exterior but was inwardly astonished.
"Someone from the 'Free Alliance'?!"
In other words, this guy was in the same organization as Li Nian?
Moreover, the number of players in the 'Free Alliance' was extremely limited...
This 'Magician' Phantom was undoubtedly a top-tier expert.
Adding to that, the previous two introductions of Li Hua and Radish also indicated they were no ordinary characters.
Lin Yu had reason to suspect that all players in this dungeon might have impressive backgrounds.
This was further evidenced by how unfazed the others appeared upon hearing the names Li Hua, Radish, and Phantom.
"I'm just a first-tier rookie who's only completed three dungeons, truly stumbling into a high-level game by mistake," Lin Yu mused inwardly.
The next self-introduction from a female player confirmed Lin Yu's suspicions.The golden-haired girl leaned back with her hands behind her head, completely disregarding their high altitude as she rocked her chair by propping her feet on the table.Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
"I was planning to make up an identity, but with Li Hua and Phantom here, lying would be pointless."
"I'm 'Fish', 'Fish' from the 'Marauders'."
She didn't mention her class.
Li Hua adjusted his glasses and added: "'Fish', deputy head of the 'Marauders' Beijing branch. Class is... Unique Class, 'Freelancer'."
"What's your ability in this dungeon?"
Fish rolled her eyes: "Why should I tell you? Don't think just because this dungeon favors cooperation that I have to play nice with you."
"Refusing to cooperate then," Li Hua remained unperturbed, merely pushing his glasses up again. "Pity. That approach reduces your probability of winning."
Fish spat: "Says who? How do I know you're telling the truth?"
Listening to their exchange, Lin Yu felt even more shocked.
A Unique Class?!
This was the first time he'd encountered another Unique Class player in a dungeon besides himself!
From Li Hua's words, it seemed Fish's abilities weren't fixed?
That sounded similar to his own situation!
And 'Fish' was indeed a renowned expert - Beijing was the headquarters of the 'Marauders'!
Beside Fish, a weathered man in a jacket cleared his throat: "Ahem— everyone, I know your organizations have history, but no need to argue here."
"Given that we're all capable players gathered here for 'cooperation'... plus that octopus earlier mentioned 'gods' and recognized us as 'players' from another world, this dungeon's difficulty must be high."
"I don't recommend fighting among ourselves!"
"Call it giving me face— while I'm an independent player without an organization, the codename 'Mosin-Nagant' should carry some weight, no?"
Lin Yu wasn't surprised.
This man was another celebrity— a veteran player active on forums, famous for writing beginner guides for all players.
But he was more than just a friendly veteran.
Anyone who'd downloaded the popular "Hunters' Association" app knew...
'Mosin-Nagant' was among the strongest known bounty hunters.
One of the few who'd completed million-level bounties solo.
His class was the relatively rare and combat-capable 'Hunter'.
Radish also mediated with a chuckle: "Well said. Young people's tempers are understandable, but we're all veterans... turning against each other before understanding the dungeon's situation is unnecessary."
With these two neutral voices speaking, both Li Hua and Fish backed down from their argument.
Mosin-Nagant gestured to the woman beside him.
She had short hair and wore a dirty white T-shirt with gray sweatpants.
Under everyone's gaze, she nervously adjusted her collar.
"Uh, hello everyone, I'm 'Robin'..."
"'Robin' of the 'Night Watchmen'."
"My class is 'Painter'."
After this rushed introduction, she fell silent.
Radish's eyes lit up: "Robin of the Night Watchmen? Hearing about you pales compared to seeing you!"
"I just had dinner with your colleagues Snowy Owl and Seagull last week! Haha!"
Li Hua also looked relieved.
Lin Yu understood Li Hua's reaction perfectly.
Of the three previous introductions, two were from the 'Free Alliance' and 'Marauders'— opposing factions to 'Order'.
While 'Mosin-Nagant' maintained a friendly forum persona, as a regular bounty hunter, he was dangerous and ungovernable.
Though Radish held high status, Lin Yu had heard the old man wasn't particularly combat-oriented.
His abilities leaned toward support— even logistical supply.
Having 'Robin' the 'Painter' from 'Night Watchmen' here balanced things out.
Judging by Li Hua and Radish's reactions, they'd heard of 'Robin' before.
But Lin Yu hadn't— making her currently the most mysterious person present.
From Mosin-Nagant, Fish and Phantom's expressions, they didn't seem familiar with Robin either.
And 'Robin' appeared uncomfortable with Radish's enthusiasm.
Rubbing her pants nervously, she muttered: "Yes... Snowy Owl and Seagull are nice people..."
"It's just... um..."
Li Hua noticed her discomfort and coughed: "Ahem, let's continue!"
He then looked at Lin Yu beside him.
Seeing Lin Yu's smile, Li Hua looked visibly uneasy.
"Your turn."
Lin Yu observed the six other players' expressions— including 'Fish' from the Marauders and 'Phantom' from the Free Alliance— all wore guarded, wary looks.
They unmistakably recognized Lin Yu's current appearance.
Though before falling, Lin Yu's fabricated "false identity" had been merely an audacious experiment.
Yet fate's coincidence had constructed the perfect stage for this "role".
No...
This dungeon, this stage, might itself be the God of Fate's blessing upon Lin Yu's nearly reckless actions.
"Fine. Since you all seem to recognize me... for your peace of mind, I'll introduce myself properly."
Leaning forward with one hand on the table, he smiled.
"Gentlemen, I am 'Fluoxetine'."
"'Fluoxetine' of the 'Psychological Society'."

chapters.title: Chapter 136: Chaotic Scene, Confrontation and Cooperation
chapters.content:
As Lin Yu's words fell.
An unprecedented abundance of "belief" poured into Lin Yu's body.
He quickly sensed that he had obtained the "Assassin" ability.
And the "Assassin" ability...
belongs to the "Special Type".
The "Assassin" ability is to acquire [Murder Weapons].
Each assassin, upon obtaining their initial profession, receives one more item called [Murder Weapon] than other players.
It could be [Poison], [Blades], [Wire], etc.
Like the [Class Items] obtained through advancement, [Murder Weapons] have the characteristics of being unloseable, unbreakable, and inexhaustible.
Every assassin is different.Moreover, assassins are inherently scarce in number.
Thus, the "Assassin" is also called the "Unique Class among Common Classes".
Thanks to these people seemingly being aware of "Fluoxetine's" identity, Lin Yu sensed that he had also gained a [Murder Weapon] item.
That was Fluoxetine's [Murder Weapon].
Surprisingly, it wasn't the Beretta M9 that Lin Yu had seen before...
but a [Hand Axe].
Of course, this was actually good news for Lin Yu.
If Fluoxetine's [Murder Weapon] was a [Hand Axe], then that meant...
"I can use 'Counterfeit' to disguise it as a [Beretta M9]."
Lin Yu understood this clearly in his heart.
Of course, risk and reward are relative.
Even though "Fluoxetine" made everyone wary, it also meant...
If given the chance, other players present would absolutely try to kill him first!
Thinking of this, Lin Yu couldn't help but feel relieved—fortunately, this was a game where players couldn't fight each other.
Otherwise, even at the risk of exposing [False Face] to these major organizations, he would have had to switch accounts in front of everyone.
But for now...
that wasn't necessary.
He still needed to play the role of "Fluoxetine" well.
After introducing himself, Lin Yu turned his head to glance at Li Hua, who was cautiously watching him.
"Using your 'Gambler' ability to assess me? Haicheng's Game Master?"
He spoke with a smile.
The "Gambler" ability is an "Information Type": when activated, it allows one to see the probability of a certain event occurring.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
The cooldown is relatively fast. Before advancement, it starts with three chances, and a new one is gained every 30 minutes, with a maximum storage of three.
After advancement, the cooldown can be further reduced.
Li Hua adjusted his glasses and shook his head. "No, I didn't waste my ability on you—so far, I've used it twice, verifying the probability of 'Magician' and 'Fish' being willing to cooperate."
"Both exceeded 50%!"
Li Hua said loudly.
This also seemed to give some confidence and hints to Radish and Robin, allies from the same righteous organization.
Upon hearing this, Phantom smiled brightly.
"Gambler, after dealing with each other for so long, you still don't trust me?"
Fish, on the other hand, spat in displeasure.
"Tch..."
Lin Yu's smile widened.
"Oh, then you still have one chance left. Why not check mine?"
"What's the point?" Li Hua said coldly. "Even if I see that you're willing to 'cooperate'... who knows what your definition of 'cooperation' is?"
Robin, standing nearby, also muttered under her breath.
Though her voice was soft, Lin Yu still heard it.
"The behavior of a mentally ill person cannot be predicted."
Hearing their words, Lin Yu gained a deeper understanding of "Fluoxetine."
Indeed, this woman must have done plenty of crazy things.
She was probably the kind even among the members of the "Psychological Society" who was particularly hard to understand.
But...
if it were the real "Fluoxetine," how would she react to these people's words?
After pondering for a moment, Lin Yu smiled and looked at "Robin."
"Thank you for the compliment, but I'm not mentally ill. My mental state is perfectly healthy."
"However... Miss Autism—"
Lin Yu pulled out a pistol from his pocket.
"My behavior truly is unpredictable... guess what, will I use this gun to kill you?"
It wasn't the [Guaranteed-Hit Revolver], but a [Beretta M9] transformed by [Counterfeit].
He aimed the gun at "Robin," and under her suddenly constricted pupils, he sensed a fleeting moment of "belief."
But shortly after...
the "belief" dissipated entirely.
The other party didn't believe the gun in Lin Yu's hand was real!
This surprised Lin Yu greatly.
"It seems this 'Robin' knows 'Fluoxetine' well."
"Perhaps the Beretta M9 isn't a [Game Item], but a real gun 'Fluoxetine' bought?"
"No, or maybe there's another explanation..."
"Because if that were the case, this 'Robin' should look more certain and confident right now."
But she simply stared at the gun barrel, her expression one of confusion.
It seemed she could only confirm that the gun before her was "fake," but she didn't know what exactly it was.
Lin Yu quickly pondered.
However, even if "Robin" didn't believe Lin Yu's words, it didn't matter much.
For Lin Yu, this move was all about playing the role of "Fluoxetine."
At the same time, it was also about...
muddying the waters.
Sure enough, the moment Lin Yu pulled out the gun, the bounty hunter "Mosin-Nagant" instinctively drew his weapon as well.
A short bow appeared in his hand, a sharp arrow nocked and ready, along with a whistle clenched between his teeth.
The short bow was likely his most reliable [Weapon Item].
After all, the "Hunter" ability is an Enhancement Type—boosting eyesight and improving the accuracy of thrown and shot projectiles.
And that whistle... was the hunter's advanced item, [Companion].
When blown, it could summon a hunting animal capable of understanding simple commands to fight for him.
Colloquially known as an "animal friend."
As soon as "Mosin-Nagant" moved, "Fish" beside him also reacted, standing up on her chair and pulling out two flintlock pistols.
One aimed at Lin Yu, the other at Li Hua.
The moment Fish jumped onto the chair, Radish and Phantom also acted—though the two were clearly focused on self-preservation.
Radish pulled out a flowerpot filled with soil from his pocket, shielding himself with it.
Phantom, on the other hand, simply yanked his entire hat downward—and bizarrely, his whole body vanished into the hat before reappearing on the chair.
Fish ignored the two, just grinning as she spoke.
"Hey hey, Sister Nail, let me announce—this round, I drew 'Soldier'..."
"Want to team up with me?"
Hearing the nickname "Sister Nail," Lin Yu was momentarily stunned before realizing.
"Could this be a nickname derived from 'Fluoxetine'?"
"Ting... Nail..."
After thinking, Lin Yu directly replied to Fish, "Sure—I kinda like you anyway."
She chuckled happily.
Fish grinned. "I'll trust you this time, Sister Nail!"
Then, Fish aimed one of her guns at "Robin" as well.

chapters.title: Chapter 137: Pre-Dinner Drinks and the Glass Grabbing Contest
chapters.content:
Fish's reaction was within Lin Yu's expectations.
He had previously noticed that while Fish's gaze held wariness and apprehension toward him, compared to the pure malice she showed when facing Li Hua...
This deputy head of the Marauders didn't seem to harbor obvious or direct hostility toward him.
It was actually quite understandable...
After the forum announced the permanent blacklisting of three organizations - aside from officially labeling them as "heretical cults"...
It had inadvertently created a natural "alliance relationship" between these three groups.
Although the Marauders were selfish, the Free Alliance acted unconventionally, and the Psychological Society was full of utter lunatics...
If they actually encountered Order together...
There was a high probability they would tacitly cooperate to take down Order first.
Sometimes Lin Yu even suspected the forum's move seemed somewhat like "cultivating scorpions in a jar."But regardless...
Now that Lin Yu was Fluoxetine, he could enjoy the benefits of this "natural alliance."
Just then, the ever-calm and steady Li Hua finally spoke up.
"What, are you trying to openly violate the game rules?"
"In a dungeon that might involve 'deities'... you'd really increase your death probability over petty conflicts?"
After Li Hua finished speaking, Lin Yu, fully prepared, immediately responded with a smile:
"But that octopus just mentioned 'banquet rules'..."
"Does the self-introduction session before any dishes are served count as part of the banquet?"
"It even deliberately left - almost like it reserved this time specifically for us to kill each other!"
As Lin Yu spoke, Fish burst into laughter.
"Well said, Sister Nail! I like that reasoning!"
"Hey Gambler... want to make a bet?"
Seeing Lin Yu fanning the flames and Fish's enthusiastic response, Li Hua coldly interjected:
"Don't be ridiculous, I won't gamble!"
He then took out a black signboard slightly larger than a tablet.
Messy handwriting soon appeared on the signboard:
"The current probability of punishment for killing each other now is 100%!"
"I've activated the Gambler's ability," Li Hua said coldly. "This [Signboard] publicly displays a known piece of 'information'... you've heard of it, right?"
"So Fluoxetine, your reasoning is wrong. The self-introduction session is indeed part of the banquet - that octopus leaving might even be entrapment."
After Li Hua finished, Lin Yu and Fish simultaneously showed disappointed expressions.
It was Mosin-Nagant who cheerfully spoke up again:
"Seems like fighting to the death isn't the best option!"
The hunter who had drawn his weapon faster than anyone just moments ago said as if nothing had happened.
"Peace and harmony are wonderful!"
"I love cooperative dungeons like this... even with different organizational allegiances, we can still conquer the game together!"
The Magician Phantom emerged from his hat.
Hearing Mosin-Nagant's words, he couldn't help but comment:
"Oh, gold medal hunter uncle... are you afraid we'll die in the dungeon and you'll miss out on all those bounties?"
Mosin-Nagant responded kindly again:
"Exactly. You're worth nine million, Fish is nine point six million... and Fluoxetine, thirteen million."
"I've got a family to feed, you know."
As Mosin-Nagant spoke, Lin Yu put away his gun and wagged his finger:
"Correction, the Hunters' Association bounty on me should be fifteen point twenty-five million."
This wasn't a random number - Lin Yu had actually checked every Fluoxetine bounty post on the Hunters' app and added them all up.
Fish also jumped down from her chair and sat back, cradling two flintlock pistols:
"Oh ho, Mosin-Nagant, wanna try me outside later?"
Mosin-Nagant waved his hands:
"Wouldn't dare... as deputy head of the Marauders, if you don't isolate yourself or give me a chance to ambush, how would I dare move against you?"
The table conversation remained full of tension.
But everyone had put away their weapons - though the verbal sparring continued, actual fighting was off the table.
Li Hua also sighed in relief.ᴛhis ᴜpdated by NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
Just as everyone "calmed down"...
The octopus Ka descended from above.
Holding several opaque bags in its eight tentacles, it plopped into the pool.
"Ho—everyone! I'm back!"
After surveying the room with its elongated eyes, the octopus cheerfully announced:
"Ah... seems you've all had a lovely chat!"
"A banquet should be joyful, after all."
Then Octopus Ka pulled out six glass cups from the pool.
"Now then... everyone!"
"Please enjoy the 'pre-dinner drinks' - make sure to grab your own glass!"
"The pre-dinner drinks are crucial. I understand if some guests don't wish to drink... but teetotalers are considered 'party poopers' by the host."
"Party poopers will have one of their seat ropes cut!"
After Octopus Ka finished speaking...
It tossed all six glasses high into the air.
Almost instantly, everyone present reacted...
Seven players, six glasses!
At least one person would definitely be punished!
Although this dungeon prohibited direct PvP, it was still a Competition-type!
Lin Yu also realized this.
"Really disadvantageous," he thought, sensing trouble.
The Assassin ability wouldn't help in grabbing glasses.
Looking at his available items:
[Guaranteed-Hit Revolver], [One-Statement Lie Detector], [Teeth of Prophecy], [Tongue of Deceit], [Fear Torch], [Chate's Supplies], [Fear Lens], [Multi-function Screwdriver], [BBE-300], [Safety Helmet (White)], [Bone Crusher]...
Plus [Class Item - False Face] and [Class Item - Counterfeit].
None of these would help in grabbing a glass.
Well, the [Teeth of Prophecy] and [Tongue of Deceit] could be useful, but Lin Yu hesitated to waste them here.
"Guess it's down to quick reflexes?"
As Lin Yu pondered, Mosin-Nagant was already making his move.
He blew a dog whistle, summoning a small hunting dog from thin air.
The dog leapt high, easily catching a glass midair and delivering it to Mosin-Nagant!
The number of remaining glasses...
Now dropped to five!
Meaning the "competition" just got fiercer!

chapters.title: Chapter 138: Robin
chapters.content:
After Mosin-Nagant made his move, Li Hua immediately sprang into action as well.Thɪs ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
He took out a copper coin from his pocket and flicked it toward the cup in midair.
"Ding!"
The coin struck the cup with a crisp sound.
Then, incredibly, one of the cups changed its trajectory unnaturally from the impact, spinning through the air alongside the gold coin before landing perfectly in Li Hua's hand.
This was the second claimed cup!
Phantom also moved. He simply removed his hat with one hand and reached inside...
One of the airborne cups vanished into thin air, only to reappear as he pulled it from his hat.
Fish's approach was more straightforward. She simply stood up from her chair again and produced a fishing net to scoop up a cup.
Next, Radish employed a similar method—the old farmer remained seated like a mountain, producing a ridiculous sticky-hand toy.The fluorescent green rubber hand shot out and snatched a cup back.
All this happened within mere seconds.
Lin Yu felt he'd only taken a few breaths when suddenly only one cup remained on the field!
"Is this what high-level play looks like?"
Yet at this point, Lin Yu found himself unexpectedly calm.
Given the current situation...
Rather than frantically competing with Robin for the last cup, it was better to consider—what would Fluoxetine do?
Lin Yu had only met Fluoxetine once...
But from that brief encounter, he'd caught glimpses of her distinctive traits.
A deranged, remorseless killer girl devoid of morality.
An extremely arrogant and neurotic powerhouse who knew her own beauty.
Someone who seemed to love rock music, understood religion, and likely harbored some bizarre faith.
Add to that her Psychological Society identity and how the others at the table reacted to her...
Fluoxetine's image had grown increasingly vivid in Lin Yu's mind.
Like a background extra evolving into a fully fleshed-out main character.
Portraying her...
Naturally became more effortless.
A mere "punishment" of cutting a rope would never make her scramble desperately for a cup.
In fact, in this situation...
Lin Yu rested his chin on interlaced fingers, eyes curving into a smile.
"Just moments ago we were talking about cooperation, yet now you're straining so hard for a single cup..."
"The game has barely begun—is it really worth showing all your cards already?"
He chuckled, his words laced with composed mockery.
"Clink—"
The cup fell onto the tablecloth-covered surface without shattering.
Lin Yu gently nudged the suspended table, causing it to tilt slightly.
Then...
The cup rolled steadily toward him until his elegant index finger stopped its motion.
With a light flick, the cup spun once before being caught perfectly between his index and middle fingers.
Lin Yu lifted the cup smoothly.
Though he didn't understand why Robin hadn't made a move...
The autistic girl remaining seated had been a huge help!
Yet Lin Yu still felt curious and suspicious.
Robin...
Based on his observations, should be incredibly strong.
Though she'd acted timid when talking to Radish, she'd instantly recognized the Beretta M9 in Lin Yu's hand was counterfeit.
She'd been absolutely certain it wasn't a real gun.
After an Assassin's "Promotion," they gain two First-Tier items: a "List" and a second "Murder Weapon."
The "List" lets the Assassin choose at least three targets—players or NPCs—to kill for temporary item rewards.
The second "Murder Weapon" differs from the first—it's not randomly generated.
Instead, it transforms a real-life murder weapon into an in-game item.
Initially Lin Yu thought the Beretta M9 was the second murder weapon...
And no one else had doubted this.
Only Robin sensed something amiss.
This meant...
She likely knew exactly what items Fluoxetine possessed and how she'd use them.
The Night Watchmen leaned toward righteousness, so she'd probably faced Fluoxetine head-on and survived unscathed.
In other words, her combat ability might rival Fluoxetine's.
Fish's reaction earlier confirmed this.
Even after Lin Yu had aimed his gun at Robin, Fish had still pointed her own weapon at Robin too.
And Robin...
This girl who grew flustered talking to Radish showed no fear when two guns were pointed at her, even knowing Fluoxetine's was fake.
So...
Robin's current inaction was undoubtedly abnormal.
But fortunately, Lin Yu was currently playing Fluoxetine.
The greatest advantage of portraying a psychopath was...
Not needing to worry about being "reasonable."
Thus, Lin Yu asked bluntly:
"Hey, thanks for letting me have it."
"But... what's your plan? Start by cutting a rope, or play your trump card right away?"
Lin Yu asked with a smile.
Robin pursed her lips and lowered her head.
"No, it's not really a trump card..."
"I just thought, rather than fighting for a cup, it'd be better to..."
Robin mumbled as paper and pencil appeared in her hands.
The paper was a smudged sketchpad, the pencil a scraped wooden drawing pencil.
She quickly sketched an identical glass cup.
Then she shook the paper—
The cup fell right out of the drawing and into her hand.
Robin looked sheepishly at the octopus Ka.
"Um... Head Chef, would it be alright if I brought my own cup since there aren't enough?"
Ka observed Robin's method with amazement.
It nodded professionally.
"Of course—the shortage reflects my failure as banquet organizer. We couldn't possibly refuse when you're so eager to enjoy fine wine and even prepared a matching cup."
Ka chuckled, then produced a bottle that looked and smelled like white wine.
A tentacle twisted into the cork like a drill, popping it open with a "plop."
As everyone tensed, watching for tricks during the pouring...
Ka honestly extended its tentacles, rotating to fill each cup one-third full.
"Please enjoy—Mourning Wine from Kirishima Vineyard."
"Vintage... the peak of Forgotten Mist in New Calendar Year 335!"
"Drink up for the optimal 'wine experience,' and please maintain decorum afterward—no crying, swearing, or breaking tableware during potential 'loss of control!'"
Ka reminded kindly.

chapters.title: Chapter 139: Phantom of the Past, Punishment for Rudeness
chapters.content:
Only the most hopeless fool wouldn't understand the hidden meaning behind the octopus "Ka's" words.
This aperitif...
Definitely had major problems.
After drinking it, one would most likely exhibit behaviors like "weeping, cursing, and damaging tableware."
Clearly, no fools were present at the table.
This was both an explanation of the rules and a well-intentioned reminder.
"Snatching glasses" wasn't the only challenge during the aperitif segment—this dungeon was far from being just a simple 'Competition' between players.
Lin Yu stared at the wine in his glass, feeling a headache coming on.
But as 'Fluoxetine'...
Lin Yu had no choice but to put on an air of confidence and keen interest."How fascinating!"
He chuckled lightly, being the first to raise his goblet and drain it in one gulp.
The wine from a "deity's" banquet—one named after the god of "fine wine" no less—was truly extraordinary.
Cool, slightly sweet, with the aroma of fermented grapes gliding across his taste buds, its deliciousness surpassed any beverage Lin Yu had ever tasted.
And yet...
This wine contained something beyond human "taste"—an experience that literally struck straight at Lin Yu's soul.
Just as Ka had introduced it as "Mourning Wine"...
The component in the crisp wine that went beyond "flavor" was "emotion."
An emotion called "grief."
These emotions violently swallowed Lin Yu whole, then conjured up the most "mournful" images from the depths of his heart.
That was...
A great fire and explosion.
Roaring flames, buildings on the verge of collapse.
People wailing in grief knelt on the ground, their cries carried by billowing smoke that pierced the sky like an accusation against the gods.
In his daze, Lin Yu saw this long-buried memory.
In the previous dungeon, to deceive the monster called 'Chate', he had fabricated a tragic past and identity—a boy whose loved ones perished in an explosion and fire during his childhood.
But this wasn't entirely a lie.
Though Lin Yu's father wasn't a miner and didn't die in an explosion...
Long ago, Lin Yu did indeed lose a loved one in a fire.
He silently watched the flames, their flickering light reflected in his eyes.
This was probably the most "grievous" event he had experienced in his life.Follow current ɴᴏᴠᴇʟs on
"No wonder that octopus said what it did..."
Lin Yu murmured to himself.
Drinking this wine seemed to forcibly make people relive their most sorrowful scenes and memories.
Even knowing they were just phantoms of the past, maintaining complete emotional control... was incredibly difficult, wasn't it?
"Bang!"
"Damn it, this accursed wine!"
Lin Yu faintly heard a curse—seemingly from 'Fish'.
And she seemed to have punched the table for good measure.
There were also faint "sobbing" sounds... someone had clearly failed to hold back their tears.
"Some people really fell for it, huh."
Lin Yu mused.
Though everyone present was highly skilled...
Being emotionally affected by painful memories wasn't really related to skill level.
Like right now...
Lin Yu still had plenty of capacity to observe others.
That explosion and fire that took his loved one did make his heart palpitate slightly when recalled.
But...
Mastering one's emotions was an actor's most fundamental skill.
Seeing this scene recreated, Lin Yu could still clearly remember his feelings from back then.
There was both "shock" and "grief," but the predominant thought...
Was precisely why Lin Yu still remembered those feelings so clearly.
"I need to remember these 'intense emotions'—they might be useful for acting."
In fact, after calming down, Lin Yu even began observing the grief-stricken expressions of others who had also lost loved ones.
This was exactly why the memory's imagery remained so vivid.
People collapsing to the ground, wailing loudly, trying to rush into the fire, trembling uncontrollably...
Thus, Lin Yu didn't need to put up any resistance against this sorrow from his past.
Even if he had been emotional at the time, after repeatedly and calmly dissecting and analyzing his state of mind, he had nearly grown accustomed to it.
So Lin Yu simply watched everything unfold with perfect calm, as if granted a rare opportunity to review and carefully observe this memory once more.
It had to be said—after professionally studying acting theory and performing on stage for two years, revisiting these rare life experiences as material did indeed bring deeper understanding.
"My acting skills actually improved a bit from this."
Lin Yu reflected inwardly.
Then, the memories before his eyes dissipated, and Lin Yu felt his vision clear again.
Though his alcohol tolerance wasn't bad, he didn't feel the slightest effect from drinking now, as if he'd never touched the wine.
"Truly miraculous!"
He marveled, then looked around.
Fish appeared to be in terrible shape—the young girl's face was dark, her killing intent almost tangible.
Next was Radish;
the simple old farmer had seen something that left him choking back tears, completely unable to control himself.
The others were doing slightly better, though their eyes were reddened, expressions tinged with sorrow.
Phantom was pinching himself hard.
Li Hua gazed up at the distant sky.
Mosin-Nagant took out a pocket watch from his coat, seemingly looking at a photo.
Robin changed her sitting position—hugging her knees with her head buried between them.
The atmosphere at the table was intensely oppressive.
Only Lin Yu's expression remained perfectly normal.
In fact, Lin Yu couldn't help but ponder:
"Should I pretend to be sad too?"
"I'm playing Fluoxetine—how would she act in this situation..."
As he thought this, Lin Yu belatedly realized something and sighed slightly.
If 'Fluoxetine' were here, she would probably also be dazed and sad for a while.
An uncomfortable truth presented itself to Lin Yu:
"Perhaps in this aspect, I'm even more abnormal than that universally acknowledged lunatic Fluoxetine."
Realizing this, Lin Yu shook his head.
Then reluctantly forced out a somewhat sorrowful expression.
Fortunately, his acting skills were superb and his expressions changed swiftly—even without an ounce of real grief, he could flawlessly display the perfect amount of melancholy befitting Fluoxetine's identity.
The octopus "Ka" spoke with a smile:
"It seems everyone thoroughly enjoyed the delicious 'mourning' brought by the aperitif..."
"Mourning is the most important emotion—the foundation of revelry. It's precisely because people seek reconciliation with grief that they often choose banquets and celebrations, using 'rituals' and 'remembrance' to soothe their pain."
"However... though you all indulged freely, some inevitably committed acts of rudeness. But the host's rules cannot be altered!"
As Ka spoke, it produced two waterproof-wrapped red buttons from the pool.
"Snap!"
After slamming the buttons down hard with two tentacles, a faint sound came from the air.
"Snap!"
The ropes on Fish and Radish's chairs abruptly snapped.

chapters.title: Chapter 140: Choosing the Appetizer—Snail and Foie Gras
chapters.content:
With the snapping of two ropes.
The chairs of Fish and Radish shook even more violently than before.
Both broken ropes were the front left ropes of their chairs.
Among them, Fish was not affected much.
Radish, however, nervously shifted backward and to the right, adjusting his center of gravity.
But it wasn’t particularly troublesome.
After all, the other three ropes were still intact.
If one more rope snapped, it might be a different story.
“Four ropes… in other words, four chances?”
“According to Western dining order, after the aperitif comes the appetizer, then soup, side dishes, main course, dessert, and after-meal drinks. There might be a salad after the main course, or there might not… so roughly seven or eight stages.”Lin Yu pondered silently.
“No, maybe later on, there will be punishments where multiple ropes break at once, so we shouldn’t be too optimistic.”
“Also, if balance isn’t good, breaking two or three ropes could already be very risky for falling.”
But no matter what…
The “first stage” should be over.
Except for Fish and Radish, no one else was punished.
Of course…
Though no one was punished, it was obvious that except for Lin Yu, everyone’s mood was rather grim.
The octopus “Ka” was indifferent to all this.
The octopus spoke to itself.
“Anyway… after enjoying a delightful and delicious aperitif, I will prepare the appetizer for everyone!”
Ka said, and mechanical noises sounded from the circle of tables around the pool.Thɪs ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
Immediately, the tables opened and a ring of iron griddles rose up.
Ka took out a spatula and a set of paper and pen from the water, then began to ask the group: “For the appetizer, we have seared foie gras with blueberry sauce on an iron plate, and cheese-sautéed snails with chopped parsley… Dear guests, which would you like to choose?”
When Ka said this, the seven players all understood a little.
“I’m afraid this choice will determine the next trial.”
With that thought, Li Hua politely asked, “Respected head chef, may we know the difference between these two dishes? Could you please introduce them to us?”
“Of course,” Ka bowed his head slightly as if paying respect, “That is my duty.”
“The seared foie gras with blueberry sauce on the iron plate has a rich, mellow taste with a sweet and sour flavor. It is an excellent appetizer, made from the meat of the well-trained, fast, and strong Giant Wild Goose from the Wasteland. Its liver is relatively firm and the portion is quite generous.”
“The cheese-sautéed snails with parsley have a rich milky flavor and are saltier, which can also stimulate appetite. They use the highly poisonous patterned snails from the Night Valley. Their movement speed is just like typical snails, but their shells are extremely hard and they can spray poisonous mist—however, don’t worry, during cooking they undergo a detoxification process that greatly reduces their toxicity, and their shells won’t appear on the dining table.”
“The tasting time for the appetizer is limited—I hope you finish eating quickly!”
After Ka finished the introduction, Li Hua nodded thoughtfully.
“I see… one has a larger portion, and the other has some toxicity.”
“The foie gras probably requires longer eating time, and the snails might cause toxic reactions after eating.”
Radish thought for a moment and was the first to speak: “Then I choose the snails.”
Li Hua adjusted his glasses and was the second to choose: “I also choose the snails.”
He had already exhausted three uses of his abilities, and although the cooldown was short, it had not yet fully refreshed.
So Li Hua made his choice based on the known information.
Obviously, the two were somewhat confident in detoxification.
“Then I’ll choose the foie gras.”
Fish crossed her arms and crossed one leg over the other as she spoke.
From her demeanor, it was clear she was deliberately opposing Li Hua.
“I also choose the foie gras.”
Mosin-Nagant said after him, explaining: “I used to be a hunter, often eating wild game… I have good teeth and eat quickly.”
He grinned, showing a set of neat, strong teeth.
Robin thought for a moment and gave her answer: “I choose the snails.”
Phantom stroked his chin: “Is that so? Then I’ll choose the foie gras—I hate the feeling of stomach upset.”
Lin Yu, who had deliberately remained silent until the end, looked at Ka and asked sincerely: “Um, can we change our choice after selecting?”
“Certainly not,” Ka raised the paper and pen in his hand, “I have already recorded each person’s choice.”
Lin Yu nodded and smiled: “Well, I have a bigger appetite… can I have two portions?”
Ka was momentarily stunned.
Then it nodded: “Of course!”
Li Hua looked at Lin Yu in surprise.
Although they were enemies in reality, he couldn’t help but ask.
“Why are you doing that?”
Lin Yu propped his chin on his hand, giving a mischievous smile.
“Oh, silly… do you think that choosing the ‘dish’ means choosing the direction of the trial?”
“If not?”
Li Hua furrowed his brows slightly and asked back.
The others also showed curious expressions looking at Lin Yu.
Leaning back, Lin Yu said: “If it was just because of the ‘ingredients,’ would it be necessary to explain the habits of these two animals?”
Li Hua’s expression turned serious.
“You mean…”
“The aperitif test had ‘two parts.’ I don’t think the appetizer only has one test,” Lin Yu said as he looked at the octopus Ka. “Besides… the ingredients should be prepared in seven portions.”
“I saw earlier… several of the bags it brought down had moving creatures inside.”
Fish had already realized.
“Damn, I get what you mean now!”
“You mean, in this stage, each of us will have to deal with two animals—but we will choose to have one cooked into a dish?”
Ka heard Fish’s words and swung two huge burlap sacks out of the pool.
“That’s exactly right—”
The octopus declared loudly as the two sacks were opened.
Inside were seven cages and seven transparent boxes.
The cages held giant geese over a person tall, with fierce horns and sharp teeth, while the boxes contained fist-sized snails with shells shining metallically.
“To ensure every guest has a choice, I prepared seven portions of each ingredient!”
“And to adhere to the principle of no waste… I will give you the ‘ingredients’ you do not choose as a gift!”
“But please, take care of harmless disposal of the remaining ingredients yourselves!”
As Ka spoke, he casually killed four snails and four giant geese with the spatula.
The octopus’s actions were extremely casual. Whether the geese or the snails, he simply opened the cage doors and lids, lightly tapped their heads and shells once, and immediately the animals lost activity and collapsed limply!

chapters.title: Chapter 141: Loopholes in the Rules
chapters.content:
Although Ka’s process of slaughtering the snails and the geese looked casual and effortless...
But knowing that one of them was about to be faced next, none of the players present dared to underestimate those geese and snails!
Ka’s actions, on the contrary, precisely proved how powerful this octopus was.
After killing eight animals, Ka’s eight tentacles simultaneously began to prepare the meals.
He cut open the goose’s abdomen to take out the liver, scooped the snail meat out of the shell...
Then, he took out various seasonings from the water and started frying that thick liver as big as a basketball and the fist-sized snail on the iron plate.
Li Hua’s analysis was indeed correct: goose liver was substantial in weight, and the snail meat retained a bit of poison.
However, that was just an added challenge for this test.
The real difficulty...
Was the remaining one that was still alive!While Ka was frying the goose liver and snail...
A tall transparent partition suddenly descended from above, landing on both sides of each person's body and extending to the center of the table.
The partition evenly divided the round table into seven zones.
And the purpose of this...
Was, of course, to prevent the animals in front of each person from running into other zones.
Each zone was assigned a box containing a snail and a cage holding a goose.
The boxes and cages in front of Lin Yu were empty.
His snail and goose were already being prepared.
So, he leisurely looked at the boxes and cages in front of the others.
Sure enough...
After Ka started cooking, the other living animal was released!
Fish, Phantom, and Mosin-Nagant had chosen the goose liver, so they had to face the pitch-black, night-valley poisonous snail.
Li Hua, Radish, and Robin had chosen the snail, so they had to face the wild giant goose.
The wild giant goose was very fast.
Almost the instant the cage door opened, it charged out, rushing toward the player in front of it.
What surprised Lin Yu was...
The first to deal with this trouble was Radish, the ‘Farmer’!
This simple-looking middle-aged man who resembled a countryside farmer didn’t hesitate at all and directly pulled out a yellow talisman paper from his pocket and tore it open.
Then, a fierce bolt of lightning, as thick as a forearm, blasted out, directly halting the charging, ferocious goose and scorching its entire body black!
Lin Yu could even smell a strong roasted aroma through the partition.
Radish breathed a sigh of relief, his face showing a slight pained expression.
“Phew...”
Lin Yu touched his chin, roughly understanding the situation.
“Knowing his front-line combat ability was weak, he used some precious consumable item, huh?”
“Like some kind of lightning talisman... probably very expensive, and he likely doesn’t have many of those on him... or maybe it’s priceless, a gift from someone.”
Although Radish dealt with it quickly, Lin Yu knew he was actually the most dangerous.
Because it was precisely Radish’s confidence in not handling the goose that made him not hesitate to use a trump card-level attack.
The ‘Farmer’ class ability allowed him to receive a “food” supply once a day, randomly obtaining some kind of food, and if plants were involved, he could consume them to reset a skill cooldown.
This was indeed a logistics support role with relatively weak front-line combat power, making it more advantageous in ‘Survival’ dungeon types.
The player ‘Radish’ was also famously weak in combat. As one of the founders of the Player Mutual Aid Association, he had a good reputation on the forum and was known as a rare “nice guy” among the player community.
Moreover, Radish always acted alongside his subordinates and various allies when participating in dungeons.
For some unknown reason, this time he chose to participate in the dungeon alone.
But because of this...
Lin Yu was even more wary of underestimating these renowned experts!
Even these well-known players who were not good at direct combat could pull out a lightning talisman that could char a goose as tall as a person to a crisp when cornered!
If you didn’t guard against being hit by that lightning...
You would definitely be dead meat!
“These veteran players’ foundations really are not to be underestimated!”
At this moment, Li Hua and Robin also started to entangle with the wild giant goose in front of them.
Li Hua pulled out a twenty-sided die from his pocket, constantly rolling it and tossing it onto the table.
Each time Li Hua rolled the die, some low-probability event would occur, severely hindering the goose’s advance.
For example, it would slip suddenly and fall flat on the table.
Or its left foot would trip over the right foot, causing another fall.
